title: Pediatric ABA Clinic Director & Investing Partner (BCBA license required)
description:
State of Location:

Virginia

Position Summary:

As a Clinic Director and Investing Partner at Ivy, you'll oversee all clinic operations, support clinical and non-clinical team members, and care for patients through individualized treatment plans, while building equity in your clinic and providing exceptional patient care to your community. You'll play a central role in building trust with local medical professionals, guiding community outreach, and helping your clinic run smoothly. You'll open and grow a brand-new practice with Ivy’s established business systems, and direct guidance from experienced clinic leaders. Ivy's rewarding work environment allows collaboration and mentorship while maintaining autonomy and growth that is specific to each of our teammates' passions and expertise.

Join Ivy Health’s dedicated team where you're not just an employee, but a valued teammate! Together, we provide world-class care in physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and applied behavior analysis (ABA) services. Our culture promotes authenticity, inclusion, growth, community, and a passion for exceptional care for every patient.

Job Description:

Pediatric ABA Clinic Director & Investing Partner (BCBA license required)

Build something of your own without having to build it alone.

As a Clinic Director and Investing Partner, you’ll help shape a new clinic from the ground up—from the community and location to the team, culture, and patient experience. You’ll bring the clinical vision and local relationships. Ivy Health will bring the infrastructure, expertise, and support needed to turn that vision into a sustainable clinic.

Location:

Newport News, VA - Please note: this clinic does not exist yet and would be considered a start-up clinic.

How Ivy supports the build

  • Salary and benefits during the approved pre-opening period.

  • De novo business and leadership training.

  • Site selection, lease, design, and build-out support.

  • Recruiting and onboarding support for the clinic team.

  • Marketing, referral development, and community-launch support.

  • Operational, financial, technology, payer, and revenue-cycle infrastructure.

  • Coaching from leaders and partners who’ve opened clinics before.

What you’ll lead

  • Deliver care within your licensed discipline and set the clinical standard for the clinic.

  • Help choose the market, location, service mix, and patient experience.

  • Recruit, develop, and lead the clinic team.

  • Build relationships with referral partners and the community.

  • Use business and clinical information to guide responsible growth.

  • Partner with Ivy Health teams across real estate, operations, recruiting, marketing, finance, revenue cycle, IT, HR, Legal, Compliance, and payer contracting.

Why Should I Partner with Ivy Health?

  • Healthcare is changing quickly. We’re continuing to invest in the people, clinical expertise, and support that make excellent care possible.

  • Across Ivy Rehab Physical Therapy, Ivy Pediatric Therapy, and our trusted local partner brands, orthopedic and pediatric teammates are connected by one shared purpose: helping patients and families make meaningful progress.

  • Exceptional Workplace: A prestigious honor to be recognized by Gallup as an Exceptional Workplace, recognizing the most engaged workplace cultures in the world.

  • Innovative Resources & Mentorship: Access to abundant resources, robust mentorship, and career advice for unparalleled success.

  • With the utilization of ScribeIQ (an AI documentation tool), clinicians can expect a significant reduction in their normal documentation time, allowing them to spend more quality time with patients and keeping their notes AT work

  • Exceeding Expectations: Deliver best-in-class care and witness exceptional patient outcomes.

  • Incentives Galore: Benefits start within 30 days, including medical, dental, vision, and pet insurance; paid parental leave; short- and long-term disability; Employee Assistance Program (EAP) + discount program; complimentary therapy services; 401(k) with company match; up to 20 PTO days, 6 holidays, 2 CEU days, and CEU reimbursement annually.

  • Exceptional Partnerships: Collaborate with leaders like Hospital for Special Surgery (HSS) and educational partners for continuous learning.

  • Empowering Values: Live by values that prioritize teamwork, growth, and serving others.

Position Qualifications:

  • Graduate from an accredited an Applied Behavior Analysis program

  • Current or pending BCBA license or certification required as there is a treating element to this role.

  • Pediatric experience strongly preferred

If you are interested in learning more about our partnership model or want to sign up for one of our informational webinars click here or simply apply to this job ad so you can connect with our talent team: Open Your Own Clinic - Ivy Rehab

Benefits & Compensation Information:

  • Full Benefits in Your First 30 Days:

    • Medical, dental, vision insurance

    • 401k with company matching contribution

    • Disability & life insurance

    • Pet insurance discounts for your fur babies

    • Paid parental leave and maternity leave

    • Gym and wellness discounts

    • Free mental health + financial services

    • Annual CEU allowance + paid CEU days annually

    • Generous PTO Program & 6 paid holidays annually

Compensation Range: $86,109.00 – $129,163.00 per year. This position is also eligible for: bonus / equity / student loan repayment / relocation assistance.

Any listed salary range or contractual rate does not include bonuses/incentive, differential pay, or other forms of compensation or benefits.

About the role

Principal, Software Engineering – InsurTech Claims & Billing Core Systems

About the role

We are looking for a Principal Engineer to provide hands-on technical leadership across Intact’s InsurTech Claims and Billing Core Systems.

This is a senior individual contributor role with broad technical influence. You will remain hands-on through prototyping, targeted code reviews, and technical troubleshooting when needed, while helping shape architecture, technology strategy, and engineering practices across the organization.

You will help solve complex engineering challenges, advance technology strategy, and raise the technical capabilities of the teams around you through expertise, collaboration, and influence.

What you’ll do here

  • Provide hands-on technical leadership through prototyping, targeted code reviews, and technical troubleshooting when needed to address difficult, complex challenges.
  • Lead the resolution of high-severity issues involving performance, reliability, security, cloud costs, and complex integrations across claims and billing systems.
  • Define architecture, technical standards, and technology roadmaps for Claims and Billing Core Systems.
  • Design scalable, resilient, secure, and cost-effective solutions in collaboration with architects and engineering teams.
  • Implement practical AI and agentic AI solutions, including frameworks and guardrails that improve engineering productivity.
  • Research emerging technologies and lead proof-of-concepts that support innovation and business outcomes.
  • Communicate technical decisions clearly, build alignment through influence, and mentor senior engineers and technical leaders.

What you bring to the table

  • Senior or Principal-level experience in software engineering, architecture, or a related technical discipline.
  • Strong hands-on engineering experience, including prototyping, targeted code reviews, technical troubleshooting, and resolving complex production issues.
  • Proven expertise in system design, architecture, cloud platforms, APIs, microservices, distributed systems, security, and observability.
  • Practical experience implementing AI or agentic AI solutions in products, platforms, or engineering processes.
  • Expert hands-on experience with Java and Node.js is a strong asset.
  • Experience with Guidewire ClaimCenter and BillingCenter is an asset.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical trade-offs clearly to executive stakeholders.
  • A collaborative, low-ego, and people-first approach, with the ability to mentor others and lead through influence rather than formal authority.
  • A bachelor’s degree in computer science or computer engineering; a master’s degree or higher is an asset.
  • No Canadian work experience is required; however, candidates must be eligible to work in Canada.

title: AI Customer Engineer, Digital Natives, Google Cloud
description:
The Google Cloud Platform team helps customers transform and build what's next for their business — all with technology built in the cloud. Our products are developed for security, reliability and scalability, running the full stack from infrastructure to applications to devices and hardware. Our teams are dedicated to helping our customers — developers, small and large businesses, educational institutions and government agencies — see the benefits of our technology come to life. As part of an entrepreneurial team in this rapidly growing business, you will play a key role in understanding the needs of our customers and help shape the future of businesses of all sizes use technology to connect with customers, employees and partners.

As a AI Customer Engineer (CE), you will partner with technical sales teams to differentiate Google Cloud to customers. You will serve as a technical expert responsible for accelerating technical wins and adoption of complex, specialized workloads. You will leverage your deep expertise in strategic product areas in partnership with platform CEs, writing code, developing prototypes, proofs-of-concept, and demos to promote new specialized solutions to customers. You will solve AI-centered customer issues and provide a critical feedback loop to influence product development.

It's an exciting time to join Google Cloud’s Go-To-Market team, leading the AI revolution for businesses worldwide. You’ll be leveraging Google's brand credibility—a legacy built on inventing foundational technologies and proven at scale. We’ll provide you with the world's most advanced AI portfolio, including frontier Gemini models, and the complete Vertex AI platform, helping you to solve business problems. We’re a collaborative culture providing direct access to DeepMind's engineering and research minds, empowering you to solve customer challenges. Join us to be the catalyst for our mission, drive customer success, and define the new cloud era—the market is yours.

  • Drive the technical solution for complex workloads within AI product areas to ensure rapid and successful adoption, primarily supporting the business cycle from technical evaluation through customer ramp.
  • Combine business strategies and direct development and prototyping to provide functional, customer-tailored solutions that secure buy-in from customer domain experts.
  • Provide deep technical consultation to customers, acting as a technical advisor and building lasting customer relationships. Leverage learnings from customer engagements to contribute to reusable solutions and assets with the Go-To-Market team.
  • Work within product and engineering management systems to document, prioritize, and drive resolution of customer feature requests and issues.
  • Travel to customer sites, conferences, and other related events as required, acting as a public advocate for Google Cloud.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in a technical field or equivalent practical experience.
  • 6 years of experience with cloud native architecture in a customer-facing role.
  • Experience in architecting solutions that integrate AI models using agents with enterprise data sources using patterns like RAG, Text-to-SQL, and semantic search.
  • Experience with coding in Python, JavaScript or TypeScript, Go, or Java, to demo, prototype, or workshop integration patterns with customers.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience in developing agents using frameworks such as LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, or the Google AI Agent Development Kit (ADK).
  • Experience with cloud technologies including SaaS applications, iPaaS, business automation solutions, cloud infrastructure, agentic AI, and cloud networking.
  • Experience engaging with, or presenting to, technical stakeholders or executive leaders.
  • Knowledge of integration patterns using OpenAPI and Model Context Protocol (MCP) to connect AI agents with business systems and Application Programming Interface (API) gateways.
  • Knowledge of observability constructs including distributed tracing, logging, and audit logging for AI applications.

title: High Speed Systems Engineer
description:
Looking for an opportunity to make an impact?

At Leidos, we deliver innovative solutions through the efforts of our diverse and talented people who are dedicated to our customers’ success. We empower our teams, contribute to our communities, and operate sustainably. Everything we do is built on a commitment to do the right thing for our customers, our people, and our community. Our Mission, Vision, and Values guide the way we do business.

Your greatest work is ahead!

Leidos’ Defense Systems Advanced Development Organization is seeking an entry‑level to early‑career Systems Engineer specializing in Value‑Driven Design (VDD), Model‑Based Systems Engineering (MBSE), and parametric lifecycle modeling to support a classified, high‑speed system portfolio. The successful candidate will apply digital engineering frameworks to capture stakeholder requirements and translate mission‑critical engineering parameters into structured architecture baselines that feed decision‑quality trade studies.

Our team is a small advanced development group focused on hypersonic mission engineering, representing military utility, modeling lifecycle impacts of design decisions, and facilitating complex conceptual, system, and detailed design choices. Work is performed onsite in Huntsville, AL within a secure environment.

Day‑to‑day activities include hands‑on MBSE modeling, requirements drafting, and trade study support, collaborative work inside a SCIF with cross‑functional engineering teams, and operating in a fast‑paced digital engineering environment with frequent technical writing, modeling, and analysis tasks. Occasional travel will be required for in‑person engagements with internal customers and suppliers across multiple Leidos sites.

If this sounds like the kind of environment where you can thrive, keep reading!

Leidos Defense Systems Sector provides a diverse portfolio of systems, solutions, and services covering land, sea, air, space, and cyberspace for customers worldwide. Solutions for Defense include enterprise and mission IT, large-scale intelligence systems, command and control, geospatial and data analytics, cybersecurity, logistics, training, and intelligence analysis and operations support. Our team is solving the world’s toughest security challenges for customers with “can’t fail” missions. To explore and learn more, click here!

Are you ready to make an impact? Share your resume with us today!

Primary Responsibilities. Using Bullet Format—

  • Draft and maintain EARS‑formatted requirement statements and attributes; produce requirement‑to‑verification traceability and test artifacts (procedures, reports).

  • Create and maintain SysML MBSE artifacts including Logical, Physical, and Allocative architecture views; document allocations of performance, cost, reliability, and verification to physical elements.

  • Build and maintain parametric manufacturing and O&S models (Excel/Python/MATLAB) to quantify lifecycle impacts of design alternatives and support sensitivity analysis.

  • Produce trade studies, decision briefs, and internal white papers that quantify warfighter utility and lifecycle cost/benefit.

  • Support integration, verification planning, and mapping of verification activities to requirements; participate in test planning and reporting.

  • Operate effectively in a matrixed environment; transition between programs as required.

  • Work full time onsite in a controlled area; comply with SCIF and program security procedures; travel approximately one week per quarter.

Basic Qualifications.

  • BS or Masters in Systems, Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, Computer Engineering, Physics, or related STEM discipline from an ABET‑accredited institution (or equivalent). Dual majors and aerospace backgrounds encouraged.

  • Entry level to early career. Candidates with 0–8 years are appropriate; hiring band flexible for recent graduates with strong artifacts.

  • U.S. citizen eligible for Top‑Secret clearance; willing to accept TS sponsorship at hire. (Position requires ability to obtain and maintain required clearance.)

  • Familiarity with SysML concepts and MBSE principles; basic scripting or modeling in Python or MATLAB; demonstrated technical writing ability.

  • Able to perform in a collaborative, multidisciplinary engineering environment and communicate effectively.

  • Travel: 10-20% travel

Preferred Qualifications.

  • Coursework or project experience in high‑speed dynamics, aerothermodynamics, propulsion, instrumentation, or related aerospace topics.

  • Exposure to Cameo/MagicDraw, DOORS, SIMIO, or other MBSE and requirements tools.

title: Contractor Special Security Officer
description:
Job Description

The Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) has an outstanding opportunity for a Contractor Special Security Officer (CSSO) to join the Security Department.

About this Opportunity:

Reporting to the Director of Security, the Contractor Special Security Officer (CSSO) provides strategic leadership and executive oversight of the University of Washington Applied Physics Laboratory’s Compartmented Security Program. The CSSO ensures security enables cutting-edge classified research and advanced technology development in support of national security priorities while protecting national security information and maintaining compliance with Intelligence Community, Department of Defense, Cognizant Security Agency, and University requirements. As the senior authority for compartmented security, the CSSO integrates SCI security, personnel security, physical security, classified information protection, Information Assurance, and regulatory compliance into a unified, mission-focused security program that supports the Laboratory’s research enterprise.

This position requires exceptional leadership, strategic vision, and independent judgment in a highly regulated environment where decisions directly affect the University’s ability to conduct classified research and maintain sponsor confidence. The CSSO interprets and applies complex IC, DoD, CSA, and University requirements across multiple integrated security disciplines, routinely resolving issues that demand balancing regulatory compliance, operational priorities, organizational risk, resource constraints, and mission objectives. The role establishes program strategy, develops policy, directs operations, manages organizational risk, and provides executive-level guidance on matters affecting classified research.

As the University’s principal advisor for compartmented security, the CSSO builds collaborative partnerships with Laboratory leadership, Principal Investigators, Program Managers, researchers, engineers, Information Technology personnel, Information Assurance professionals, government sponsors, and oversight agencies. The CSSO provides strategic leadership for the Special Security Office, directly supervises Contractor Special Security Representatives (CSSRs), and offers functional leadership to Information Assurance personnel supporting classified information systems. Success requires balancing compliance, operational effectiveness, customer service, workforce development, and continuous improvement within a dynamic and rapidly evolving research environment.

Decisions made by the CSSO influence organizational risk, sponsor confidence, regulatory compliance, workforce effectiveness, SCIF readiness, and the University’s ability to compete for and execute classified research. Errors in judgment, policy interpretation, leadership, or program execution may result in the compromise of classified information, loss of government confidence, regulatory findings, operational disruption, or adverse impacts to the University’s national security mission. The position therefore demands exceptional technical competence, integrity, discretion, and the ability to make sound decisions in complex operational environments.

Key Responsibilities:

Compartmented Security Program Leadership & Administration (30% FTE):

  • Lead the Compartmented Security Program — Provides strategic direction, executive oversight, and long-range vision for the University’s Compartmented Security Program.
  • Direct Special Security Office Operations — Manages daily operations, resources, workflows, and organizational performance of the Special Security Office.
  • Establish Security Policy — Develops, implements, and enforces security policies, procedures, and operating standards governing SCI/SAP operations.
  • Advise Executive Leadership — Provides executive‑level guidance on compartmented security, organizational risk, and regulatory compliance.
  • Align Security Strategy — Ensures security strategy supports Laboratory research priorities and University objectives.

Personnel Security, Information Assurance & Integrated Security Operations (20% FTE):

  • Oversee Personnel Security — Directs SCI eligibility, indoctrinations, debriefings, visit authorizations, and personnel access management.
  • Lead Information Assurance Integration — Provides functional leadership for IA personnel supporting classified information systems and cybersecurity coordination.
  • Coordinate Integrated Security Operations — Ensures cohesive security operations across IT, IA, and research programs to support mission readiness.

SCIF Operations, Physical Security & Information Protection (20% FTE):

  • Manage SCIF Accreditation — Directs accreditation, lifecycle management, compliance, and operational readiness of Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities.
  • Oversee Physical Security — Ensures protection of classified information, government assets, and secure facility infrastructure.
  • Approve Secure Facility Requirements — Reviews and authorizes security requirements for construction, renovation, and modification of secure spaces.

Governance, Risk Management, Compliance & Government Relations (20% FTE):

  • Lead Governance & Compliance — Directs regulatory compliance, internal controls, enterprise risk management, and program governance activities.
  • Conduct Inspections & Assessments — Executes internal inspections, self-assessments, and program evaluations to measure compliance and organizational performance.
  • Resolve Security Findings — Directs corrective actions for vulnerabilities, incidents, inspection findings, and compliance deficiencies.
  • Represent University to Government — Serves as a primary interface with government sponsors and oversight agencies for inspections, accreditation, and program reviews.

Leadership, Workforce Development & Stakeholder Engagement (10% FTE):

  • Develop Security Workforce — Recruits, mentors, evaluates, and retains a high-performing security team, including CSSRs and IA personnel. This position manages employees.
  • Promote Security as a Mission Enabler — Fosters a customer-focused culture that integrates security early in research planning and supports operational excellence.

title: Global Lead, Women's Protection and Empowerment Systems Transformation
description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

Background

The Violence Prevention and Response Unit (VPRU) is one of IRC's four Technical Units, bringing together Child Protection, Women's Protection and Empowerment, and Protection Rule of Law across over 35 countries. VPRU is increasingly strengthening connective tissue across GBV, child protection, and case management through a shared social work systems lens, in service of IRC's Safety Strategy. IRC's Technical Excellence teams offer five core services to IRC country programs: Program Design, Quality Assurance, Business Development, Research and Learning, and External Influence.

Job Overview

The WPE field is at a strategic inflection point. The humanitarian system is contracting, siloed sectoral programming by default is under scrutiny, and the organizations that will define the next decade of protection practice are those that can ground a social work systems approach in feminist practice, building connective tissue with child protection, rule of law, and case management bridge prevention and response as two expressions of a single protective logic , and take seriously the financing of services for those most at risk of violence as a structural condition of impact rather than a donor-cycle variable.

The Global Lead, Women's Protection and Empowerment Systems Transformation is hired for this moment. They are IRC's organizational leader on GBV prevention and response and women's and girls' empowerment, a core member of the VPRU senior management team, and the person responsible for transforming how IRC delivers, finances, and positions its WPE work at a critical juncture for the sector. The role carries the full authority of a senior staff member and demands intellectual independence, diagnostic acuity, and appetite for institution-building.

A deliberate attention to financing is central to the mandate: how services are resourced, how prevention and livelihoods approaches are financed as integral parts of the protection architecture, and how IRC engages donors, governments, and multilateral actors to build more durable financing models for WPE outcomes — whether or not these are delivered by humanitarian actors. IRC's WPE work spans humanitarian response, recovery, and system strengthening, and this role's financing agenda is shaped by that full arc across the humanitarian-development-peace nexus.

Major Responsibilities

Strategy, program design and business development

  • Lead the transformation of IRC's WPE practice, acting as the organizational reference point on GBV prevention and response, women's empowerment, and WPE systems strengthening, internally and externally.

  • Lead strategic direction for WPE in line with S100 and the Safety Strategy; identify global areas of programmatic risk and elevate issues to Regional Leads and VPRU leadership.

  • Lead global business development for WPE, bringing a clear distinction between financing for portfolio growth and financing for the quality, continuity, and sustainability of services. Advocate for funding architectures that cover the workforce, systems, referral infrastructure, and community relationships that make delivery possible — not only project outputs.

  • Steer the adaptation of the WPE operating model to current conditions without compromising service integrity. Revenue generation matters as a condition of sustaining the mission, not as the mission itself, and the Global Lead holds both imperatives with clear-eyed honesty.

  • Collaborate with Global Practice Leads and Regional Leads to promote programmatic synergies within WPE and across IRC sectors, with explicit attention to shared models with Child Protection and Case Management as foundational components of a social work systems approach.

  • Line manage global practice area and strategic project staff; manage in partnership other roles as applicable.

Global practice implementation support

  • Accountable for evidence-based technical oversight of WPE standards, methodologies, and tools, including cross-cutting issues such as diversity, inclusion, and climate adaptation; and for building working fluency in case management strategy and information system architecture.

  • Approach quality as a diagnostic function, not a compliance one: distinguish between failures of implementation logic, funding or capacity constraints, context shifts that have rendered approaches maladapted, and policies that have not kept pace with the communities they serve. Ask not only whether targets are being met but whether the right targets are being pursued, and act on that diagnosis in partnership with country and regional teams.

  • Support Regional Leads, Technical Advisors, and Technical Coordinators with thorny technical problems, capacity strengthening, mentorship, and career planning.

Research, data, knowledge management and learning

  • Bring intellectual credibility to debates about evidence standards: make a rigorous case for implementation learning, longitudinal qualitative evidence, cross-system data linkage, practice-based inquiry, and community-level outcome tracking as legitimate, ethical, and contextually generative forms of knowledge alongside experimental evidence. Hold both orientations without collapsing into relativism.

  • Guide research and evidence use with a genuine intelligence orientation: read across datasets — SRH, mental health, social protection, GBV — to build a coherent narrative on violence and help-seeking behavior. Be as interested in what the data cannot see as in what it shows; understand why certain populations and outcomes remain unmeasured, and treat those gaps as arguments for where the sector needs to go. Familiarity with data architectures in social welfare, public health, or financing systems adjacent to humanitarian protection is a meaningful asset.

  • Establish and maintain relevant Communities of Practice; provide technical inputs to WPE-specific MEAL tools; support data interpretation in learning routines.

External influence, representation and thought leadership

  • Exercise entrepreneurial judgment in external representation: identify where consequential conversations about women's safety, protection systems, and financing are happening before the WPE sector has found them, and position IRC there with an intellectual contribution, not primarily a funding ask. Build thought leadership presence across forums, publications, and cross-sector platforms including social work systems strengthening, care reform, social finance, and feminist movements beyond WPE's traditional scope.

  • Act as key strategic advisor to Policy and Advocacy, Research and Innovation, and External Relations on WPE-related advocacy campaigns and policy shifts.

  • Develop and maintain strategic relationships and partnerships with a wide range of actors — donors, UN agencies, INGOs, academia, social justice organizations, and financing institutions.

Team leadership and culture

  • Lead the WPE global team through transition with integrity and care: manage people whose roles may evolve, hold team morale through institutional pressure, and model the balance between honest acknowledgment of difficulty and genuine forward orientation, creating conditions in which staff can do serious, difficult work without losing sight of why it matters.

  • Hold serious work with humanity: sustain analytical rigor without clinical detachment, and support staff wellbeing without minimizing the weight of work that daily engages violence, trauma, and suffering. This is a named leadership competency for this role, not a peripheral consideration.

  • Invest in the relationship between global technical leadership and field practitioners: case workers, community mobilizers, GBV officers, clinical staff, and community-based protection networks. Understand what the global function owes these practitioners in standards, tools, accessible guidance, and professional recognition, alongside the more visible external dimensions of the role.

  • Contribute actively to VPRU unit culture, shared leadership, cross-team learning, and the collective responsibility of the senior management team for unit cohesion.

Key Working Relationships

On partnerships and collective action

Meaningful localization is a collective responsibility and organizational commitment, not a project deliverable. The Global Lead models this in how they build relationships with women-led and local organizations. Beyond this, the systems shaping outcomes for women and girls are changed through coalitions cutting across social justice movements, private sector actors, governments, and academia. The Global Lead builds bridges across these divides — connecting women's rights organizations with financing institutions, protection practitioners with public health researchers, feminist movements with social welfare system architects, and humanitarian actors with the domestic systems whose standards ultimately determine whether the structural conditions of violence change or persist. This is not relationship management. It is a theory of change.

Key internal relationships

  • VPRU Deputy Director; VPR Regional Leads across 5 regions and regional WPE Technical Advisors

  • Global Practice Leads for Child Protection, Protection Rule of Law, Sexual and Reproductive Health, Water and Sanitation, Economic Inclusion

  • Safe, Inclusive and Transformative Programming Team; VPRU Policy and Advocacy Lead; VPRU Program Development and Partnerships Lead

  • Global System Strengthening Team; Global HQ and AMU focal points

Key external relationships

The Global Lead actively expands and diversifies VPRU's external network beyond the conventional GBV coordination architecture. This includes GBV AoR and Global Protection Cluster leads; INGOs and Red Cross/Crescent counterparts; institutional and bilateral donors and policy makers; UN agency counterparts; and academic institutions working on gender, violence, and social work systems. Beyond the humanitarian sector: regional and national civil society and social justice organizations, philanthropic actors, social finance intermediaries, and feminist movements. These relationships are not supplementary to the mandate — they are part of how WPE systems transformation happens and how it is resourced.

Desired Experience and Skills

Core WPE and GBV expertise (required)

  • Established or growing recognition as an expert at regional or global level, with 12+ years of progressive experience designing, leading, and implementing programs, including 7+ years in GBV/WPE is required. Additional experience in social work, social welfare systems, or case management practice would be an asset.

  • Strong track record of driving uptake of evidence-based practice.

  • Demonstrated experience in sectoral strategy design and planning; experience with policy and advocacy efforts and campaigns for change.

Systems, financing, and cross-sectoral orientation (strongly preferred; can be further strengthened in role)

  • Demonstrated interest in social work systems, case management practice, or integrated protection service delivery models, with genuine curiosity about how GBV connects to broader systems strengthening.

  • Intellectual engagement with the financing of protection and prevention programming, including how services for survivors and prevention mechanisms are resourced, and how more durable financing models for WPE outcomes can be built.

  • Experience working across sectoral boundaries (both programmatically and with different datasets)— GBV and child protection, health, livelihoods, social protection — is a strong asset; familiarity with, and curiosity in, data and financing architectures in systems adjacent to humanitarian protection is a meaningful additional asset.

Orientation toward inflection and institution-building

  • Energized by building something as well as consolidating what works; thrives in strategic inflection moments; brings diagnostic clarity to distinguish core mandate from what can be adapted.

  • An active thought leadership presence and a demonstrated ability to hold a clear directional view in ambiguous or transitional contexts, and to bring others along, even when the structure is not fully resolved

General leadership and management

  • Ability to shape the transformative vision and agenda, complemented with excellent and an ability to identify and convert business development opportunities and the necessary communication, influencing, and storytelling skills to turn this vision into action ;

  • Demonstrated capacity to lead, grow and sustain high performing teams, including through transition

  • Demonstrated for self and staff; to influence across a wide range of diverse stakeholders; and to within the domain area.

  • Demonstrated comfort engaging non-transactionally across donors, civil society, social justice movements, financing organizations, and academic communities: building and sustaining relationships as a basis for influence and trust over time.

  • An understanding of innovation that transcends technology, behavior change and comfort with disruptive thinking

  • Fluency in English required. Arabic, French, and/or Spanish welcome. Fluency in Farsi, Urdu, Swahili, Bambara, or other languages dominant in IRC's programming footprint is celebrated as a form of professional capital: speakers of these languages bring proximity to the realities of the women and girls we serve that expands technical expertise .

  • Ability to travel globally up to 20% of the time.

Education

  • Master's/post-graduate degree in Social Work, Social Policy, Gender Studies, International Law, Human Rights Law, International Development, Public Administration, or a related field required, or an equivalent combination of education and work experience demonstrating comparable depth.

  • Candidates whose academic formation is in fields concerned with how social services are planned, governed, and financed — public administration, social policy, health systems, domestic social welfare architecture — are strongly encouraged to apply and will be weighted favorably alongside conventional humanitarian backgrounds.

  • Sound training and/or demonstrated experience in the use of data and research evidence for programmatic decisions; rigorous analytic skills are an advantage.

IRC recognizes that the most relevant expertise for this role may have been built across institutional boundaries, and that a non-linear trajectory is often a marker of exactly the kind of cross-sector fluency this role demands. Career pauses — whether for caregiving, personal reasons, independent research, or other life circumstances — are not disqualifying and will not be treated as gaps requiring justification.

Some of the strongest candidates may have spent years in adjacent sectors — social welfare, public health, education, social protection, feminist movements, or financing — carrying a deep commitment to GBV and WPE work without a formal WPE title. If you have followed this field closely, hold a genuine view on where it needs to go, and have built the cross-sector fluency to help take it there, we encourage you to apply or to reach out with questions before doing so.

Supplementary information for external comms:

Who we are looking for

This role is for someone who loves this field enough to want to see it move beyond itself, and who can hold a clear vision of the shifts it needs without losing sight of what makes it worth fighting for. Someone who has seen what survivor-centered, feminist, rights-based programming can do at its best, and who is equally clear-eyed about the ways the sector has sometimes missed opportunities, been left out of innovations that social services in other contexts have leveraged for better impact and scale, and built protection frameworks that keep women safe in the short term while leaving the structural conditions of violence entirely intact.

We are not looking for someone who mistakes disruption for progress, but for someone who leverages activist conviction for concrete change in policy and implementation. Someone who holds an uncompromising commitment to the rights of all women and girls in crisis alongside a clear-eyed understanding of the specific opportunities the WPE sector can champion in advancing those rights: not to carry the entire women's rights agenda, but to ensure that our sector's focus on safety and empowerment is ambitious, strategic, and transformative — and to bring the intellectual honesty to continuously ask whether we are adequately challenging the systems that enable violence, not only responding when it occurs.

IRC is a global organization embedded in systems of power and bureaucracy. Part of this role's mandate is to engage those systems strategically, not only position against them. We are looking for someone with the integrity to use access and influence for the people this work is meant to serve: neither naive about institutional constraints nor paralyzed by them. If you derive more satisfaction from naming power imbalances than shifting them, we thank you because this work is important, but this is not the role for you. If you know how to do both, we want to hear from you.

This is a hybrid position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.

This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in United States of America, Kenya, and United Kingdom.

title: Intern - PHY Digital Design & Automation Engineer, HBM
description:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all.

Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

About the Team

At Micron Technology, we transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all. The Heterogeneous Integration Group (HIG) HBM Architecture team develops future High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) architectures, PHY design methodologies, and automation solutions that enable next-generation AI, high-performance computing, networking, and data center applications. The team works closely with Architecture, Design Engineering, Verification, Product Engineering, and external partners to advance memory technologies while improving design quality, productivity, and development efficiency.

Position Overview

As a Senior or Graduate Engineering Intern, you will collaborate with experienced HBM architects and engineers to support the development of digital design methodologies, automation frameworks, timing analysis flows, and architecture validation solutions for next-generation HBM PHY and IO subsystems. This role offers hands-on experience in digital design, verification, automation, and timing analysis, while providing opportunities to leverage AI Assisted engineering workflows, Large Language Models (LLMs), and Generative AI tools to enhance engineering productivity and design efficiency.

Responsibilities

  • Support digital design, integration, and timing analysis activities for HBM PHY and IO subsystems, including timing constraint development and timing closure efforts.
  • Develop and implement verification solutions using Verilog/SystemVerilog and UVM-based environments, analyze simulation results, and debug functional or timing-related issues.
  • Create Python-based automation tools and AI Assisted engineering workflows that leverage Large Language Models (LLMs) and Generative AI technologies to improve engineering efficiency.
  • Collaborate with architecture, design, verification, and product engineering teams to evaluate features, validate architectures, and improve design quality metrics.
  • Document technical findings and present results through design reviews, engineering discussions, and project presentations.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing a Master's or Ph.D. degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field.
  • Demonstrated understanding of digital design concepts including finite state machines (FSMs), pipelining, clock-domain crossing (CDC), timing analysis, and computer architecture.
  • Experience with RTL design and verification concepts using Verilog or SystemVerilog.
  • Proficiency in Python, C++, or a comparable programming language, and experience working in Linux-based development environments.
  • Strong analytical, debugging, problem-solving, written communication, and verbal communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with digital implementation flows, static timing analysis (STA), timing closure methodologies, and timing constraint development.
  • Familiarity with UVM-based verification environments and regression infrastructure development.
  • Experience using EDA tools from Cadence, Synopsys, Siemens, or equivalent vendors.
  • Exposure to automation, software development, data analytics, AI Assisted workflows, Large Language Models (LLMs), or Generative AI-based productivity solutions.
  • Coursework, research, or project experience related to VLSI design, digital systems, computer architecture, memory systems, timing analysis, or mixed-signal design environments.

title: Korean Interpreter
description:
LanguageLine Solutions is Hiring!

At LanguageLine, we strive for a world in which language and cultural barriers no longer exist. Use your language skills to dramatically improve the lives of limited-English speakers, as well as the Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing. Even better, you can do this while working from your own home.

LanguageLine has been certified as a Great Place to Work, and is regularly listed as one of America’s top work-from-home employers.

Our interpreters serve clients across numerous industries, including health care, 911, first responders, education, government agencies, and all walks of business.

As an interpreter, you will receive training that is the best in the industry. We’ll ensure that you learn new skills while further developing your skillset. We provide numerous opportunities for advancement. You’ll be in a certified ASTM and ISO environment. You'll also be supported by a Senior Language Specialist, as well as our Interpreter and Technology Help Desks.

Join our team now!

Job Description

Work at Home Bilingual Korean-English Video-Phone Interpreter

Job Title: Korean Interpreter

Location: Work at Home position in United States

Position: Video-Phone Interpreter

Pay: $23 - $25 per hour.

  • Compensation will not be less than any applicable state or local minimum wage.

We Offer:

  • Paid professional interpreter training and continuous development.
  • Incentives for meeting attendance targets.
  • Benefits include: Paid Sick Leave in accordance with applicable law, Medical, Dental, Vision, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Accident, Critical Illness & Life, AD&D, Insurance Package, Inpatient Hospital, Short Term Disability, and 401K Retirement.
  • Employee Referral Program.
  • Advancement opportunities within the organization.
  • Interpreter support.
  • An inclusive and diverse work environment.

Position Overview:

The Korean Video-Telephone- Interpreter is responsible for handling calls on demand, and renders the meaning of conversations between Korean and English speakers. The interpreter breaks the communication barrier in a wide range of industries that LanguageLine Solutions serves: Healthcare, Government, Insurance, Financial, Utilities, Travel & Hospitality, General Business, Law Enforcement, Court, and 911.

The interpreter processes information quickly, concisely and recognizes sensitive cultural differences. The interpreter is professional and courteous at all times and uses appropriate terminology and understands common industry procedures and practices. The video and audio interpreting sessions may involve simple or complex, technical or non-technical subjects.

This position does not involve written translation however translators and other skilled linguists are encouraged to apply. The interpreters translate verbally.

**This is a remote position. The Interpreter works from his/her home-office. It is essential to ensure a quiet & secure environment**

Essential Job Functions:

  • Respond to video and audio interpreting sessions promptly and conduct interpretation in a friendly and professional manner.
  • Participate in online, video and audio training sessions.
  • Deliver interpretation services via video and expediently type data on a dedicated device, such as a laptop, desktop computer, mobile phone, or tablet, in order to perform the essential functions of the job.
  • Render correct concepts and meanings according to the conventions of established interpretation protocol, avoiding omissions or additions.
  • Speak clearly in both languages using proper pronunciation, enunciation and polite expressions.
  • Maintain a professional demeanor throughout the video and audio interpreting sessions at all times.
  • Remain calm during video and audio interpreting sessions in the event that one of the primary speakers is incoherent or upset, especially in emergency situations such as 911 calls.
  • Maintain punctuality and availability during scheduled work hours.
  • Follow client instructions, in compliance with protocol to ensure client expectations are met with the Limited English-speaking Person (LEP), avoiding interaction with the LEP without client’s permission.
  • Understand protocol and terminology for various industries including, but not limited to, Medical, Insurance, Finance and Law.
  • Demonstrate commitment to cultural sensitivity and working in a diverse environment.
  • **Some calls may be highly emotional and/or stressful in nature. The interpreter may need to remain on a call for extended periods without breaks due to the nature of the call or may, at times experience high call volumes. The interpreter must have the ability to provide the required, company standards of service within this dynamic environment. **

Qualifications

  • Fluency in Korean and English and skilled in the associated cultural dynamics.
  • Ability to provide cultural competency and assess regional and accent differences to find ways of communicating with the LEP.
  • Excellent listening, retention and note-taking skills to maintain a high level of accuracy during interpretation.
  • Ability to concentrate, stay detached from the conversation, remain neutral and objective at all times, and remain on calls that involve sensitive subjects such as end of life conversations, pregnancy termination, vaccinations, and matters concerning sexual orientation and/or gender expression.
  • Education or work experience in language-related fields such as teaching, language assessment, translation or interpretation preferred.
  • Must be able to adapt to any LLS technology enhancements that improve service delivery and meet client demands.
  • Must be at least 18 years of age.
  • Legally authorized to work in the United States.
  • Applicants for employment in the US must have work authorization that does not now or in the future require sponsorship of a visa for employment authorization in the United States and with LanguageLine Solutions (i.e., H1-B visa, F-1 visa (OPT), TN visa or any other non-immigrant status).
  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Candidates who are currently employed by a client of LanguageLine Solutions or an affiliated LanguageLine Solutions business may not be eligible for consideration.
  • Ability to read and write the requested languages – highly preferred.

**Based on your location, a post-offer, a pre-employment background check and/or drug screen may be required**

Technical Requirements:

  • Dedicated personal device for business purposes.
    • Desktop / Laptop Computers with any of the following Operating Systems: Windows, MacOS, or ChromeOS.
    • Tablets (iPadOS or Android) are acceptable.
    • Smartphones (iOS or Android) are also acceptable.
  • Restricted brands:
    • Kaspersky products.
    • Huawei hardware.
  • High speed Internet connection for work related electronic communication. This internet connection should provide download speeds of no less than 5 Mbps, upload speeds of 3 Mbps, Ping value of no more than 300 ms, Jitter value of no more than 30 ms.
  • Must have access to a quiet space free from background noise or distraction.

Physical Requirements:

  • Must be able to operate a keyboard and mouse and remain in a stationary position in front of a computer and webcam the majority of the workday.
  • Must use a headset for prolonged periods of time.
  • Must be able to operate company provided software and systems to perform all aspects of the job.
  • Must have sufficient manual dexterity to type or write.
  • Able to lift up to 26 lbs.
  • May be exposed to moderate noise levels; i.e. computer, audio, telephone.

Overweegt u te solliciteren op deze baan? Wacht niet langer, scroll naar beneden en solliciteer zo snel mogelijk om deze kans niet te missen.

Hoe je samen met ons vooruit gaat. Bij Actemium Logistics & Automation krijg je de kans om een directe impact te maken op de efficiëntie van onze klanten. Efficiënter werken is voor hen cruciaal, onder andere vanwege de uitdagingen zoals personeelstekorten en de noodzaak van duurzame inzetbaarheid. Dit vraagt om verdere automatisering en duurzame oplossingen.

Als softwareontwikkelaar werk je aan diverse projecten die bijdragen aan deze oplossingen en een efficiëntere inrichting van logistieke processen. Hierdoor kunnen onze klanten hun doelen behalen en waarde blijven bieden. Je ontwerpt, bouwt, test en implementeert software en denkt proactief mee over logistieke oplossingen. Tijdens de implementatie bied je ondersteuning op locatie, voornamelijk in Nederland. Je ontwikkelt maatwerksoftware binnen ons Actemium Warehousemanagement System (WMS) en integreert dit met andere systemen.

In de eerste weken volg je een 1-op-1 trainingsprogramma om onze softwareoplossingen te leren kennen. Daarna start je in je team, waar een ervaren mentor je begeleidt tijdens je eerste jaar. In het begin is die begeleiding intensief, maar naarmate je zelfstandiger werkt, bouw je dit stap voor stap af. Daarna is er via ons ontwikkelpad voor Software Engineers volop ruimte om je verder te specialiseren – in je eigen tempo en richting.

Jouw vaardigheden

Jouw kijk op vooruit gaan

  • Met jouw .NET en C# kennis bouw je moeiteloos aan stabiele en schaalbare software.
  • Je werkt graag samen met collega’s in kleine projectteams aan mooie, afwisselende projecten in de logistieke sector.
  • Je vindt het leuk om klanten met legacy systemen te helpen en ziet het als een uitdaging om deze functioneel draaiend te houden.
  • De wereld van de logistiek spreekt je aan, vooral als het gaat om het efficiënter inrichten van processen voor onze klanten.
  • Je vindt het leuk om mee te denken met klanten en hen te adviseren.
Wat wij jou bieden

Zo helpen we jou vooruit

  • Aantrekkelijke arbeidsvoorwaarden: Zoals een goed basis salaris, aangevuld met een zeer goede servicetoeslag, een aantrekkelijke winstdelingsregeling en keuze vrijheid in het opbouwen of verkopen van je ADV dagen.
  • Professionele ontwikkeling: Jaarlijks individueel trainingsbudget van € 750,- en mooie, afwisselende projecten bij zowel kleine als grote (internationale) spelers in de logistieke sector.
  • Werk-privébalans: Veel ruimte voor een goede werk- en privébalans, flexibele werktijden, de mogelijkheid tot parttime werken en 25 vakantiedagen en 13 ADV dagen op jaarbasis.
  • Hybride werken: Mogelijkheid om hybride te werken.
  • Goede werksfeer: Leuke collega’s, toekomstperspectief, een informele werksfeer, vrijheid en verantwoordelijkheid.
  • Extra voordelen: Leaseauto zodra je ook naar klanten gaat, vaste onkostenvergoeding, goede telefoonregeling en de mogelijkheid om financieel aantrekkelijk aandelen te verwerven van de VINCI groep.

Ga je mee? Wil jij samen met ons vooruitgang boeken in de wereld van industriële softwareoplossingen? Solliciteer dan direct! Ken je iemand voor wie dit écht iets is? Tip hem of haar. Je helpt ons én diegene vooruit – alvast bedankt!

Ben je recruiter? We waarderen je interesse, maar we werven deze functie graag zelf. We vragen je daarom vriendelijk om geen contact met ons op te nemen, tenzij wij jou zelf benaderen. xgiwjmb Dank je wel voor je begrip!

title: Electrical Assembler
description:
About Us:

BW Papersystems, part of the Barry-Wehmiller Group, builds capital equipment that transforms paper into products for consumers - every day, around the world. We offer innovative technologies, service and parts, and years of global experience in corrugating, finishing; slitting and packaging; stationery; bookbinding and security documents. Customers rely on our machines to produce and convert items such as corrugated boxes, folding cartons, passports, notebooks, copy paper, board, and coated and other specialty papers. For more information, visit bwpapersystems.com.


Barry-Wehmiller is a diversified global supplier of engineering consulting and manufacturing technology for the packaging, corrugating, sheeting and paper-converting industries. By blending people-centric leadership with disciplined operational strategies and purpose-driven growth, Barry-Wehmiller has become a $3 billion organization with nearly 12,000 team members united by a common belief: to use the power of business to build a better world.


Job Description:

BW Papersystems is seeking a skilled and detail-oriented Electrical Assembler to join our production team! As an Electrical Assembler, you will play a crucial role in the assembly and installation of electrical components on our company-produced equipment. Your expertise in reading wiring diagrams, interpreting specifications, and following assembly instructions will be instrumental in ensuring the quality and functionality of our products.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Read and interpret wiring diagrams, specifications, and work orders to determine materials requirements and assembly instructions.

  • Assemble electrical or electronic systems, including support structures, by installing components, units, subassemblies, wiring, and assembly casings using various methods such as rivets, bolts, or soldering equipment.

  • Label, wire, and connect switch boxes and control panel terminal boards according to wiring diagrams.

  • Inspect wiring for proper coding and termination, checking for shorts, grounds, and continuity. Report any design or print errors to the supervisor.

  • Participate in the testing of completed machines and assist in diagnosing and remedying electrical issues if required.

  • Identify and report defective materials, unusual conditions, or operating difficulties to the appropriate supervisor with accurate and detailed descriptions to facilitate proper corrective actions.

  • Complete all necessary documentation to meet quality and production requirements.

  • Actively engage in team meetings to communicate and collaboratively resolve any cost, quality, or production challenges.

  • Adhere to established safety procedures while performing all tasks.

  • Maintain a clean and orderly work area and ensure equipment is in good working condition.

Essential Duties:

  • Strong understanding of electrical components and their installation processes.

  • Familiarity with soldering equipment and basic hand tools.

  • Detail-oriented with a commitment to producing high-quality work.

  • Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to identify and communicate issues effectively.

  • Basic knowledge of testing procedures and diagnosing electrical problems is a plus.

Basic Qualifications and Requirements:

  • High School Diploma or GED Equivalent.

  • 2+ years of experience in electrical assembly or a related field.

The approximate pay range for this position is $24/HR - $34/HR. Please note that the pay range provided is a good faith estimate for the position at the time of posting. Final compensation may vary based on factors including but not limited to background, knowledge, skills, and abilities as well as geographic location of the position

We know that our differences often can bring about innovation, excellence and meaningful work—therefore, people from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply to our positions. Please let us know if you require reasonable accommodations during the interview process. ​

title: ED Technician (24hr, Day/Evening)
description:
When you join the growing BILH team, you're not just taking a job, you’re making a difference in people’s lives.

Job Summary: Fully versed in all areas of department operations, performs as a member of a team responsible for completing all tasks necessary for the smooth functioning of the department. Coordinates and expedites the flow of patients and providers. Able to manage multiple clinical responsibilities which may include EKGs, phlebotomy, splinting, wound care, crutch walking, patient activities of daily living and post-mortem care. Provides assistance and support to the physicians and nurses as needed. Assists with clerical and receptionist duties. Adheres to hospital policy regarding patient confidentiality. Exhibits a willingness and ability to communicate self as a caring and respectful person, capable of sensitively responding to patients needs.<br><br>

Job Description:

Essential Responsibilities:

  • Performs competently and safely in clinical tasks of EKGs, phlebotomy, wound care, splinting, crutch walking, patient activities of daily living and post-mortem care.

  • Performs lab testing, specimen collection, according to protocol and communicates results to the appropriate department personnel and documents in the medical record. Inclusive of Point of Care Testing.

  • Performs vital signs according to protocol and communicates results to appropriate department personnel and documents interventions in the medical record.

  • Performs visual acuity testing competently and reports results to clinical nurse and ED attending.

  • Performs oxygen saturation testing competently and reports results to clinical nurse and ED attending.


Required Qualifications:

  • BLS-AHA required or obtained within 30 days of hire

  • High School diploma or GED required.

  • 0-1 years related work experience required.

  • Experience with computer systems required, including web-based applications and some Microsoft Office applications which may include Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint or Access.


Competencies:

Written Communications: Ability to communicate clearly and effectively in written English with internal and external customers.

Oral Communications: Ability to comprehend and converse in English to communicate effectively with medical center staff, patients, families and external customers.

Knowledge: Ability to demonstrate basic knowledge of fundamental concepts, practices and procedures with the ability to use them in routine situations. Specialized knowledge not required.

Teamwork: Ability to interact respectfully with other employees, professional staff and/or external contacts to offer ideas, identify issues, obtain information or deliver services.

Customer Service: Ability to provide a high level of customer service to patients, visitors, staff and external customers in a professional, service-oriented, respectful manner using skills in active listening and problem solving. Ability to remain calm in stressful situations.

Age based Competencies: Employees in this job must be competent to provide patient care to the following age groups: Neonatal: Birth to 6 months, Youth: 6 months to 16 years, Young adult: 16-30 years, Middle Age: 30 - 60 years, Elderly: 60 -.
Physical Nature of the Job: Medium work: Exerting up to 50 pounds of force occasionally and or up to 20 pounds of force frequently. Job is physical in nature and employee needs to stand and/or move around through the majority of their shift.

Pay Range:

$19.50 - $26.24

The pay range listed for this position is the base hourly wage range the organization reasonably and in good faith expects to pay for this position at this time. Actual compensation is determined based on several factors, that may include seniority, education, training, relevant experience, relevant certifications, geography of work location, job responsibilities, or other applicable factors permissible by law. Compensation may exceed the base hourly rate depending on shift differentials, call pay, premium pay, overtime pay, and other additional pay practices, as applicable to the position and in accordance with the law.

More than 35,000 people working together. Nurses, doctors, technicians, therapists, researchers, teachers and more, making a difference in patients' lives. Your skill and compassion can make us even stronger.

title: ASIC Design Verification Manager, Google Cloud
description:
In this role, you’ll work to shape the future of AI/ML hardware acceleration. You will have an opportunity to drive cutting-edge TPU (Tensor Processing Unit) technology that powers Google's most demanding AI/ML applications. You’ll be part of a team that pushes boundaries, developing custom silicon solutions that power the future of Google's TPU. You'll contribute to the innovation behind products loved by millions worldwide, and leverage your design and verification expertise to verify complex digital designs, with a specific focus on TPU architecture and its integration within AI/ML-driven systems.

As an ASIC Design Verification Manager for Google's TPU designs, you will lead a team and own the functional verification for key components by guiding the development of advanced infrastructure at the subchip, subsystem, and full-chip levels. This includes developing comprehensive test plans, writing diagnostic codes, and building monitors and checkers to ensure quality assurance.

Additionally, you will partner closely with front-end design, architecture, and performance teams. By analyzing coverage across multiple dimensions, you will help ensure architectural compliance, verify functional correctness, and guide your team to meet key performance goals.

The AI and Infrastructure team is redefining what’s possible. We empower Google customers with breakthrough capabilities and insights by delivering AI and Infrastructure at unparalleled scale, efficiency, reliability and velocity. Our customers include Googlers, Google Cloud customers, and billions of Google users worldwide.

We're the driving force behind Google's groundbreaking innovations, empowering the development of our cutting-edge AI models, delivering unparalleled computing power to global services, and providing the essential platforms that enable developers to build the future. From software to hardware our teams are shaping the future of world-leading hyperscale computing, with key teams working on the development of our TPUs, Vertex AI for Google Cloud, Google Global Networking, Data Center operations, systems research, and much more.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $192000 - $278000 (USD) + 20% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google.
  • Guide the functional verification team for portions of TPU designs, setting and communicating individual and team priorities that support organizational goals, providing regular feedback and coaching, and developing functional verification infrastructure across subchip, subsystem, and fullchip level environments.
  • Define and guide advanced verification strategies, including the use of simulation, for bug hunt, formal verification for corner-case bugs and emulation for system validation.
  • Partner with front-end design, architecture, and performance teams to help ensure architectural compliance and achievement of performance goals.
  • Analyze coverage from various dimensions and develop monitors and checkers for quality assurance.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 10 years of experience with verification, SystemVerilog, and UVM.
  • 3 years of experience in people management.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Master's degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or Computer Science, with an emphasis on computer architecture.
  • Experience with universal verification methodology (UVM), SystemVerilog, or other scripting languages such as Python, Perl, Shell, Bash, etc.
  • Knowledge of general purpose operating systems such as Linux and Android.
  • Familiarity with ARM Instruction Set Architecture.

Position Title:

Office Specialist 2, Out of Facility Medical Scheduler (Salem)

Job Description:

Office Specialist 2, Out of Facility Medical Scheduler (Salem)

CTRS – Salem, Oregon

Oregon Department of Corrections

About the Job – Your Role

In this role, you will provide clerical support for the operation of the Medical Services Division. The successful candidate will be responsible for ensuring the accurate maintenance and filing (paper and electronic) medical and dental records, facilitating timely written and verbal communication, compiling statistics and routine reports, and scheduling healthcare appointments.

This position ensures adults in custody (AICs) receive the necessary healthcare services outside of the correctional facility, such as specialized medical treatments, consultation, or diagnostic tests that cannot be provided within the facility. Coordinating the scheduling of the appointments and transportation to and from the institution and medical appointments. Responsible for interpreting and applying rules, statues, procedures, guidelines, and polices. This position requires a high level of organization, attention to detail, the ability to manage multiple tasks and problem solve as things occur.

Office equipment and systems:

  • Microsoft Office Programs:

    • Word

    • Excel

    • Outlook

    • Publisher

  • Typing - 60wpm

  • Multi-line telephone system

  • Copy machine

  • Shredder

The person in this position may work within a prison setting and is responsible for maintaining security and supervision of adults in custody (AICs). The demands of the work environment are chaotic. Clerical staff are responsible for maintaining accurate AIC tracking systems for populations ranging from 100 to 3000, with large volumes of AIC movement in and out of the institution on a daily basis.

This position is represented by American Federation of State, County, and Municipal Employees (AFSCME). This position may be eligible for Police & Fire (P&F) benefits through Public Employees Retirement System (PERS), as defined by statute.

Minimum Qualifications

Two years of general clerical experience that includes keyboarding, word processing, or other experience generating documents.

OR

An associate degree in any field.

OR

An equivalent combination of education and experience.

Requested Skills

  • Medical and appointment scheduling

  • Coordination with external providers

  • Interpersonal and communication skills

  • Procedure codes and medical terminology

  • Strong customer service

  • Working with HIPAA guidelines and confidential information

  • A minimum of two years of experience working in a medical healthcare setting

  • Experience with an electronic health record

Preference will be given to those candidates with medical scheduler experience.

Application Information

  • In the Work Experience section of your application make sure to include the dates and duties of all relevant positions and details to support how you meet these attributes. If you do not include education or work experience meeting the minimum qualifications, you will not be considered for the position. Only the candidates whose experience most closely matches the qualifications and requested skills of this position will be invited to interview. Applicants must meet the minimum qualifications on or before the job posting close date.

  • The job posting closes at 11:59 PM (PDT/PST) on the close date. After you submit your application, be sure to respond to the two questionnaires relating to public records requests and veterans’ preference immediately following your submittal. These questions are necessary to complete the application process.

  • Please monitor both your email and Workday account for updates regarding this recruitment.

  • As part of our selection process, we may require additional assessment stages, such as written exercises, to further evaluate candidates’ qualifications. Meaningful participation in these exercises is required for all applicants moving forward in the process. Failure to complete the required exercise(s) within the specified timeframe will result in disqualification from consideration. All candidates who successfully complete these screening stages and meet the necessary requirements will advance to the next stage in the selection process.

  • Please save a copy of this job announcement for reference, as it is not available for you to view after the announcement deadline.

Working Conditions

Will be expected to share the mission, vision, and core values of the department; requires being a role model of pro-social behavior and having an attitude that conveys dignity and respect in the treatment of others; must be able to acknowledge that everyone is capable of positive change; requires contact with AICs who may become violent; requires walking or standing for long periods, requires climbing and descending stairs; exposed to chemicals, radiation, communicable diseases or other hazards inherent in a health care and correctional setting. Supervision and control of AICs is an inherent responsibility. May be required to assist with the inventory and accountability of controlled items including sharps, tools, and other items that cause a potential security concern. May also be required to perform other tasks that assist with the safety and security of the institution including, but not limited to, performing area searches, supervision of AIC orderlies, and performing AIC counts.

You must have a valid driver’s license and a good driving record or be able to provide an acceptable alternative method of transportation.

About the Department

The Oregon Department of Corrections is responsible for over 12,000 adults in custody in 12 state prisons throughout Oregon. It advises and evaluates counties regarding administration of probation and parole programs supervising more than 24,000 offenders in Oregon communities. The mission is to protect communities, promote accountability, and transform lives.

The Oregon Department of Corrections serves a diverse and changing population of people who are incarcerated and on supervision. We commit to creating an organization both reflecting the diversity of the population we serve and ensuring all employees thrive in a culture of safety, trust, and belonging. We strive to be an anti-racist corrections system. Welcoming, inclusive, and respectful of all people. Free of discrimination, harassment, and retaliation.

The Department offers a variety of programs and opportunity to create a safe and healthy environment to for our staff, volunteers, and adults in custody. Joining the Oregon Department of Corrections is joining a team working for the benefit of our communities through innovative and proven correctional practices.

Benefits

The salary range listed above is for non-PERS qualifying applicants. PERS qualifying applicants may be eligible for an adjusted range to reflect an additional 6.95%.

The State of Oregon provides a generous benefit package, which includes:

  • Family health, vision, and dental insurance

  • Vacation, sick leave, and 11 paid holidays

  • 21 days paid military leave for national guard and reserve components

  • Optional short and long-term disability

  • Term life insurance

  • Fully paid retirement program

  • Oregon Saving Growth Plan

  • Flexible spending accounts for health and childcare

  • And more

  • Top candidates will be referred to the hiring manager.

  • The hiring manager will review your application and schedule interviews.

  • Interview will be held with a panel of stakeholders who have completed panel assessment training. Scores will be determined based on predetermined questions and scoring guides. Preferences points will be applied in compliance with relevant laws and bargaining agreements. There may be multiple rounds of interviews.

  • Final candidates will have a background check, PREA check, and reference checks.

  • A Classification and Compensation analyst will review the Workday Application of the successful candidate to determine starting wages. Learn more about Equal Pay.

  • A job offer will be extended through Workday to the successful candidate. Congratulations, and welcome to the team!

The successful candidate for this position must pass a Criminal Justice Information Systems (CJIS) fingerprint-based background check and maintain CJIS eligibility. Due to CJIS requirements related to system access, there may be some felony convictions that could disqualify you for this position. However, having a felony record does not exclusively restrict you from being considered as an applicant. CJIS clearance is done at the conditional job offer. If you have questions about whether or not your criminal record could disqualify for you, please contact the recruiter for more information.

Additional information can be found from The U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) Know Your Rights.
