title: Säkerhetsskyddsspecialist
description:
Vi söker nu en erfaren säkerhetsskyddsspecialist till ett kvalificerat uppdrag inom samhällskritisk offentlig verksamhet. Rollen passar dig som har gedigen erfarenhet av systematiskt säkerhetsskyddsarbete, säkerhetsskyddsbedömningar och analytiskt arbete kopplat till säkerhetskänslig verksamhet.

Du får en central roll i arbetet med att säkerställa att samarbeten med externa företag och organisationer sker under rätt säkerhetsmässiga förutsättningar.

Om uppdraget

Som säkerhetsskyddsspecialist kommer du att arbeta med leverantörssäkerhet och säkerhetsskyddad upphandling. Arbetet omfattar hela kedjan från särskilda säkerhetsskyddsbedömningar till utformning, tecknande och uppföljning av säkerhetsskyddsavtal.

En viktig del av rollen är att genom strukturerade analyser och välgrundade bedömningar utreda företag och organisationer som kan exponeras för säkerhetskänslig verksamhet.

Du kommer även att fungera som stöd och rådgivare till verksamheten samt ha kontakt med myndigheter och andra externa aktörer.

Arbetsuppgifter

  • Stödja verksamheten vid framtagning av särskilda säkerhetsskyddsbedömningar
  • Granska och kvalitetssäkra säkerhetsskyddsbedömningar
  • Stödja vid utformning av säkerhetsskyddsavtal
  • Arbeta med samarbets- och samverkansavtal ur ett säkerhetsskyddsperspektiv
  • Genomföra lämplighetsprövningar
  • Genomföra leverantörsbedömningar
  • Analysera exponering av säkerhetskänslig verksamhet
  • Bedöma skyddsvärden och sårbarheter
  • Utbilda och vägleda verksamheten inom säkerhetsskydd
  • Genomföra samråd och samverkan med relevanta myndigheter och organisationer

Obligatoriska krav

Vi söker dig som har:

  • Minst 5 års arbetslivserfarenhet av systematiskt säkerhetsskyddsarbete
  • Minst 5 års arbetslivserfarenhet av analytiskt arbete inom ramen för säkerhetsskydd
  • Minst 2 års arbetslivserfarenhet av att genomföra, granska eller ta fram särskilda säkerhetsskyddsbedömningar
  • Minst 2 års arbetslivserfarenhet inom offentlig verksamhet
  • God förmåga att uttrycka dig på svenska och engelska i både tal och skrift

Mervärdeskrav

Det är särskilt meriterande om du har:

  • Minst 2 års erfarenhet av arbete med säkerhetsskyddsanalys
  • Minst 2 års erfarenhet av arbete med exponering av säkerhetskänslig verksamhet
  • Minst 2 års erfarenhet av arbete med bedömningar av skyddsvärden och sårbarheter

Personliga egenskaper

För att lyckas i rollen ser vi att du är analytisk, strukturerad och noggrann med god förmåga att göra välgrundade bedömningar i komplexa säkerhetsfrågor.

Du är kommunikativ och pedagogisk och känner dig trygg i att vägleda verksamheten och förklara säkerhetsskyddsfrågor för olika målgrupper. Rollen kräver även hög integritet, ansvarstagande och förmåga att arbeta både självständigt och tillsammans med andra.

Viktigt

Säkerhetsprövning och registerkontroll krävs.

  • Plats: Sundbyberg, Stockholm
  • Arbetsform: huvudsakligen arbete på plats
  • Distansarbete: kan förekomma upp till 40 % efter överenskommelse och utifrån verksamhetens behov
  • Sista ansökningsdag: 30 september 2026

Om Soros Consulting

Soros Consulting arbetar med kvalificerad konsultförmedling inom IT, teknik och verksamhetsutveckling. Vi matchar erfarna specialister med uppdrag där deras kompetens skapar tydliga resultat. Vårt fokus är kvalitet, långsiktighet och att skapa goda förutsättningar både för konsulter och uppdragsgivare genom tydlighet, professionalism och hållbara relationer.

title: MAX Midgårdsvägen söker restaurangbiträde
description:
Vi vill bli världens bästa burgarkedja och vi vet att vägen dit går genom engagerade medarbetare, starka team, grym service och riktigt goda burgare. Nu söker vi dig som vill vara med och skapa serviceupplevelser i världsklass vid varje besök.

Som restaurangbiträde på MAX är du en nyckelperson i vårt dagliga arbete. Tillsammans med dina kollegor ser du till att våra gäster får bästa möjliga bemötande och att restaurangen alltid levererar på högsta nivå. Både när det gäller kvalitet, tempo och service. Du arbetar i team och har varierande arbetsuppgifter: du serverar gäster, håller rent och snyggt i restaurangen, jobbar i köket med att laga burgare och pommes, och ansvarar för kassan där du ser till att gästerna får det som beställts varor. Hos oss är arbetsglädje, gemenskap och utveckling alltid i centrum. Så under dina första dagar lär du dig jobbet steg för steg av din restaurangchef eller en erfaren kollega och på vår lärplattform MAX Academy via digitala utbildningar.

Huvudsakliga arbetsuppgifter

  • Servera gäster, ge ett schyst bemötande och skapa serviceupplevelser i världsklass
  • Hålla rent och snyggt i restaurangen
  • Laga burgare, smoothies och pommes i köket
  • Ansvara för kassan och se till att gästerna får det som beställts
  • Arbeta i team och stötta dina kollegor

Vad erbjuder vi?

  • Ett fartfyllt jobb i ett sammansvetsat team med mycket goda möjligheter att växa och utvecklas
  • Interna utbildningar och tydliga karriärvägar
  • Lön och villkor enligt kollektivavtal samt friskvårdsbidrag
  • En arbetsplats där bemötandet, goda burgare, en ren och fräsch restaurang och snabb service alltid står i fokus
  • En kultur där vi lägger stor vikt vid hälsa, miljö och socialt ansvar

Hur går processen till?

För våra tjänster som restaurangmedarbetare har vi valt ett enklare och mer relevant sätt att söka jobb. Det betyder att du inte behöver skicka in CV eller personligt brev. I stället får du svara på några urvalsfrågor och genomföra ett Servicetest. Vi rekommenderar att du svarar så utförligt och ärligt du kan på frågorna.

När du har skickat in din ansökan får du ett mejl med en länk till Servicetestet. Testet består av olika situationer som kan uppstå i vardagen på MAX, där du får beskriva hur du skulle agera. På så sätt får du redan tidigt en bra bild av hur det är att jobba hos oss. Testet tar cirka 15 minuter att genomföra.

När vi har gått igenom både din ansökan och ditt test återkopplar vi till dig så snart vi kan. Går du vidare i processen blir du inbjuden till intervju. Om du inte går vidare får du besked via mejl. Vi hanterar ansökningarna löpande, vilket innebär att tjänsten kan tillsättas innan sista ansökningsdag.

Observera att Servicetestet är ett obligatoriskt steg i vår rekryteringsprocess och att vi därför inte kan ta kandidater vidare som inte genomför testet.

Välkommen att skicka in din ansökan!

Vill du läsa om hur vi hanterar dina personuppgifter? Gå in på www.max.se/dataskydd

Öppen för alla Vi fokuserar på din kompetens, inte dina övriga förutsättningar. Vi är öppna för att anpassa rollen eller arbetsplatsen efter dina behov.

title: Data Engineer
description:
Bij de ASN Bank geloven we dat data de sleutel is tot het begrijpen van onze klanten en het behalen van onze organisatiedoelen in een steeds digitalere wereld. Als Data Engineer binnen ons CFO-domein speel jij een centrale rol in het vertalen van complexe toezichthoudervereisten naar concrete, werkbare oplossingen voor de ASN Bank. Daarnaast ben je betrokken bij de implementatie van een nieuwe regulatory reporting engine.


Ontdek hieronder precies welke vaardigheden, ervaring en kwalificaties u nodig heeft om te slagen in deze functie, voordat u solliciteert.
Wat ga je doen?

Als Data Engineer ben jij de go-to persoon voor data vraagstukken binnen het team. Je werkt in een dynamisch DevOps-team dat verantwoordelijk is voor één of meerdere datamarts en draagt bij aan betrouwbare rapportages voor zowel interne stakeholders als externe toezichthouders.

Jouw dagelijkse werkzaamheden omvatten:
  • Datamonitoring: Je dag start met een stand-up en het controleren of data correct is geladen in het datawarehouse en de datamart
  • Requirement analyse: Je vertaalt eisen van toezichthouders naar duidelijke, voor de ASN Bank geldende requirements
  • Datamodellering: Je modelleert nieuwe data entiteiten en stelt modelleringsvoorstellen op
  • Stakeholder management: Je schakelt actief met business, broneigenaren en finance developers
  • Incidentbeheer: Je lost complexe technische en functionele vraagstukken op
  • Code reviews: Je reviewt het werk van collega's en presenteert je eigen ontwerpen
Hier kom je te werken

Je maakt deel uit van het Data Delivery team binnen het CFO-domein, een team van gedreven data professionals die dagelijks werken aan betrouwbare cijfers en rapportages. We werken volgens de Agile/Scrum methodiek, waarbij samenwerking en kennisdeling centraal staan. Iedereen reviewt elkaars werk en belangrijke kennis wordt geborgd in onze eigen Wiki.

Wat breng jij mee?

Wij zoeken een collega die:

  • Nieuwsgierig, proactief en inhoudelijk gedreven is
  • Over afdelingsgrenzen heen kan kijken en informatieketens in kaart kan brengen
  • Makkelijk contact legt met zowel business- en IT-collega's
Vereiste kennis en ervaring:
  • Aantoonbare ervaring met Datawarehousing
  • Sterke kennis van SQL
  • Kennis van Power Designer
  • Ervaring in informatie- en probleemanalyse
Pré als je ook beschikt over:
  • Kennis van GIT, Powercenter en/of Stonebranch
  • Kennis van Regulatory Reporting en/of Regnology
Wat krijg je van ons?
  • Een flexibel in te delen 36-urige werkweek, zoals 4x9 en thuiswerken
  • Vakantiegeld en een 13e maand, op een moment dat het jou goed uitkomt
  • Op basis van een fulltime dienstverband: 208,8 uur verlofuren per jaar
  • Een goede collectieve pensioenregeling
  • € 750,- per jaar om jezelf te blijven ontwikkelen (te sparen tot € 3.000,-)
  • Elke 5 jaar € 900,- om je thuiswerkplek weer helemaal op orde te maken
  • Een NS-Business Card en een kilometervergoeding voor als je op de fiets komt
Over ons

ASN Bank is een toegankelijke en vooruitstrevende bank met oog voor mens, maatschappij en de toekomst. We dragen op duurzame wijze bij aan financiële oplossingen voor onze klanten én aan maatschappelijke vraagstukken in Nederland. Daarbij hebben we bijzondere aandacht voor duurzaamheid, financieel welzijn en goed wonen. xgiwjmb Als bank combineren we het gemak van veilig mobiel bankieren met de kracht van persoonlijk advies.

title: Senior Account Representative, SMB (West/Central)
description:
The Company

PayPal has been revolutionizing commerce globally for more than 25 years. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy.

We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We help merchants and consumers connect, transact, and complete payments, whether they are online or in person. PayPal is more than a connection to third-party payment networks. We provide proprietary payment solutions accepted by merchants that enable the completion of payments on our platform on behalf of our customers.

We offer our customers the flexibility to use their accounts to purchase and receive payments for goods and services, as well as the ability to transfer and withdraw funds. We enable consumers to exchange funds more safely with merchants using a variety of funding sources, which may include a bank account, a PayPal or Venmo account balance, PayPal and Venmo branded credit products, a credit card, a debit card, certain cryptocurrencies, or other stored value products such as gift cards, and eligible credit card rewards. Our PayPal, Venmo, and Xoom products also make it safer and simpler for friends and family to transfer funds to each other. We offer merchants an end-to-end payments solution that provides authorization and settlement capabilities, as well as instant access to funds and payouts. We also help merchants connect with their customers, process exchanges and returns, and manage risk. We enable consumers to engage in cross-border shopping and merchants to extend their global reach while reducing the complexity and friction involved in enabling cross-border trade.

Our beliefs are the foundation for how we conduct business every day. We live each day guided by our core values of Inclusion, Innovation, Collaboration, and Wellness. Together, our values ensure that we work together as one global team with our customers at the center of everything we do – and they push us to ensure we take care of ourselves, each other, and our communities.

Job Summary:

As PayPal continues its mission to revolutionize commerce, we’re looking for a driven Senior Account Representative to join our Small and Medium Business Sales team in Germany.

Small businesses are the engine of local economies everywhere, and PayPal’s SMB team helps them compete on a bigger stage. In this role, you’ll own the end-to-end commercial relationships for a portfolio of around 80 of our higher-value SMB merchants across West and Central Germany.

You’ll proactively identify opportunities to deepen relationships, expand product adoption and solve merchant needs to protect and grow transaction margin. It’s a role for someone who wants real ownership, from spotting the next growth opportunity to working through merchant problems that don’t yet have a playbook.

This is a virtual position, with our German headquarters located in Berlin.

Essential Responsibilities:

  • Collaborate internally to influence process quality and efficiency.
  • Determine appropriate actions and consider alternative solutions.
  • Acquire, manage, and expand relationships with small and medium-sized merchants.
  • Use analytical skills and judgment to recommend best solutions.
  • Influence through defined processes and procedures.

  • Own the commercial relationship with your merchants across West and Central Germany, working closely with colleagues across PayPal to deliver strong end-to-end outcomes.

  • Develop tailored account plans and commercial strategies for these strategically important merchants.

  • Use AI-powered tools to identify growth, cross-sell and risk signals across your portfolio.

  • Keep pipeline, forecast and portfolio health reporting accurate, and support less experienced AM colleagues by sharing what works.

  • Bring together the right internal teams to resolve merchant needs and work through ambiguous issues where no established playbook exists.

  • A track record of owning high-value or strategic customer relationships and the commercial outcomes that come with them.

  • Quantifiable examples of retaining and growing a complex book of business through cross-sell, upsell or wallet-share growth.

  • Comfortable using AI and commercial data to prioritise opportunities, focus your time and intervene early where there is a risk of churn or decline.

  • A problem-solver who can work beyond standard playbooks, weigh alternatives and reach commercially sound outcomes on ambiguous merchant issues.

  • A strong internal collaborator who can mobilise partners across the business, maintain clear account plans and forecasts, and reliably close out actions.

title: Logistics Assistant MedLog
description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

Background

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the world's largest humanitarian agencies, providing relief, rehabilitation, and post-conflict support to victims of oppression and violent conflict in 42 countries. IRC is committed to bold leadership, innovation, and creative partnerships. South Sudan, an independent nation since 9th July 2011, is emerging from decades of brutal civil war rooted in disputes over religion, ethnicity, resources, governance, and self-determination. The security situation remains fragile, and the operational context is challenging. IRC has been in South Sudan since 1989 and currently operates in Northern Bahr el Ghazal, Lakes, Unity, Upper Nile, and Central Equatoria States.

This position sits within IRC South Sudan's Supply Chain function and supports both general field-office inventory/asset management and the pharmaceutical and cold-chain logistics needs of IRC's health programs in responding to emergency in Akobo.

Job Overview

The Logistics Assistant Med Log is responsible for the efficient coordination, supervision, and management of warehousing, inventory, and asset/property functions at the IRC field office, while also serving as the dedicated focal point for receiving CIKs and management, and reporting of any Warehouse related activities. Advise on the storage space needs as the program Implementation grows and plans. S/he will act as the bridge between the Supply Chain team and the Health Unit, ensuring that both general inventory/asset management and medical commodity management are carried out to IRC, donor, national Ministry of Health (MOH), and international drug-management standards.

Key Responsibilities/Duties

1. Pharmaceutical, Vaccine & Cold Chain Management

  • Ensure, cold chain items, medicines, and medical supplies are properly stored in the warehouse and compliant with international, national, and IRC drug management standards and protocols.
  • Maintain accurate stock records, submit periodic supply requisitions, and ensure safe Medicines and vaccine storage in the warehouse.
  • Ensure documentation and reporting of all medical commodities, vaccine, and cold chain data, including vaccine wastage, from all project locations.
  • Assist health officers and County Health Departments (CHDs) in developing micro-plans, including drafting monthly and annual progress reports and vaccine forecasts for adequate and timely supply of vaccines and logistics; distribute to session sites as per the micro-plan.
  • Immediately report any breach of the cold chain or other protocol to the technical supervisor and line manager to allow for timely corrective response.
  • Ensure injection safety, including proper waste disposal and daily temperature monitoring/recording, per national protocols and guidelines.
  • Implement GSC SOPs on pharmaceutical inventory management and follow up the essential drug list (EDL) in collaboration with the Country Pharmacist.
  • Check that deadlines for medicine, pharmaceutical, and vaccine deliveries to designated field sites are respected; flag short-expiry items for early distribution.
  • Ensure dedicated, temperature-controlled space is allocated for sensitive medicines, vaccines, and other pharmaceuticals, and that temperature control devices are recorded and always reported.
  • Support medical data collection, entry, analysis, and reporting in collaboration with M&E and the Emergency Coordinator.

2. Materials Receiving, Dispatch & Warehouse Documentation

  • Manage and document the materials receiving process (handling and storage), and inspect materials during dispatch, maintaining up-to-date documentation.
  • Monitor potential inventory shortages and provide regular updates on stock levels.
  • Organize a cold chain system to ensure "keep-cool" items are handled appropriately and manage all Contribution in Kind (CIK) and closed-grant inventory.
  • Organize replenishment of field drug warehouses as need arises, based on approved requisitions.
  • Update stock cards, bin cards, and the inventory system regularly; implement standard warehouse documentation (Delivery Reports, Waybills, Store Release forms, Bin Cards, Stock Cards).
  • Maintain the Warehouse Activity Book (Warehouse Register) for all incoming and outgoing receipts and activities and ensure the Warehouse Authorization Schedule is up to date and displayed.
  • Ensure consistency of warehouse documentation and reporting, including dispatch documents, waybills, distribution, and/or donation letters.
  • Report any loss or damage of pharmaceuticals, vaccines, or other supplies observed during shipment or delivery to management through documentation.
  • Inspect samples of delivered supplies and check for conformity upon goods receipt and during dispatch, using order documentation and receipt SOPs.

3. Warehouse Controls & Safety

  • Participate in and produce accurate reports for year-end count exercises and fully participate in the 20% inventory cycle count for all stock kept in the warehouse.
  • Conduct internal inventory checks and maintain records of all cycle counts; ensure physical inventories are conducted monthly and communicated to the health program and Supply Chain.
  • Implement FIFO, FEFO, and LIFO procedures for goods in the warehouse, and drive improvements in stock reporting accuracy for medicines and medical supply inventories.
  • Ensure the warehouse is restricted to visitors, with appropriate signage displayed in strategic locations, and manage casual laborers working in the warehouse.
  • Implement clear safety procedures; ensure maintenance of warehouse buildings, fittings, and equipment.
  • Ensure the warehouse is regularly fumigated against pests, rats, and rodents, and that fire extinguishers are maintained and serviced regularly.
  • Work with the Safety, Security, and Admin team on warehouse safety and security measures, and prepare plans for improvement.

4. Asset & Property Management

  • Take the lead on assets and property management, including needs assessments and implementation of donor requirements (e.g., UNHCR, USAID, DFID, MOH, UN, USG, EU, SV, and other private donors), and South Sudanese government regulations.
  • Develop assets running-cost analyses and ensure reporting accuracy.
  • Conduct periodic spot checks on asset movements and maintain transfer records of assets between the Juba office and field sites.
  • Ensure all assets are controlled and managed properly in accordance with donor-specific policies and implement/maintain standard IRC asset management policies and procedures.
  • Update the Asset Register, Asset Inventory List, and Expendable Store Inventory List, and produce monthly reports.
  • Work closely with the Supply Chain Coordinator on asset disposal processes (donation, auction, transfer), disposing of IRC assets per donor regulation, approval, and organizational policy.
  • Visit field sites or partner offices for asset inventory (physical counts) during reporting periods and pull updated asset lists for end-of-grant reporting.

5. Field Support, Training & Quality Assurance

  • Provide day-to-day orientation and training to storekeepers and EPI vaccinators on warehouse forms and stock-rotation mechanisms (FIFO/FEFO).
  • Conduct relevant training for health field officers and logistics staff as needed, and ensure that the warehouse is properly set up, cleaned, and secured.
  • Follow up with the line manager and technical supervisor on any field-reported product-quality issues and maintain a claims file.
  • Conduct any other duties and responsibilities assigned by the supervisor.

6. Reporting

  • Prepare weekly/monthly drug and pharmaceutical receipt, distribution, and dispatch records for the Country Pharmacist.
  • Prepare and submit a monthly Warehouse/Inventory and Asset/Property report to the Supply Chain Manager based in Juba by the 1st of every month.

7. Key Working Relationships

Reports to: Field Manager/ Country Pharmacist, with a matrixed reporting line to the Senior Supply Chain Manager.

Direct supervisors: Field Manager.

Internal/External Contacts: Builds and maintains excellent relationships with country health and supply chain teams at all levels, health managers and coordinators, County Health Departments across counties Regular relationships with program staff, Operations, and Juba Supply Chain staff. Actively participates in Emergency project activities and may lead sessions as required. May serve as an IRC representative in external meetings with other NGOs, inter-agency groups, foundations, partners, and donors at field level as may be required.

8. Job Qualifications, Skills, and Experience

Education: Bachelor's degree or diploma in Pharmacy, Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business Administration, or a related field. An advanced professional certificate in health supply chain management and/or emergency response management is preferred.

Work Experience: At least 2–3 years of relevant experience in humanitarian health supply chain, warehousing, inventory, and/or asset management. Demonstrated ability to participate in developing and rolling out supply chain policy and SOPs. Clear training and mentoring ability. Experience working with a diverse portfolio of donors and knowledge of specific donor guidelines.

Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:

High degree of flexibility and ability to work under sometimes extreme hardship conditions against tight deadlines.

Familiarity with drug inventory management and medical supply chain principles.

Good knowledge of practical supply chain procedures and maintaining supply pipelines in areas with weak infrastructure.

Strong computer and communication equipment skills, including Microsoft Office applications (word processing, spreadsheets, databases).

Ability to lead teams; skilled in change management, risk management, decision-making, cross-functional collaboration, and conflict resolution.

Strong organizational, interpersonal, and analytical skills; a good collaborator and influencer able to work seamlessly across cultures, organizational units, and suppliers.

Willingness to participate and contribute as a team member under challenging working and living conditions, and to work effectively in a highly matrixed structure.

Language Skills: Fluency in English required. Good working knowledge of Arabic is an added advantage.

9. Compliance

Ensure that all activities respect the principle of confidentiality and that all incidents reported to IRC are handled with due regard to protection principles.

Ensure adherence to IRC South Sudan-specific finance, logistics, IT, security, communications, and human resources/administration policies and procedures.

Incorporate and comply with any new procedures and guidelines designated in circulars from the Country Director.

Ensure any violations of the IRC Sexual Abuse and Exploitation Code of Conduct are reported to the supervisor, the Country Director, or through the anonymous reporting mechanism; reporting violations is an obligation of all staff members.

Assist, where necessary, in undertaking activities that aim to prevent sexual abuse and exploitation of beneficiaries by IRC and other humanitarian workers.

Ensure compliance with IRC's Child Safeguarding policy in all IRC activities, and report any violations observed or reported through the necessary channels immediately.

10. The IRC Core Values and Commitments

Standards of Professional Conduct: The IRC and IRC workers must adhere to the values and principles outlined in the IRC Way – Standards for Professional Conduct. These are Integrity, Service, Accountability, and Equality. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Beneficiary Protection from Exploitation and Abuse, Child Safeguarding, Anti Workplace Harassment, Fiscal Integrity, and Anti-Retaliation.

Safeguarding and PSEA Policy: The IRC has a zero-tolerance policy for safeguarding/PSEA violations by staff, incentive workers, visitors, sub-grantees, suppliers/sub-contractors, and implementing partners. Safeguarding/PSEA at IRC is integral to the organization's values and ethics; staff and associates are expected to take all reasonable steps to prevent the sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment of any person linked to the program, whether by IRC employees or any downstream partner. The successful candidate will be subject to a thorough background check and satisfactory references.

IRC promotes and actively participates in initiatives to build team engagement, inclusion, and cohesion, fostering ongoing learning, honest dialogue, and reflection to strengthen safeguarding and promote adherence to IRC values and policies.

Narrowing the Gender Gap: IRC is committed to narrowing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer benefits that provide an enabling environment for women to participate in our workforce, including parental/maternity leave, flexible hours (when possible), transportation support, and gender-sensitive security protocols.

Equal Opportunity Employer: IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants based on merit, without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

We encourage applications from members of historically underrepresented racial/ethnic groups, women, individuals with disabilities, veterans, LGBTQIA2S+ community members, and others to help us achieve our vision of a diverse and inclusive community.

This is a temporary position and is approved through 06/30/2027. Temporary positions will end approximately 6 months after the employment start date (after 1,040 hours have been worked).

Opportunity awaits! Are you passionate about engaging with families and communities? Are you committed to ensuring the well-being of others and offering them support? Would you enjoy working with a team that is dedicated to serving children, families, and communities? If so, we’d love to hear from you!

Summary of Duties

As a Temporary Lodging SSA, you will:

As an employee working within the Child Welfare Program, you will have an opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of Oregon’s most vulnerable children and families. Your dedication will help us achieve the Child Welfare Vision for Transformation that will support children and young adults to be safer, healthier, experience less trauma and achieve a greater well-being.

  • Stay with and supervise children throughout the day in temporary lodging and transport them to different destinations as needed.

  • Transport children as needed for appointments, school, or any other needs as directed by caseworker, supervisor. Transportation may include inter- or intrastate as well as medical/dental appointments.

  • Address inappropriate behavior by applying general parenting techniques while honoring ethnic, and cultural standards according to policy.

  • When not in temporary lodging you will support in-home safety plans by providing detailed documentation, support, engagement, and promptly reporting any concerns.

  • Review and implement supervisory and safety plans, while also supporting their behavior and emotional needs.

  • Maintain care for children related to hygiene, basic needs, school attendance, appointments, and transportation.

  • Treat people with compassion and dignity, ensuring that children and family members feel respected and valued.

Minimum Qualifications

  • One year of experience working in a human services or behavioral health setting; OR

  • An associate degree in any field; OR

  • An equivalent combination of education and experience.

Essential Attributes

We are looking for candidates with:

  • Experience remaining patient, composed, and professional when responding to challenging situations, individuals, or competing priorities, while maintaining respectful and equitable interactions.

  • Experience recognizing how trauma and challenging life experiences may affect individuals and respond with patience, empathy, respect, and appropriate professional boundaries.

  • Experience communicating clearly, professionally, and respectfully through written and verbal communication, adapting communication to the audience and situation.

  • Experience identifying solutions to challenges by assessing available information, considering options, and taking appropriate action to achieve positive outcomes.

Attention all candidates! A COVER LETTER IS PREFERRED.

  • Your application materials will determine if you are selected to move forward in the selection process. Please include detailed work and education history.

  • Please upload a resume or complete the work history profile. Note: Your resume and cover letter may be uploaded in the Resume/CV field on the online application.

  • If you are selected as the final candidate and a degree is listed as a minimum qualification for the position, please be prepared to provide verification of your completed education before moving forward in the hiring process.

  • The use of outside resources such as Artificial Intelligence software during applicant skill assessments, examinations, and/or interviews is prohibited unless otherwise stated by the hiring agency. Unauthorized use of outside resources during the hiring process will result in disqualification.

  • The State of Oregon does not request or require your age, date of birth, attendance or graduation dates from an educational institution during the application process.

Working Conditions

  • Work Schedule: There is no typical normal workday of 8 hours, from 8 AM to 5 PM. Working hours are often adjusted within a given week.

  • Occasional, compensated overtime may be required, including evening and weekend work.

  • Work will be conducted in offices, participant's homes, hotels, hospitals, and other community sites.

  • Occasional travel is required for meetings, training, and case-related activities.

  • You will interact with a wide range of people, including some who have experienced trauma and may exhibit challenges in controlling their emotions.

  • You may encounter stressful situations that require quick decision-making to ensure safety of yourself and others.

  • Activities include traversing stairs, moving on uneven terrain, and helping children (weighing up to 50 pounds) in and out of car seats.

Background Checks and Requirements

Within three days of hire, you will be required to complete the US Department of Homeland Security’s I-9 form confirming authorization to work in the United States. ODHS will use E-Verify to confirm that you are authorized to work in the United States.

  • Finalists must be cleared by the FBI Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) through a fingerprint-based criminal records check.

Benefits

Employment Preference

Veterans’ and Oregon National Guard preference:

description:

Over Eduface

Eduface is een Nederlandse EdTech-startup die een AI‑assistant bouwt voor feedback en beoordeling in het hoger onderwijs. Ons lokaal gehoste model helpt universiteiten de kwaliteit van feedback te verbeteren, terwijl docenten doorgaans tot 50 % van hun tijd besparen. title: Nordic Country Controller
description:
Job Summary

Nordic Country Controller

Ready to play a key role in financial controllership, statutory reporting, and compliance across the Nordic region while partnering with the Finance Director and global stakeholders?

IFF is a global leader in flavors, fragrances, food ingredients and health & biosciences. We deliver sustainable innovations that elevate everyday products.

Finance: Empowering strategic decisions through expertise; fueling sustainable growth by delivering insights, managing risk and driving value across global operations.

The role is based in Budapest, Hungary (hybrid role). Be part of a collaborative, detail-oriented, and solution-focused team where together we can achieve greatness and make a real impact. Your potential is our inspiration.

Where You'll Make a Difference

  • Act as the primary local finance coordinator and point of contact for statutory reporting, compliance, and controllership activities across Denmark, Sweden, and Finland, working closely with the Finance Director.

  • Coordinate statutory audits, manage auditor requests, and ensure timely delivery of supporting documentation and audit requirements in partnership with the Finance Director and key stakeholders.

  • Support the preparation, review, and submission of annual financial statements, disclosures, and statutory reporting packages.

  • Partner with Tax, Legal, Shared Service Center, and external auditors to ensure compliance with local regulations and reporting deadlines.

  • Monitor and follow up on tax authority correspondence, tax audits, regulatory inquiries, and statutory filing requirements.

  • Perform monthly general ledger reviews, balance sheet analyses, and financial statement variance assessments.

  • Support month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close activities while ensuring key account reconciliations are completed accurately and on time.

  • Facilitate finance review meetings with business stakeholders and support the Finance Director on accounting, compliance, and reporting matters.

  • Coordinate Board of Directors approval processes, statutory filings, governance activities, and legal entity compliance requirements.

  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives within controllership, audit coordination, statutory reporting, and compliance processes.

What Makes You the Right Fit

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, or a related field.

  • Minimum 5 years of experience in accounting, controllership, statutory reporting, audit coordination, or a related finance function.

  • Strong understanding of financial reporting, balance sheet reviews, reconciliations, and internal controls.

  • Experience coordinating with external auditors, tax authorities, and regulatory bodies.

  • Knowledge of local accounting and statutory reporting requirements within the Nordic region.

  • Proven ability to coordinate activities across multiple countries and diverse stakeholder groups.

  • Strong project coordination, communication, and organizational skills.

  • Proficiency in Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems, preferably SAP.

  • Fluent English language skills, both verbal and written.

How Would You Stand Out?

  • Experience in a multinational corporate environment with regional or global responsibilities.

  • Familiarity with Nordic tax regulations and local Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP).

  • Experience supporting statutory audits, annual financial statements, and regulatory compliance processes.

  • Continuous improvement mindset with the ability to streamline processes and enhance financial controls.

Why Choose Us?

  • Hybrid working environment with work-life balance flexibility.

  • Opportunity to support multiple Nordic markets and gain broad regional exposure.

  • Collaborative and international work environment.

  • Professional onboarding and ongoing learning opportunities.

  • Career development within a global organization.

  • Competitive total rewards package including local benefits.

For your awareness, IFF has announced its intention to sell its Food Ingredients Business to CVC Capital Partners. The sale is presently expected to close in the first half of 2027, pending regulatory approvals and other closing conditions. The Food Ingredient business unit will remain a part of IFF until close and, at such time, it will transition to CVC Capital Partners. In applying for this position, you acknowledge your awareness that the position is a part of the Food Ingredient business unit and has been identified to transition to CVC Capital Partners.

We are a global leader in taste, scent, and nutrition, offering our customers a broader range of natural solutions and accelerating our growth strategy. At IFF, we believe that your uniqueness unleashes our potential. We value the diverse mosaic of the ethnicity, national origin, race, age, sex, or veteran status. We strive for an inclusive workplace that allows each of our colleagues to bring their authentic self to work regardless of their religion, gender identity & expression, sexual orientation, or disability.

title: Investment Analyst, Infrastructure & Natural Resources
description:
The opportunity

As an Investment Analyst in the Greenfield & Renewables (“G&R”) team within the Infrastructure and Natural Resources (“INR”) group, you will have a key role in analyzing potential private equity investment opportunities, executing transactions and working with existing portfolio companies to craft strategy and implement value-enhancing initiatives.

If you are an excellent teammate, highly motivated, and have a desire to travel internationally while working on multiple projects in a fast-paced transaction-based environment – this is the job for you.

Who you’ll work with

You will be joining our Toronto office, where you will work in a dynamic team-based environment, directly supporting senior team members across all sectors and geographic regions. You will have the chance to define and differentiate yourself as an investor and build strategic relationships within the global market.

INR consists of a team of over 70 highly-specialized private equity investment professionals, with offices in Toronto, London and Singapore, and an additional presence in Santiago, Chile. INR leads a geographically diverse portfolio of approximately C$58 billion with assets in North America, South America, Europe, the Middle East, Asia, Australia and New Zealand.

Our G&R team focuses on renewable investments in development, construction, and operating stages, as well as other core and core-plus greenfield infrastructure. G&R has a global mandate, allowing for investments in all of OTPP’s target geographies. G&R’s existing portfolio covers investments in onshore and offshore wind, solar, hydrogen, battery storage, and waste-to-energy.

What you’ll do

  • Build and employ financial modeling tools to analyze investment opportunities;

  • Assist in the due diligence process and incorporate the findings into a financial model;

  • Identify key value drivers and financial risks and perform related financial sensitivity and scenario analysis;

  • Work closely with external advisors, consultants and partners to assess risks and submit bids under tight timelines;

  • Prepare presentations, reports, and investment recommendations to senior management and, where applicable, the Board of OTPP;

  • Review and analyze financial reports, budgets, board books and other information prepared by management of our portfolio companies;

  • Work with portfolio company management to build and maintain financial models that are used to analyze strategic issues and value the company;

  • Support internal strategic project initiatives, and;

  • Support the preparation of internal annual valuations.

What you’ll need

  • Minimum 1 year experience, preferably in investment banking, principal investing, or mergers & acquisitions advisory

  • Bachelor’s degree required, with the pursuit of a CFA designation considered a plus

  • Strong communication skills with the ability to influence others and comfort presenting to senior audiences

  • Excellent analytical and quantitative skills and ability to perform in-depth financial modelling analysis

  • Ability and desire to work in a vigorous, fast-paced environment, and balance multiple priorities under demanding timelines, while remaining detail oriented

  • A proactive attitude and drive to deliver value in a team of highly motivated investment professionals

  • Advanced skills in Excel and PowerPoint

  • Desire and ability to travel and work internationally

What we’re offering


Pay-for-performance with base salary and annual incentive based on individual and enterprise performance.

The Base salary for this level is $115,000 in Year 1 and $125,000 in Year 2.

Individual compensation and placement of this role in the range is based on different factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to relevant experience, skills, demonstrated competencies, and internal equity as they relate to the role.

  • Numerous opportunities for professional growth and development

  • Comprehensive employer paid benefits coverage

  • Retirement income through a defined benefit pension plan

  • The opportunity to invest back into the fund through our Deferred Incentive Program

  • A flexible work environment combining in office collaboration and remote working

  • Competitive time off

  • Our Flexible Travel Program gives you the option to work abroad in another region/country for up to a month each year

  • Employee discount programs including Edvantage and Perkopolis

We are building an inclusive and equitable workplace where our talent is respected, accepted and empowered to be themselves. title: Principal Software Engineer (Clearance Required)
description:
Sierra Space Careers:

At Sierra Space, we build the missions and systems that keep our world secure in the domain above Earth.

Sierra Space team members share a spirit of innovation and collaboration and a belief that we can deliver on the boldest missions in space today. Together with our customers, we aim to safeguard our nation, sustain human presence in space, and secure the freedom of operations in low Earth orbit and beyond.

Our success is measured by the trust of those who rely on what we build and deliver, and our technologies keep the United States and its allies mission-ready throughout space.

We are mission-driven, and together, we are an extraordinary team.

About the Role

The Principal Software Engineer role involves designing, developing, and testing software applications for space systems and technologies. This advanced position requires extensive expertise in multiple programming languages, an advanced understanding of software development principles, and the ability to design, architect, and implement complex software systems. The role includes writing clean, maintainable code, collaborating with team members to understand project requirements, and contributing to the development of innovative software solutions. Additionally, this position requires a deep understanding of software engineering processes, advanced algorithmic knowledge, and system scalability. The role also involves providing technical leadership and mentorship to other engineers.

In this role, you will plan and drive multidisciplinary system development initiatives and architect comprehensive systems that integrate multiple subsystems. You will resolve conflicting system requirements and ensure alignment with project objectives while collaborating with cross-functional teams and subject matter experts to understand project requirements and objectives. Leading the derivation, decomposition, allocation, tracing, and management of system requirements and architectures will be a key responsibility, along with defining and documenting system concepts of operation. You will plan, define, and lead development milestone reviews, oversee system integration and verification activities to ensure system functionality and performance, and identify and manage technical risks while developing mitigation strategies. Additionally, you will contribute to continuous improvement initiatives by identifying areas for enhancement and help define and implement corporate Systems Engineering policies and processes. Effective communication with team members and stakeholders will be essential to ensure project alignment and successful execution.

About You

Our mission is driven by an unyielding commitment to advancing space-based technology in service of our customers and safeguarding national security. We seek individuals who are passionate about innovating beyond boundaries and relentlessly pursuing solutions that protect, preserve and empower – to join us in this critical mission.

We’re looking for team members who align with our values, mission and goals – while also meeting the minimum qualifications below. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Requires bachelor's degree in a related field (or equivalent work experience in lieu of degree or master's +10 yrs experience).

  • Typically, 12+ years of related experience.

  • Extensive expertise in multiple programming languages and software development principles.

  • Ability to design, architect, implement, and test complex software systems.

  • Expert understanding of software engineering processes, advanced algorithmic knowledge, domain-specific design patterns, performance tuning, and system scalability.

  • Mastery in writing scalable, optimized code, ability to design complex software systems, and knowledge of best practices, including secure coding, and system architecture principles.

  • Ability to independently contribute to the design and development of software applications, conduct unit tests, and participate in code reviews.

  • Experience with different software development methodologies such as Agile and Scrum/Kanban.

  • An active Top Secret U.S. Security Clearance is required.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Advanced degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field.

  • Extensive experience with kernel-level programming.

  • Proficiency in programming languages (Python, C++, Java) and their ecosystems.

  • In-depth knowledge of scripting languages and automation tools.

  • Proven experience with software development methodologies such as Agile or Kanban/Scrum.

  • Exceptional analytical skills and meticulous attention to detail.

  • Superior communication skills and the ability to work effectively in a collaborative team environment.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead large-scale software projects from inception to completion.

  • Strong strategic thinking and decision-making skills.

  • Strong analytical skills, performance profiling, and debugging complex systems.

  • Excellent communication and teamwork skills, with experience using collaborative tools (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket).

  • Ability to write and maintain technical documentation.

  • Familiarity with SysML/UML to create software designs.

  • Experience utilizing and setting up static analysis tools.

Compensation:

Pay Range:

$184,628.00 - $253,884.50

Your actual base compensation will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on job-related knowledge and skills, education, experience, internal equity and market competitiveness.

This position requires current/active Top Secret U.S. Security Clearance. U.S. Citizenship status is required as this position needs an active U.S. Security Clearance for employment. Non-U.S. Citizens may not be eligible to obtain a security clearance. The Department of Defense Consolidated Adjudications Facility (DoD CAF), a federal government agency, handles the adjudicative aspects of the security clearance eligibility process for industry applicants. Adjudicative factors which affect the outcome of the eligibility determination include, but are not limited to, allegiance to the U.S., foreign influence, foreign preference, criminal conduct, security violations and illegal drug use.

Elevate Your Career

At Sierra Space, we are committed to your personal and professional development. We empower you to make profound and meaningful contributions and foster a vibrant culture of collaboration, where teamwork ignites breakthrough innovations.


We also offer a generous benefit package, including medical, dental, and vision plans, 401(k) with 150% match up to 6%, life insurance, 3 weeks paid time off, and more.

Sierra Space is an industry-leading space and defense technology company providing satellites, spacecraft, and enabling mission systems and components. We deliver mission-proven technologies to our customers that safeguard our nation, protect space-based assets and enable space exploration.

Application Deadline: This role will remain posted until a qualified pool of candidates is identified.

Please note: Sierra Space does not accept unsolicited resumes from contract agencies or search firms. Any unsolicited resumes submitted to our website or to Sierra Space team members not through our approved vendor list or Talent Acquisition will be considered property of Sierra Space, and we will not be obligated to pay any referral fees.

Sierra Space Corporation is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities. If you need special assistance or a reasonable accommodation related to applying for employment with Sierra Space or at any stage of the recruitment process, please contact us.

description:

We are looking for a Software Engineer to help modernize and improve our medication production software. This software controls and supports robotic systems that prepare medication. The role focuses on replacing older desktop applications with modern, easy-to-maintain web applications that run securely on our local systems.


As a Full Stack Engineer, you will:

  • Help ensure the system keeps running even when problems occur
  • Build tools to reassign work if machines or processes fail
  • Find and fix the causes of system errors
  • Create automated tests to prevent mistakes and production issues
  • Prepare releases that can be tracked, repeated, and audited
  • Write clear documentation for users, support teams, and future developers

  • 4+ years of working experience in a similar role
  • Strong experience with modern front-end web technologies (e.g. React, Angular, Blazor)
  • Strong experience with C#/.NET Core and ASP.NET for back-end API development
  • Strong experience with relational databases (MySQL, MSSQL, or MariaDB)
  • Strong experience with writing automated unit testing

Working Conditions

  • You get a lease car with a fuel card
  • Possibility of hybrid working
  • Monthly net expense allowance
  • 27 vacation days with the possibility to purchase 10 extra vacation days
  • Pension scheme without personal contribution

What we offer

  • Access to exciting projects in key sectors: Defence, Transport, Telecom, Finance
  • A diverse client base: Collaborations with both large corporations and smaller players across the Netherlands
  • A real career development plan: Continuous training, coaching, daily knowledge sharing
  • An innovative and collaborative environment

title: WARN Mental Health Advocate
description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

IRC opened an office in Seattle in 1976 and provides a continuum of services including intensive case management, employment and economic empowerment services, immigration assistance, health and wellness programming, and education support to refugee and immigrant families in Washington State. IRC Seattle is committed to providing trauma-informed, equitable, and accessible services and maintaining and evolving a diverse, inclusive, and supportive workplace.

Job Overview:

The Mental Health Advocate supports the mental health and resilience of survivors of trafficking through the WARN program, providing one-on-one peer support, referrals, and group-based services. This client-facing role includes one on one support, offering psychoeducation and skill-building workshops, and facilitating MHPSS groups. The Mental Health Advocate also coordinates program logistics, recruit participants, documents services, and supports evaluation through data collection. Additionally, they connect clients to appropriate mental health resources, assist with care coordination, and collaborate with supervisors to provide crisis support as needed.

Major Responsibilities:

Client Engagement & Support

  • Provide Psychosocial support including manualized interventions to clients. (Training in interventions will be provided.)

  • Develop individualized action plans with clearly defined goals and activities based on assessment findings.

  • With support from supervisor, provide health navigation services through referrals for clients requiring higher levels of mental health care to culturally and linguistically appropriate providers.

  • Support crisis assessment and intervention for program participants in collaboration with supervisor.

  • Represent the WARN Mental Health program at external and internal outreach events.

Program Facilitation

  • Facilitate psychosocial group programs, ensuring alignment with contract guidelines.

  • Facilitate psychoeducation and skill-building group sessions using evidence-based approaches under supervision.

  • Recruit and enroll participants for WARN programs.

  • Plan and organize logistics for WARN programs, including scheduling, transportation, materials, and space coordination.

Monitoring & Evaluation

  • Prepare and administer Participant Service Reports with guidance from supervisor.

  • Document client interactions and program activities through detailed case notes and data entry.

  • Assist in evaluating current services and identifying opportunities for new program offerings.

  • Use IRC software to document client information and other program materials.

Administrative & Team Support

  • Attend and actively participate in team meetings, staff meetings, and relevant IRC trainings and conference calls.

  • Collaborate with supervisor and team members to ensure program quality and compliance.

  • Perform other duties as assigned to support the success of WARN programming.

Key Working Relationships:

Position Reports to: MHPSS Program Manager

Indirect Reporting: Clinical Services Supervisor

Position Supervises: N/A

Other Internal and/or external contacts:

Internal: WARN Team, Family Wellness Team, Resettlement Team, Employment Team, Immigration Team, Youth Program Team, New Roots Team, Health Empowerment Team, Volunteer Coordinator, Finance Team, Operations Team, Development Team.

External: API Chaya, REST, KIND, Northwest Justice Project, Northwest Immigrant Rights Project, Seattle Police Department, US Attorney’s Office, Homeland Security Investigations, Washington Advisory Committee on Trafficking, City of Seattle Human Services Division, Washington State Office for Crime Victim Advocacy, Washington State Task Force Against Trafficking in Persons, and additional partners.

Job Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in relevant social services field (i.e., social work, human development, psychology) or equivalent professional and/or lived experience with social work, social service provision, psychosocial support, mental health, and community engagement.

  • Lived experience as a refugee or immigrant is preferred. However, in lieu of lived experience, experience working with refugees and/or immigrants; cross-cultural or overseas experience accepted.

  • Understanding of the systems that intersect with migration and resettlement.

  • Understanding of social service system.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

  • Fluency in English and Spanish or other relevant language(s)

  • Strong intercultural communication skills and demonstrated ability to work effectively with people from diverse cultural backgrounds.

  • Strong computer, keyboard, email, and general office skills.

  • Current driver’s license and valid insurance.

Working Environment:

  • Standard, professional office environment (flexible remote and in-office)

  • Access to a reliable transportation to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area

  • Position may involve evening and weekend work and travel

Compensation: (Pay Rate: $28-$31/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.


Cookies:


Benefits: IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.


Equal Opportunity Employer: IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: PGIM | Intern, Real Estate Private Equity Portfolio Management (all genders) as of Q1 2027, Based in Frankfurt
description:
A GLOBAL LEADING ASSET MANAGER WITH A DIVERSE & INCLUSIVE CULTURE

As the Global Asset Management business of Prudential, we’re always looking for ways to improve financial services. We’re passionate about making a meaningful impact - touching the lives of millions and solving financial challenges in an ever-changing world.

We also believe talent is key to achieving our vision and are intentional about building a culture on respect and collaboration. When you join PGIM, you’ll unlock a motivating and impactful career – all while growing your skills and advancing your profession at one of the world’s leading global asset managers!

Earliest start date: 18th of January, 2027

If you’re not afraid to think differently and challenge the status quo, come and be a part of a dedicated team that’s investing in your future by shaping tomorrow today.

At PGIM, You Can!

WHAT YOU WILL DO

As an intern in our pan-European Core and Core Plus Portfolio Management team, you will gain hands-on exposure to the management of institutional real estate private equity funds and portfolios across multiple countries and property sectors. Working closely with experienced portfolio managers, you will contribute to asset- and fund-level analysis, investment decisions, business planning, financing, the evaluation of potential acquisitions and disposals and investor communication.

The role provides a broad perspective across the full real estate investment lifecycle, from acquisition and underwriting through active ownership, financing and eventual disposition. You will collaborate with colleagues across Portfolio Management, Transactions, Asset Management, Investment Research, Sustainability, Fund Operations, Finance, Tax and Legal.

WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT

·Prepare asset- and fund-level cash-flow analysis, budgets and return forecasts using established financial models

·Support the review of asset business plans, including leasing and operating assumptions, capital expenditure, financing and valuation scenarios

·Contribute to hold/sell analyses and disposition planning by evaluating alternative exit timings, pricing assumptions and their impact on asset and fund-level returns and liquidity

·Support the Portfolio Management team in evaluating potential acquisitions and disposals by reviewing the investment rationale, key underwriting assumptions, downside scenarios, risks and suitability for the relevant fund or portfolio

·Analyze portfolio performance, including income and capital returns, valuation movements, leverage and the key drivers of performance relative to business plans and investment objectives

·Support financing and refinancing analyses, including debt sizing, interest costs, covenant headroom and maturity planning

·Contribute to fund-level liquidity planning, cash-flow forecasting, capital deployment and distribution analysis.

·Prepare analyses and presentation materials for portfolio reviews, investor meetings, quarterly reporting and other internal and external discussions

·Conduct market, sector and transaction research to assess portfolio positioning and support strategic investment decision

·Work with colleagues across Portfolio Management, Transactions, Asset Management, Investment Research, Sustainability, Fund Operations, Finance, Tax and Legal, while ensuring accuracy and consistency across portfolio and asset-level data

WHAT YOU WILL BRING

·Currently pursuing or recently completed a bachelor’s or master’s degree in real estate, finance, business administration, economics or a related discipline

·Previous internship or working-student experience in real estate, private equity, investment banking, corporate finance, consulting, asset management or a related field is preferred

·Strong analytical and numerical skills, with an interest in understanding the commercial drivers of real estate investments

·A foundational understanding of fundamental finance concepts such as cash flow, yield, leverage, valuation and investment returns

·Required: Strong Excel and PowerPoint skills and experience with financial modelling

·Fluency in English and German, both written and spoken

·Ability to analyze detailed information, identify key issues and communicate conclusions clearly

·High attention to detail and a reliable, structured approach to working with financial and operational data

·Curiosity, initiative and a willingness to take ownership of defined workstreams

·Ability to work effectively in an international, collaborative and deadline-driven environment

WHAT WILL SET YOU APART

·Demonstrated interest in institutional real estate investing and private markets

·Previous experience analyzing real estate cash flows, business plans or investment opportunities

·Ability to combine detailed financial analysis with commercial judgement

·Confidence in presenting analytical findings clearly and concisely

WHY YOU WANT TO JOIN US

·Gain hands-on experience within a leading global real estate investment platform, with exposure to institutional funds and portfolios across multiple European markets and property sectors.

·Work closely with experienced investment professionals and contribute to meaningful asset- and fund-level analyses from an early stage.

·Build an international network through collaboration with colleagues across European offices and specialist functions.

·Gain insight into institutional fund structures, investor requirements and decision-making processes that are rarely accessible at an early stage of a career.

·We understand that every role has its distinct requirements, so our managers treat their team as individuals, finding the way that works best for them to perform at the top of their game.

·We like to maintain an in-office culture at the centrally located workplace in the heart of Frankfurt which is accessible with S-Bahn, subway or tram.

·With us, you can broaden your expertise and experience. We offer you interesting and varied tasks in an international and multicultural working environment.

·Work is not everything! That's why we regularly organize informative office events, summer parties and Christmas parties.

·We support you in all situations! Together with partner companies as well as mental health first aiders, we offer life coaching, emergency care and individual assistance in challenging life situations.

·We are aware of our responsibility! The real estate industry is responsible for a large part of the global CO2 emissions - PGIM Real Estate has set itself ambitious goals to change something and you can make your contribution!

ABOUT PGIM REAL ESTATE

PGIM Real Estate is one of the largest Real Estate managers in the world and one of the nation’s largest full-service commercial, multi-family and agricultural real estate lenders and has been serving the commercial real estate market for over 125 years.

Through our investment, financing, asset management and talent management approach, we engage in practices that ignite positive environmental and social impact, while pursuing activities that strengthen communities around the world. When you join our team, you’ll find yourself inspired by an inclusive company culture that believes that diversity of all kinds allows us to develop better and more innovative solutions for our client.

ABOUT PGIM – GLOBAL ASSET MANAGEMENT

PGIM is the global asset management business of Prudential Financial, Inc. (NYSE: PRU), a leading global investment manager with nearly US$1.5 trillion in assets under management as of June 30th, 2026. With offices in 20 countries, PGIM’s businesses offer a range of investment solutions for retail and institutional investors around the world across a broad range of asset classes, including public fixed income, private fixed income, fundamental equity, quantitative equity, real estate and alternatives.

With a history dating back over 140 years, and experience through more than 30 market cycles, PGIM takes a long-term view, not only in our investment philosophy, but also in how we develop our talent. We want to see our employees excel from their first day with the firm and throughout their tenure with PGIM. We will inspire you, support you, and help you reach your greatest personal and professional aspirations. If PGIM sounds like the place for you, join us. For more information about PGIM, visit PGIM.com.

title: Administrative Travel officer
description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

Reporting to the Operations Administrative Manager, the Administrative Travel Officer will serve as the central focal point for travel and visa coordination for IRC Ukraine. The position will provide end-to-end support to national and international staff, covering visa and immigration support, international and cross-border travel arrangements, accommodation, ground transportation, travel-related financial and administrative follow-up, and traveller support. The role will also provide additional administrative support to the Central Administration team as required.


The position is based in Kyiv and works closely with the Operations Administrative Manager, Administrative Officer, Finance, People & Culture, Safety and Security, travellers, contracted service providers and relevant consular authorities.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES


1. Visa and Immigration Support

  • Coordinate the full cycle of Ukrainian visa support for international staff, including consular appointments, application forms, supporting documents and follow-up with relevant authorities or consulates.
  • Coordinate Schengen, Moldovan transit and other travel-related visas where required for approved routes.
  • Facilitate in-country submissions for medium- and long-term stay and/or residence permits for expatriate staff.
  • Support national staff with visas required for approved international missions, trainings and business travel.
  • Maintain accurate guidance, checklists and records relating to visa requirements and case status.

2. Travel Planning and Arrangements

  • Coordinate and, where applicable, arrange international flights, accommodation and associated travel services in accordance with IRC procedures and approved travel requests.
  • Develop and coordinate complex routes involving Ukraine, Poland, Moldova and other transit locations, including domestic connections and international onward travel.
  • Arrange or coordinate train tickets between Ukraine and Poland when travellers cannot purchase them independently, and ensure controlled transfer of original tickets or travel documents.
  • Coordinate ground transportation, including taxis and transfers in Poland, Moldova and other transit locations where operationally required.
  • Support local and cross-border travel arrangements in coordination with relevant IRC teams.

3. Financial and Administrative Follow-up

  • Coordinate travel-related invoices, supporting documentation and payment follow-up with Finance and service providers.
  • Maintain complete and auditable travel records, including approvals, itineraries, tickets, accommodation confirmations, invoices and visa documentation, as applicable.
  • Support reconciliation and resolution of booking changes, refunds, credits and additional charges.
  • Monitor recurring service issues and provide information to support vendor performance management and cost control.

4. Traveller Support and Operational Coordination

  • Provide travellers with complete itineraries, visa documentation, practical travel information and pre-departure checks.
  • Ensure travellers receive the required security information and briefings from the appropriate Safety and Security focal points before travel.
  • Monitor active travel cases and provide timely support when disruptions, missed connections, documentation issues or urgent changes arise.
  • Maintain an agreed escalation and backup arrangement for urgent travel-related issues outside normal working hours, in line with IRC working arrangements and management direction.
  • Provide regular status information and operational reporting to the Operations Administrative Manager.

5. General Administrative Support

  • Provide additional administrative support during peak workload periods, staff absences, office events and urgent operational needs.
  • Support administrative documentation, records, vendor and invoice follow-up, and other departmental coordination as assigned.
  • Provide backup coverage for agreed administrative processes to strengthen service continuity within the Central Administration team.
  • Perform other reasonable administrative duties assigned by the Operations Administrative Manager that are consistent with the position's grade and job description.

JOB REQUIREMENTS


Education:

  • Diploma or degree in Administration, Finance, Travel Management, International Relations or a related field.

Experience:

  • At least 2 years’ experience in a similar travel, visa, administrative or coordination role, preferably within a humanitarian or development organisation.
  • Demonstrated experience coordinating travel arrangements, visas, accommodation and/or related administrative processes.
  • Previous experience handling different stakeholders and coordinating activities is desirable.
  • Previous experience working in an international or multicultural environment is desirable.

Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:

  • Strong organisational and time-management skills, with a demonstrated ability to prioritise tasks and meet deadlines.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate records and documentation.
  • Ability to coordinate multiple travel and visa cases simultaneously and follow up consistently with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ability to work independently and effectively in a dynamic, cross-functional team environment.
  • Ability to work under pressure and respond appropriately to urgent travel-related issues in unstable security conditions.
  • Good understanding of working with people from different cultures.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook.
  • Personal qualities: team player, flexible, service-oriented, reliable, network-builder and able to handle pressure well.

Language Skills:

  • Fluency in Ukrainian and English, both written and spoken, is required.

REPORTING STRUCTURE AND TEAM COLLABORATION

Reports to: Operations Administrative Manager

The position works closely with the Administrative Officer and relevant Finance, People & Culture, Safety and Security and Supply Chain colleagues, as well as travellers, service providers and consular authorities.


WORK ENVIRONMENT AND OTHER RELEVANT INFORMATION

  • This position is full-time and Kyiv-based, with office-based or hybrid working arrangements in accordance with IRC policy.
  • The role requires a high level of organisation, responsiveness, multitasking and attention to detail.
  • The position may require urgent follow-up on active travel cases and coordination outside normal working hours in line with agreed IRC working arrangements and management direction.
  • Fast-paced work environment, multiple priorities and psychological pressure.
    The organization supports flexible working arrangements where operationally possible.


IRC employees are eligible to the following benefits:

  • Competitive salary
  • Purposeful job and development opportunities
  • English classes and unlimited online training courses
  • Life Insurance
  • Medical insurance for staff and family members
  • Free psychological support to employees and their family members
  • 30 calendar days of annual vacation with flexibility beyond the legally set minimum requirements
  • Up to 10 days of paid medical leave
