Gestionar el proceso de plan de demanda y el ciclo de planeación de ventas y operaciones (S&OP), generar el plan de demanda mediante la elaboración del pronóstico estadístico, colaboración y consenso del plan con el equipo comercial y marketing, proveer información para la Junta Pre-S&OP y S&OP, y la elaboración de plan operativo anual de demanda con el fin de establecer las metas anuales de Ventas y Producción.

Localización: Tultitlán, Estado de México.

Responsabilidades principales:

  • Gestionar el pronóstico estadístico anual, cuatrimestral, mensual y semanal. Análisis de tendencia, estacionalidad y limpieza de historia de facturación y pedidos mediante modelos avanzados de pronóstico y el uso de software de pronósticos.

  • Análisis de plan de demanda incorporando información y sensibilidad de mercado provista por Ventas, Inteligencia Comercial, Mercadotecnia y Atención a Clientes.

  • Incorporación de lanzamientos, promociones, campañas y proyectos, así como la estacionalidad normal al plan de demanda.

  • Evaluar que el proceso y los métodos de forecasting se sigan, analiza las tendencias a través del comportamiento histórico, detecta variaciones de la demanda hacer los ajustes necesarios para garantizar la oferta de servicio.

  • Interactuar con las áreas de ventas y MKT, facilitando información de diferentes periodos de tiempo a nivel SKU/CEDIS, SKU/CLIENTE, SKU/CANAL/CEDIS, ETC. y agregado venta, demanda, tendencia, estacionalidad, forecast de los próximos 4 a 18 meses que permitan al equipo definir estrategias alineadas al Business plan vigente.

  • Revisar las tendencias históricas de ventas, preparar escenarios de venta con impulsos para la demanda (campañas, proyectos, licitaciones, etc..), prepare datos de pronóstico, desarrolle modelos estadísticos de pronóstico y evalúe los resultados del pronóstico estadístico.

  • Participar activamente en el comité de magna carta, como producto owner, y liderar todo el proceso de seguimiento a los planes de acción definidos.

Requisitos:

  • Tener conocimiento/ nociones en sistema Forecast Pro es indispensable para el rol.

  • Experiencia en aplicación de modelos estadísticos.

  • Sólido manejo en Excel

  • Ingles deseable intermedio

  • Nivel de estudios: Universidad.

title: AI Agent Engineer
description:
At Intrum, you will grow by making a difference. You will do it in a highly international environment and in a supportive culture where effort counts.

Olisitko sinä seuraava intrumlainen?

Liiketoimintamme perusajatus on toisten auttaminen. Autamme loppuasiakkaitamme löytämään ratkaisuja talousvaikeuksiin ja asiakkaitamme tehostamaan yritystensä rahankiertoa. Toimimme terveen talouden suunnannäyttäjänä, ja juuri se tekee työstämme merkityksellistä.

AI Agent Engineer

Intrumilla IT on tärkeässä roolissa liiketoiminnan kehittämisessä. Panostamme digitalisaatioon, automaatioon ja tekoälyn hallittuun hyödyntämiseen sekä kehitämme jatkuvasti toimintatapojamme, prosessejamme ja IT-ratkaisujamme.

Haemme nyt Suomen IT-organisaatioomme AI Agent Engineeriä rakentamaan tekoälyä hyödyntäviä ratkaisuja liiketoimintamme tarpeisiin.

Hyödynnämme konsernin yhteisiä AI-alustoja ja niihin liittyviä teknologiapalveluita. Suomessa keskitymme rakentamaan niiden avulla AI-agentteja osaksi liiketoimintaprosessejamme.

Mitä pääset tekemään?

AI Agent Engineerinä osallistut kielimalleihin perustuvien agenttien suunnitteluun, rakentamiseen, testaamiseen ja jatkuvaan kehittämiseen.

Tehtävässä yhdistyvät liiketoimintaprosessien ymmärtäminen, generatiivinen tekoäly, promptaus sekä agenttien toimintalogiikan ja laadun kehittäminen. Tavoitteena on rakentaa agentteja, jotka toimivat johdonmukaisesti, laadukkaasti ja turvallisesti erilaisissa tilanteissa.

Tyypillisiä työtehtäviäsi ovat:

  • AI-agenttien suunnittelu ja rakentaminen: suunnittelet agenttien prompteja, ohjeita, keskustelurakenteita ja toimintalogiikkaa sekä toteutat niitä Intrumin käyttämillä AI-työkaluilla.

  • Liiketoimintatarpeiden muuttaminen toimiviksi agenteiksi: mallinnat liiketoiminnan tarpeita, prosesseja ja sääntöjä agenttien ohjeiksi ja toimintaperiaatteiksi.

  • Agenttien testaus ja laadun kehittäminen: testaat agenttien toimintaa, arvioit vastausten laatua, analysoit virheitä ja kehität ratkaisuja havaintojen perusteella.

  • Yhteistyö ja käyttöönotto: työskentelet liiketoiminnan asiantuntijoiden, prosessien omistajien, IT-asiantuntijoiden ja muiden AI-osaajien kanssa agenttien kehittämisessä ja käyttöönotossa.

Tehtävä tarjoaa mahdollisuuden päästä rakentamaan ratkaisuja, jotka eivät jää kokeiluiksi, vaan joiden tavoitteena on tulla konkreettiseksi osaksi liiketoiminnan päivittäistä toimintaa.

Mitä odotamme sinulta?

Etsimme uteliasta, analyyttistä ja käytännönläheistä henkilöä, jolla on kiinnostusta generatiiviseen tekoälyyn ja halua kehittyä AI-agenttien rakentamisessa. Voit hyvin olla myös työurasi alkuvaiheessa.

Tehtävä sopii henkilölle, joka on käyttänyt generatiivista tekoälyä käytännössä ja ymmärtää, miten kielimalleja voidaan ohjata, testata ja hyödyntää liiketoiminnassa. Sinun ei tarvitse osata kaikkea valmiiksi. Meille tärkeää on myös halu oppia, kokeilla ja kehittää.

Toivomme sinulta:

  • käytännön kokemusta generatiivisten AI-palveluiden tai kielimallien hyödyntämisestä

  • kiinnostusta AI-agenttien ja kielimallipohjaisten ratkaisujen rakentamiseen

  • analyyttistä ja kriittistä ajattelutapaa sekä kykyä arvioida AI tuottamien vastausten laatua

  • kiinnostusta liiketoimintaprosessien ymmärtämiseen ja digitaalisten palveluiden kehittämiseen

  • oma-aloitteisuutta, oppimishalua ja hyviä yhteistyötaitoja

  • valmiutta työskennellä suomeksi ja englanniksi kansainvälisessä ympäristössä

  • soveltuvaa korkeakoulututkintoa esimerkiksi tietojenkäsittelyn, tietotekniikan, liiketoiminnan, kieliteknologian tai muun tehtävää tukevan alan parista.

Arvostamme myös oman kiinnostuksen kautta hankittua osaamista. Kokemusta on voinut kertyä omissa AI-, chatbot- tai agenttikokeiluissa, opintojen yhteydessä tai osana nykyisiä työtehtäviä.

Katsomme eduksi

Tehtävässä on hyötyä kokemuksesta tai ymmärryksestä seuraavilla alueilla:

  • AI-agentit, chatbotit ja muut kielimallipohjaiset ratkaisut

  • promptien suunnittelu ja kielimallien vastausten arviointi

  • testitapausten ja testiaineistojen laatiminen

  • liiketoimintavaatimusten ja käyttäjätarpeiden määrittely

  • ketterä kehittäminen

  • Azure tai muu pilviosaaminen

  • ohjelmoinnin tai skriptauksen perusteet

  • rajapinnat ja tietorakenteet

  • tietoturva ja tietosuoja.

Kaikkien näiden osa-alueiden hallintaa ei edellytetä. Tärkeämpää on kiinnostus ymmärtää, miten teknologia, AI ja liiketoiminnan tarpeet voidaan yhdistää toimiviksi ratkaisuiksi.

Mitä tarjoamme?

Tarjoamme mahdollisuuden päästä mukaan rakentamaan Intrumin AI-ratkaisuja vaiheessa, jossa tekoälyä viedään konkreettiseksi osaksi liiketoiminnan toimintaa ja digitaalista kehittämistä. Pääset työskentelemään todellisten liiketoiminnan tarpeiden parissa ja näkemään, miten AI-ratkaisuja suunnitellaan, testataan, arvioidaan, otetaan käyttöön ja kehitetään hallitusti.

Saat tehtävään tukea Intrumin liiketoiminnan asiantuntijoilta, kokeneilta IT-osaajilta, tehtävän tekniseltä vastinparilta sekä konsernin kansainväliseltä AI-organisaatiolta.

Intrum tarjoaa kansainvälisen markkinajohtajan työympäristön ja mahdollisuuden tehdä merkityksellistä työtä sekä kehittää omaa osaamistasi nopeasti kehittyvällä alueella. Meillä on kannustava työkulttuuri, jossa työpanostasi arvostetaan ja pääset työskentelemään motivoituneiden kollegoiden kanssa.

Palkan lisäksi tarjoamme hyvän lounasedun sekä virike-edun, jota voit hyödyntää esimerkiksi liikuntaan, kulttuuriin, hierontaan ja hammashoitoon. Lisäksi käytössäsi ovat silmälasietu ja henkilöstöetuohjelman vaihtuvat tarjoukset.

Modernit toimitilamme sijaitsevat hyvien yhteyksien päässä Helsingin Herttoniemessä. Työskentelemme hybridimallimme mukaisesti vähintään 12 päivänä kuukaudessa toimistolla.

Työ alkaa sopimuksen mukaan mahdollisimman pian ja tehtävä on vakituinen. Käytäntömme mukaisesti tehtävään valittavalta henkilöltä tarkistetaan luottotiedot, ja luottotietoselvityksen läpäiseminen on edellytys työsuhteen solmimiselle.

Kiinnostuitko?

Lähetäthän hakemuksesi mahdollisimman pian hakujärjestelmämme kautta. Hakuaika päättyy viimeistään 29.9.2026, mutta aloitamme haastattelut jo hakuaikana ja täytämme tehtävän heti sopivan henkilön löydyttyä.

Lisätietoja tehtävästä antaa:
AI Transformation Lead Teemu Saarinen (teemu.saarinen@intrum.com), p. 050 331 4848. Tavoitat Teemun puhelimitse torstaina 17.9. ja 24.9. klo 15–16.

Do you feel that you might be the right person? Great! Apply now. Looking forward to hearing from you!

title: Contractor Special Security Representative
description:
Job Description

The Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) has an outstanding opportunity for a Contractor Special Security Representative (CSSR) to join the Security Department.

About this Opportunity:

Reporting to the Contractor Special Security Officer (CSSO), the Contractor Special Security Representative (CSSR) provides operational leadership in executing the University of Washington Applied Physics Laboratory’s Compartmented Security Program. The CSSR ensures security enables cutting‑edge classified research and advanced technology development in support of national security priorities while protecting national security information and maintaining compliance with Intelligence Community, Department of Defense, Cognizant Security Agency, and University requirements. Working under the CSSO’s direction, the CSSR administers SCI security, personnel security, classified information management, SCIF operations, and related security activities that directly support the Laboratory’s classified research mission. The role translates complex government requirements into practical, mission‑focused solutions that protect classified information while enabling scientific innovation and operational success.

The CSSR performs work requiring independent judgment, technical expertise, discretion, and operational decision‑making in a highly regulated environment where actions directly affect the Laboratory’s ability to conduct classified research. The position routinely interprets and applies IC, DoD, CSA, and University requirements across multiple security disciplines, evaluating unique situations where established guidance requires professional interpretation and sound judgment. Serving as the primary day‑to‑day security advisor to researchers, engineers, Principal Investigators, Program Managers, Information Technology personnel, Information Assurance professionals, and government representatives, the CSSR balances regulatory compliance with mission requirements, operational efficiency, and exceptional customer service while managing competing priorities and anticipating emerging operational needs.

Working with considerable independence, the CSSR coordinates closely with the CSSO on issues affecting organizational risk, regulatory compliance, SCIF readiness, and classified research operations. Through proactive problem‑solving, continuous process improvement, and consistent application of professional judgment, the CSSR contributes directly to the operational effectiveness and readiness of the University’s Compartmented Security Program. Errors in judgment, regulatory interpretation, or operational execution may delay research activities, affect personnel access, compromise classified information, or diminish government sponsor confidence. Accordingly, the position demands exceptional attention to detail, technical competence, sound judgment, and a strong commitment to operational excellence.

Key Responsibilities:

Compartmented Security Program Operations & Administration (30% FTE):

  • Execute Daily CSP Operations — Administers day‑to‑day Compartmented Security Program activities supporting classified research.
  • Implement Security Policies — Applies approved security policies, procedures, and operating practices across assigned programs.
  • Interpret Security Requirements — Translates IC, DoD, CSA, and University requirements into practical operational actions.
  • Advise Research Personnel — Serves as the primary operational security advisor to researchers, engineers, PIs, and PMs.
  • Improve Security Processes — Identifies and implements process improvements that enhance program efficiency and compliance.
  • Support CSSO Initiatives — Executes strategic and operational priorities established by the CSSO.

Personnel Security, Classified Information Management & Operational Support (25% FTE):

  • Administer Personnel Security — Processes SCI access determinations, indoctrinations, debriefings, and visit certifications.
  • Manage Classified Information — Controls receipt, storage, transmission, reproduction, inventory, and destruction of classified material.
  • Maintain Security Systems — Maintains personnel security records and government security information systems.
  • Coordinate IA/IT Activities — Aligns personnel security and classified operations with Information Assurance and IT personnel.

SCIF Operations, Physical Security & Facility Readiness (20% FTE):

  • Maintain SCIF Readiness — Ensures SCIF operational readiness, compliance, and secure daily operations.
  • Support SCIF Accreditation — Assists with accreditation actions, inspections, and facility modifications.
  • Conduct Security Inspections — Performs physical security checks, assessments, and compliance reviews.
  • Coordinate Secure Access — Manages visitor access, classified meetings, and secure facility operations.

Compliance, Risk Management & Government Coordination (15% FTE):

  • Perform Compliance Reviews — Conducts self‑inspections, compliance assessments, and regulatory evaluations.
  • Identify and Mitigate Risks — Evaluates operational risks and recommends corrective actions.
  • Coordinate with Government — Works with government security representatives during inspections and program reviews.

Security Education, Customer Partnership & Professional Excellence (10% FTE):

  • Deliver Security Training — Provides Security Education, Training, and Awareness (SETA) briefings and training.
  • Serve as Trusted Advisor — Offers timely, mission‑focused guidance enabling secure and efficient research operations.
  • Promote Professional Excellence — Reinforces a culture of professionalism, collaboration, innovation, and operational excellence.

Required Qualifications:

To be considered for this opportunity, your application must demonstrate you meet both the minimum qualifications and additional qualifications listed below. Equivalent education and/or experience may substitute for minimum qualifications except when there are legal requirements, such as a license, certification, and/or registration.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Criminal Justice, Security Management, Business Administration, Public Administration, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, or a related field, and a minimum of 4 to 6 years of progressively responsible experience administering Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI), Special Access Programs (SAP), collateral security, or comparable classified security programs.

Equivalent combinations of education, military service, and progressively responsible security experience may substitute for the degree requirement.

Additional Qualifications:

  • Experience supporting classified operations, research, engineering, advanced technology, or national security programs.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage multiple priorities while exercising sound judgment and discretion.
  • Working knowledge of Intelligence Community and DoD security requirements, including ICD 704 (personnel security), ICD 705 (SCIF standards), DoDM 5105.21 (SCI security), and 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM).
  • Familiarity with key security directives and reporting requirements, including ICDs, ICSs, ICD 705 Technical Specifications, DoDM 5105.21, and SEAD 3 for incident and foreign contact reporting.
  • Ability to apply regulatory guidance to routine security tasks, including personnel security processing, visit certifications, access verification, document control, and support to SCIF operations under CSSO direction.
  • Strong organizational, communication, and customer service skills, enabling effective coordination with program staff, visitors, and government security personnel.
  • Proficiency with government security systems, including DISS, NISS, NBIS, and standard Microsoft Office applications.
  • Active Top Secret security clearance with eligibility for Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) access.
  • Ability to maintain all required security clearances and government approvals as a condition of employment.
  • US Citizenship.

A federal security clearance is required to hold this position. The person hired into this position must be a U.S. citizen and successfully obtain and continue to maintain a Department of Defense (DOD) Personnel Security Clearance. The process for obtaining a DOD Security Clearance can be viewed using the following links: Processing Applicants (dcsa.mil) or General Investigations and Clearance Processes (dcsa.mil)

Applicants who do not meet these qualifications WILL NOT be forwarded to the Hiring Department.

Preferred Qualifications

The following qualifications enhance success in this position and support the continued maturity of the University's Compartmented Security Program.

  • Experience supporting classified research within a university, federal laboratory, Federally Funded Research and Development Center (FFRDC), University Affiliated Research Center (UARC), Intelligence Community, Department of Defense, or cleared contractor environment.
  • Experience administering integrated security disciplines, including SCI Security, Personnel Security, Classified Information Management, Physical Security, SCIF Operations, and Security Education.
  • Experience supporting SCIF planning, accreditation, inspections, operations, or lifecycle management.
  • Experience partnering with researchers, Principal Investigators, Program Managers, engineers, Information Technology professionals, and government sponsors.
  • Completion of advanced professional education through DCSA, CDSE, the Intelligence Community, the Department of Defense, or equivalent government security training programs.
  • Professional certifications related to security management, cybersecurity, project management, leadership, or organizational excellence.
  • Demonstrated commitment to operational excellence, customer service, collaboration, continuous improvement, and the philosophy that security enables research while ensuring compliance.

About APL:

The Applied Physics Laboratory is a research unit at the University of Washington. Our research expertise is in ocean physics and engineering, ocean and medical acoustics and imaging, polar science, remote sensing, and signal processing. We conduct research and development that is sponsored by a variety of federal and state agencies and take great pride in our long-standing status as a US Navy-designated University Affiliated Research Center (UARC). Our work takes place not only on the University of Washington campus and medical centers, but in field locations around the world – at sea, in the air, and on polar ice caps. We apply rigorous scientific inquiry and engineering excellence in pursuit of solutions to important problems for the good of our region, nation, and world.

We are focused on building and sustaining a laboratory where all students, staff, and collaborators can realize success. We believe every member of our team enriches our research enterprise by exposing us to a broad range of ways to understand and engage with the world, identify challenges, and discover, design, and deliver solutions. We invite you to explore our laboratory, to find answers to Common Questions about the University’s application process, and to See Yourself at APL.

title: Senior Software Engineer: Data Infrastructure
description:
About Flexport:

Ligt uw cv klaar? Zo ja, en bent u ervan overtuigd dat dit de functie voor u is, zorg er dan voor dat u zo snel mogelijk solliciteert.

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.


The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.


The opportunity

Global trade runs on data. Every shipment, every customs clearance, every delivery depends on the right information flowing through the right systems at the right time. At Flexport, data infrastructure is the foundation that enables billions of dollars in global commerce.


We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer, Backend who will take end-to-end ownership of the data systems that power Flexport's global trade platform. In this role, you'll own critical data pipelines and architecture that process millions of supply chain events daily, ensuring that our customers have real-time visibility into their shipments across the world.


As a Senior Software Engineer focused on Data Infrastructure and Backend development, you'll have deep technical ownership over the systems that ingest, process, store, and deliver data across Flexport. You'll architect solutions that handle the complexity of global trade, from tracking containers across oceans to coordinating multi-modal logistics, all while ensuring our data infrastructure scales reliably as we grow.


You will

  • Build strong relationships with producers and consumers of data across the organization.
  • Partner with other engineers on the infrastructure team to continuously improve existing systems and processes.
  • Design, build, and maintain data infrastructure systems such as distributed compute, data orchestration, distributed storage, streaming infrastructure while ensuring scalability, reliability, and security.
  • Create a culture of transparency, information sharing, and collaboration through the development of excellent documentation, mentoring of junior team members, and living Flexport’s values.
  • Participate in an on call rotation to respond to critical incidents.

You should have

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or related field.
  • 2+ years of data infrastructure engineering experience AND
  • 2+ years of experience in either

    • infrastructure engineering experience supporting product development and engineering teams in a fast-paced global environment OR
    • software development experience building tools in languages such as Java, Ruby, Go, or Python.


  • Experience with common data pipelines such as Kafka, or Kinesis.
  • Experience with common cloud data warehousing solutions such as Snowflake, BigQuery, AWS RDS/Redshift, or DataBricks.
  • Familiarity with developer tools including source code and artifacts management, CI/CD pipelines, and configuration automation with Infrastructure as Code (CloudFormation, Terraform, etc)
  • Experience with IaaS cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, containers, and service-oriented architectures.
  • Excellence in problem-solving, strategic thinking, and collaboration with cross-functional teams.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to connect with empathy when delivering constructive feedback regarding infrastructure matters to engineers and product designers.

title: Project Manager, Cardiac Solutions
description:
Join Clario, a part of Thermo Fisher Scientific and help drive the successful delivery of cardiac safety solutions that support clinical trials around the world. As a Project Manager within our Cardiac Solutions team, you will lead cross-functional project teams through the execution of global clinical studies, ensuring high-quality delivery, exceptional customer service, and adherence to project timelines and budgets. You will serve as a trusted partner to sponsors and internal stakeholders, helping bring life-changing therapies to patients faster through operational excellence and strong project leadership.

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation and incentives.

  • Engaging employee events and hybrid work technology support.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Lead the planning, setup, monitoring, and closeout phases of cardiac safety studies and programs.

  • Gather customer requirements and translate study needs into actionable plans for cross-functional operational teams.

  • Develop, maintain, and manage study documentation throughout the project lifecycle.

  • Coordinate the distribution, tracking, reconciliation, and management of study equipment and related materials.

  • Create, review, and distribute study status reports, project metrics, and client communications.

  • Ensure appropriate archival of study data, documentation, and project records in accordance with company and regulatory requirements.

  • Establish, manage, and fulfill customer expectations through proactive communication and stakeholder engagement.

  • Monitor study timelines, milestones, and deliverables to ensure successful project execution.

  • Manage financial aspects of assigned studies, including budget reviews, revenue forecasting, scope change assessments, and invoice reconciliation activities.

  • Identify project risks, develop mitigation strategies, and escalate issues appropriately to support study success.

  • Facilitate collaboration between sponsors, vendors, and internal teams to optimize resources, maximize efficiency, and achieve contractual commitments.

  • Lead internal and external discussions and negotiations to support successful study execution and customer satisfaction.

  • Apply structured problem-solving methodologies to address customer concerns, operational challenges, and project escalations.

  • Maintain issue tracking documentation and ensure timely follow-up and resolution of project-related concerns.

  • Present Cardiac Solutions services and operational workflows during investigator meetings, site initiation meetings, and client presentations as required.

  • Participate in business development meetings and support customer discussions regarding operational processes and service delivery.

  • Assist in onboarding, mentoring, and training new Project Management team members.

  • Contribute to departmental initiatives, process improvements, and special projects as assigned.

What We Look For

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant project management experience.

  • 1 to 4 years of project management experience within pharmaceutical, biotechnology, healthcare, clinical research, life sciences, medical device, or related industries.

  • Understanding of the drug development process and clinical trial environment.

  • Experience supporting cardiac safety studies, clinical technology solutions, eClinical platforms, or related clinical research services is preferred.

  • Strong project planning, organizational, prioritization, and time management skills.

  • Experience coordinating multiple stakeholders, timelines, budgets, and deliverables simultaneously.

  • Knowledge of project financial management concepts, including budgeting, forecasting, invoicing, and scope management.

  • Strong risk management and problem-solving abilities with a proactive approach to issue resolution.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively in English.

  • Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build productive relationships with sponsors, sites, vendors, and cross-functional teams.

  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook, and Teams.

  • Detail-oriented with demonstrated responsiveness to customer inquiries and operational requests.

  • Clario Project Management Certification required as applicable to the line of business.

  • Valid passport and willingness to travel internationally up to approximately 20% as business needs require.

At Clario, a part of Thermo Fisher Scientific, our purpose is to transform lives by unlocking better evidence. It’s a cause that unites and inspires us. It’s why we come to work and how we empower our people to make a positive impact every day. Whether you're advancing clinical science, building innovative technology, or supporting our global teams, your work helps bring life-changing therapies to patients faster.

title: Senior Account Representative, SMB (North)
description:
The Company

PayPal has been revolutionizing commerce globally for more than 25 years. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy.

We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We help merchants and consumers connect, transact, and complete payments, whether they are online or in person. PayPal is more than a connection to third-party payment networks. We provide proprietary payment solutions accepted by merchants that enable the completion of payments on our platform on behalf of our customers.

We offer our customers the flexibility to use their accounts to purchase and receive payments for goods and services, as well as the ability to transfer and withdraw funds. We enable consumers to exchange funds more safely with merchants using a variety of funding sources, which may include a bank account, a PayPal or Venmo account balance, PayPal and Venmo branded credit products, a credit card, a debit card, certain cryptocurrencies, or other stored value products such as gift cards, and eligible credit card rewards. Our PayPal, Venmo, and Xoom products also make it safer and simpler for friends and family to transfer funds to each other. We offer merchants an end-to-end payments solution that provides authorization and settlement capabilities, as well as instant access to funds and payouts. We also help merchants connect with their customers, process exchanges and returns, and manage risk. We enable consumers to engage in cross-border shopping and merchants to extend their global reach while reducing the complexity and friction involved in enabling cross-border trade.

Our beliefs are the foundation for how we conduct business every day. We live each day guided by our core values of Inclusion, Innovation, Collaboration, and Wellness. Together, our values ensure that we work together as one global team with our customers at the center of everything we do – and they push us to ensure we take care of ourselves, each other, and our communities.

Job Summary:

As PayPal continues its mission to revolutionize commerce, we’re looking for a driven Senior Account Representative to join our Small and Medium Business Sales team in Germany.

Small businesses are the engine of local economies everywhere, and PayPal’s SMB team helps them compete on a bigger stage. In this role, you’ll own the end-to-end commercial relationships for a portfolio of around 80 of our higher-value SMB merchants.

You’ll proactively identify opportunities to deepen relationships, expand product adoption and solve merchant needs to protect and grow transaction margin. It’s a role for someone who wants real ownership, from spotting the next growth opportunity to working through merchant problems that don’t yet have a playbook.

This is a virtual position, with our German headquarters located in Berlin.

Job Description:

Essential Responsibilities:

  • Collaborate internally to influence process quality and efficiency.
  • Determine appropriate actions and consider alternative solutions.
  • Acquire, manage, and expand relationships with small and medium-sized merchants.
  • Use analytical skills and judgment to recommend best solutions.
  • Influence through defined processes and procedures.

  • 3+ years relevant experience and a Bachelor’s degree OR Any equivalent combination of education and experience.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the commercial relationship with your merchants, working closely with colleagues across PayPal to deliver strong end-to-end outcomes.
  • Develop tailored account plans and commercial strategies for these strategically important merchants.
  • Use AI-powered tools to identify growth, cross-sell and risk signals across your portfolio.
  • Keep pipeline, forecast and portfolio health reporting accurate, and support less experienced AM colleagues by sharing what works.
  • Bring together the right internal teams to resolve merchant needs and work through ambiguous issues where no established playbook exists.
What We’re Looking For
  • A track record of owning high-value or strategic customer relationships and the commercial outcomes that come with them.
  • Quantifiable examples of retaining and growing a complex book of business through cross-sell, upsell or wallet-share growth.
  • Comfortable using AI and commercial data to prioritise opportunities, focus your time and intervene early where there is a risk of churn or decline.
  • A problem-solver who can work beyond standard playbooks, weigh alternatives and reach commercially sound outcomes on ambiguous merchant issues.
  • A strong internal collaborator who can mobilise partners across the business, maintain clear account plans and forecasts, and reliably close out actions.
What You’ll Bring
  • 5+ years of relevant experience and a Bachelor’s degree, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
We Believe in You
Interested? Don’t hesitate to apply or reach out and let's talk —we’d love to get to know you!

PayPal

That’s why we offer comprehensive, choice-based programs, to support all aspects of personal wellbeing—physical, emotional, and financial—delivering meaningful value where it matters most. title: Senior Technical Program Manager, GTM AI Tech, Google Cloud

You’ll work with stakeholders to plan requirements, identify risks, manage project schedules, and communicate clearly with cross-functional partners across the company. You're equally comfortable explaining your team's analyses and recommendations to executives as you are discussing the technical tradeoffs in product development with engineers.

In this role, you'll lead strategic technical programs for the Forward Deployed Engineering organization, owning the operating cadence that turns executive priorities into structured, measurable execution. You'll engage with various stakeholders: Engineering, Product, field sales, account teams, and customer technical leadership, bridging the gap between customer expectations and engineering capacity. The position offers significant exposure to the business at an executive level and requires the credibility to hold executive stakeholders to their commitments.

It's an exciting time to join Google Cloud’s Go-To-Market team, leading the AI revolution for businesses worldwide. You’ll excel by leveraging Google's brand credibility—a legacy built on inventing foundational technologies and proven at scale. We’ll provide you with the world's most advanced AI portfolio, including frontier Gemini models, and the complete Vertex AI platform, helping you to solve business problems. We’re a collaborative culture providing direct access to DeepMind's engineering and research minds, empowering you to solve customer challenges. Join us to be the catalyst for our mission, drive customer success, and define the new cloud era—the market is yours.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $240000 - $333000 (USD) + 25% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google.
  • Manage programs with deep technical and product understanding, applying rigorous program management to complex AI contexts. Leverage technical knowledge to identify efficiencies and provide thought leadership.

title: Spectrum Radio Frequency Engineer
description:
Leidos’ NISC IV program seeks a Spectrum Radio Frequency Engineer to support the FAA Spectrum Engineering Services Group.

The Spectrum Engineering Group is responsible for securing, managing, and protecting all civil aviation spectrum resources to ensure interference-free operation of FAA communications, navigation, and surveillance (CNS) systems across the National Airspace System (NAS).

The ideal candidate will have an electrical engineering degree or other training and at least 2 years of spectrum engineering and/or radio frequency engineering experience. This role performs engineering and coordinating of frequency assignment actions for primary surveillance radar systems, air-to-ground voice communication, Land mobile radio, microwave, satellite, and various other Radio Frequency (RF) Spectrum Engineering disciplines while ensuring compliance with FAA Order 6050.32 and NTIA Redbook requirements.

*Must be commutable to the Washington DC area.

*While the position itself is hybrid/remote (most of the time) – the candidate will be expected to go into the office in DC on an as needed basis to access SCIF.

Core Responsibilities (All Bands):

  • Contributes to the planning, coordination, and execution of FAA and non-FAA frequency assignment actions, ensuring that technical analyses and documentation conform to FAA Orders, the NTIA Manual (Redbook), and established engineering standards.

  • Perform radio-frequency compatibility analyses using the FAA’s spectrum-automation and modeling tools to identify and mitigate potential interference among communications, navigation, and surveillance systems.

  • Conduct RF propagation, link-budget, EMC, and interference analyses using FAA spectrum-automation and modeling tools.

  • Validate all technical data (location, equipment, parameters, emission designator, power, bandwidth, and antenna characteristics) for completeness and accuracy.

  • Collaborates closely with other federal and contractor engineers, Service Area Spectrum Offices, and FAA program offices to resolve technical issues and advance records through the assignment and coordination process.

Basic Qualifications:

This individual contributor position works under general direction, and within broad authority limits, to provide technical oversight of complex, high-exposure commercial Workers’ Compensation claims handled by Third-Party Administrators (TPAs). While not responsible for people management, the role functions as a subject matter leader, influencing claim outcomes through expertise, collaboration, and oversight.



The position is responsible for reviewing and guiding claim strategies, reserves, and resolution plans to ensure alignment with company protocols, regulatory requirements, and best practices. Success in this role requires the ability to lead through influence by setting expectations, partnering effectively with TPAs, clients, and internal stakeholders, and driving accountability for quality, compliance, and performance through consultative engagement and clear communication. The role may support designated accounts and requires regular interaction with internal and external partners to achieve optimal claim outcomes and customer service standards.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities
Performs a combination of duties in accordance with departmental guidelines:

  • Manages highly complex investigations of claims, including coverage issues, liability, compensability and damages. Determines if a major claim should be settled or litigated and implements an appropriate resolution strategy accordingly. Effectively manages loss costs and claim expenses.

  • Manages all types of investigative activity or litigation on major claims, including the posting of appropriate reserves in a timely manner. Coordinates discovery and litigation strategy with staff counsel or panel attorneys.

  • Negotiates highly complex settlement packages, and authorizes payment within scope of authority, settling claims in most cost effective manner and ensuring timely issuance of disbursements.

  • Coordinates third party recovery with subrogation/salvage unit.

  • Makes recommendations on claims processes and resolution strategies to management.

  • Analyzes claims activities; prepares and presents reports to management and other internal business partners and clients.

  • Works with attorneys, account representatives, agents, doctors and insureds regarding the handling and/or disposition of highly complex claims.

  • Keeps current on state/territory regulations and issues, industry activity and trends. May participate in industry trade groups.

  • Provides guidance and assistance to less experienced claims staff and other functional areas.

  • Responsible for input of data that accurately reflects claim circumstances and other information important to our business outcomes.

Reporting Relationship
Manager or above.

Skills, Knowledge and Abilities

  • Advanced technical and product specific expertise, claims resolution skill and knowledge of insurance and claims principles, practices and procedures.

  • Strong communication, negotiation and presentation skills. Ability to effectively interact with all levels of CNA's internal and external business partners.

  • Advanced analytical and problem solving skills, with the ability to manage and prioritize multiple projects.

  • Ability to deal with ambiguous situations and issues.

  • Creativity in resolving unique and challenging business problems.

  • Knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite and other business-related software.

title: Systems Engineer II
description:
Sierra Space Careers:

At Sierra Space, we build the missions and systems that keep our world secure in the domain above Earth.

Sierra Space team members share a spirit of innovation and collaboration and a belief that we can deliver on the boldest missions in space today. Together with our customers, we aim to safeguard our nation, sustain human presence in space, and secure the freedom of operations in low Earth orbit and beyond.

Our success is measured by the trust of those who rely on what we build and deliver, and our technologies keep the United States and its allies mission-ready throughout space.

We are mission-driven, and together, we are an extraordinary team.

About the Role

The Systems Engineer II contributes to the development and implementation of advanced system solutions by providing alignment, connection and direction to the technical team throughout the product development lifecycle. The Systems Engineer II represents the viewpoint of the integrated whole during system development and works to glue segments and subsystems together via top-down decomposition of stakeholder requirements, traceability through development artifacts, and bottom-up validation and verification of the system. They help to shepherd the team through technical development milestones, track performance measures and identify technical risks to arrive at a compliant and cohesive system solution. The Systems Engineer II should have a firm grasp on Systems Engineering principles as they build expertise on specific systems engineering skills such as requirements management, system architecture development, concept of operation definition, system integration and system verification.

In this role, you will specify, architect, and integrate complex system solutions while collaborating with cross-functional teams to understand project requirements and objectives. You will derive, decompose, allocate, trace, and manage system requirements and architectures, as well as define and document system concepts of operation. Supporting development milestone reviews by creating artifacts and deliverables will be a key responsibility, alongside participating in system integration and verification activities to ensure system functionality and performance. You will identify and manage technical risks, develop mitigation strategies, and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives by identifying areas for enhancement. Adhering to established engineering processes and standards will be essential, and you will communicate effectively with team members and stakeholders to ensure project alignment and successful execution.

About You

Our mission is driven by an unyielding commitment to advancing space-based technology in service of our customers and safeguarding national security. We seek individuals who are passionate about innovating beyond boundaries and relentlessly pursuing solutions that protect, preserve and empower – to join us in this critical mission.

We’re looking for team members who align with our values, mission and goals – while also meeting the minimum qualifications below. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Requires Bachelor's degree in a related field (or equivalent work experience in lieu of degree).
  • Typically 2+ years of related experience.
  • Practical understanding of Systems Engineering principles and practices, including a basic understanding of the systems development lifecycle.
  • Conceptual knowledge of requirements management, functional requirements parsing, derivation, and allocation.
  • Conceptual knowledge of systems architecture, systems integration, and Verification and Validation (V&V) principles.
  • Clear verbal and written communication of technical concepts and information.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master's degree in Engineering, Physics, or a related field.
  • Experience with Requirements Management and Model Based Systems Engineering tools and frameworks, such as DOORS, CAMEO EA, Rhapsody, Matlab, and SysML.
  • Basic understanding of spacecraft systems, including hardware and software subsystems and components.
  • Familiarity with project management methodologies including risk management and technical performance tracking.
  • Familiarity with technical baseline and configuration management.
  • Experience or certification in INCOSE standards.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to adapt to a fast-paced and dynamic work environment.
  • Participated in 2026 SS Intern Academy.

$94,090.00 - $129,394.75

Your actual base compensation will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on job-related knowledge and skills, education, experience, internal equity and market competitiveness.

Elevate Your Career

At Sierra Space, we are committed to your personal and professional development. We empower you to make profound and meaningful contributions and foster a vibrant culture of collaboration, where teamwork ignites breakthrough innovations.


We also offer a generous benefit package, including medical, dental, and vision plans, 401(k) with 150% match up to 6%, life insurance, 3 weeks paid time off, and more.

title: Corporate Affairs Graduate
description:
Salary: £33,000, Permanent role.
Start date: September 2027

Location: Based within the Anglian Water area, with periodic travel to Huntingdon and London. Please note your placements and final role may vary across the region and departments, so flexibility is essential.

Help shape the future of water, the environment and the communities we serve

With a plan worth over £11 billion of investment, we're building for better — for you, for the communities we serve, for our environment. As part of this we are looking for you to join Anglian Water's Graduate Programme and tackle some of the biggest environmental and infrastructure challenges facing the region. From climate resilience and major engineering projects to digital innovation and customer experience, you'll develop the skills, experience and support needed to become one of our future leaders or specialists.

Your career path

The water industry is changing rapidly, creating exciting opportunities for the next generation of talent. At Anglian Water, you'll work on real challenges that matter, developing expertise across your chosen profession while contributing to projects that support customers, communities and the environment.

You'll learn from experienced colleagues, take on meaningful responsibility and build the skills, knowledge and confidence to shape your future career, while helping us shape the future of water.

To find out more from our recent graduates please visit our Anglian Water careers page: Graduates - Anglian Water Careers.

Professional Development & Memberships

We're committed to helping you build a career, not just gain a job. Through our two-year graduate programme, you'll experience different placements, work on real business challenges and learn from experienced colleagues across the organisation. You'll have access to a wide range of development opportunities, support towards professional qualifications and funded membership of a relevant professional institution, helping you grow your expertise and achieve professional accreditation where appropriate.

Your programme

You will work within the Policy and Public Affairs teams as part of the Corporate Affairs directorate. Responsibilities will vary but are likely to include:

  • Policy and political research and insight. Monitoring and summarising parliamentary activity, government announcements and wider policy developments.

  • Drafting internal briefings and external engagement documents. For example, updates on political and policy announcements, responses to government and parliamentary consultations.

  • Stakeholder engagement support. Assisting with the preparation and follow‑up for meetings, for example by researching MPs’ interests, or drafting key messages.

We are looking for people who are curious, ambitious and ready to learn. Individuals who enjoy solving problems, working collaboratively and bringing different perspectives to the challenges we face. Most importantly, we're looking for graduates who want to help shape the future of water while developing a successful and rewarding career of their own. We welcome applicants who are excited about technology products and passionate about the water industry.

For this role, you’ll need to have obtained in the last 3 years or be studying towards a minimum 2:2 in any degree discipline and have graduated by September 2027 for the 2027 intake.

Benefits

Alongside a competitive salary, you'll receive a comprehensive health and wellbeing package, private healthcare, 26 days' annual leave plus bank holidays, and a double-matched pension scheme with up to 21% total contribution. We also offer an excellent family leave package, including enhanced maternity, paternity and shared parental leave, helping you balance your career with the moments that matter most.

Assessment Centres (in Person): Monday 9th November in Huntingdon

description:
Looking for an opportunity to make an impact?

Leidos Defense Sector provides a diverse portfolio of systems, solutions, and services covering land, sea, air, space, and cyberspace for customers worldwide. Solutions for Defense include enterprise and mission command and control, and data analytics, cybersecurity, logistics, training, and operations support. Our team is solving the world’s toughest security challenges for customers with “can’t fail” missions. To explore and learn more, click here!

Are you ready to make an impact? Begin your journey of a flourishing and meaningful career, share your resume with us today!

The Defense Sector of Leidos is seeking a Senior Subcontracts Specialist to support our ever-growing Business Areas. We are seeking a motivated self-starter who can work independently and as part of a team in a dynamic environment. Under limited supervision, the Senior Subcontracts Specialist is responsible for activities that span the entire procurement cycle, including but not limited to negotiation of non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) and teaming agreements, preparation of solicitation packages to subcontractors, evaluation of subcontractor proposals, price analysis, negotiation of terms and conditions, subcontract administration, issue resolution, and closeout activities. Subcontracts will primarily be in support of federal programs. This role will require close collaboration with other functions, such as, but not limited to: Contracts, Program Management, Finance, Accounting, Engineering, Manufacturing, Growth and Business Development to ensure the successful execution of the assigned portfolio.

Primary Responsibilities

  • The position requires great business acumen and the demonstration of sound judgement with a high level of ethics
  • Creates moderate to complex RFP solicitations in accordance with Government and Leidos requirements.
  • Negotiates NDA’s and Teaming Agreements
  • Evaluates supplier proposal responses.
  • Conducts price and cost analysis.
  • Negotiates pricing and terms/conditions with subcontractors.
  • Administers subcontracts of various types and complexity
  • Identifies and resolves moderate issues and problems on assigned subcontracts and make recommendations to management
  • Performs subcontract close-out activities.
  • Thorough knowledge of federal subcontracting and experience providing creative solutions to business and program requirements, while ensuring compliance with all prime customer requirements and commitments
  • Lead negotiations and execution of strategic long-term agreements with key suppliers to support supply continuity, affordability, innovation, and long-term procurement savings
  • Collaborate with Contracts, Supply Chain, Business Development, Program Management, Engineering, Manufacturing, Finance, and other stakeholders to integrate supplier strategies early in capture, proposal, and program lifecycles
  • Identify and mitigate complex issues or risks for the managed subcontract portfolio
  • Translate supplier data into executive-ready insights, recommendations, and action plans that enable measurable savings, stronger supplier performance, improved compliance, and reduced Sector risk

Basic Qualifications

  • Requires a Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience and 4+ years or prior relevant experience or Master’s degree with 2+ years of prior relevant experience. Generally, has 2+ years of experience supervising or leading teams or projects. Equivalent experience may be considered in-lieu of a degree.
  • Experience awarding and managing subcontracts in a government approved purchasing system (CPSR) including an advanced knowledge of the requirements of the FAR/DFARS, other Federal agency requirements and small business participation.
  • Successful background of using negotiating skills to maximize organizational return, minimize risk, improve price, and terms and conditions position
  • Successful track record of managing a variety of subcontract types, interfacing with internal customers, other functional support staff, and suppliers
  • Experience independently leading the subcontracts portion of proposal efforts
  • Must have the organizational skills to manage concurrent projects and possess the business acumen to appropriately prioritize actions and deal effectively with subcontract management issues of varying degrees of complexity
  • Must be able to clearly communicate, including presenting status updates and issues to senior management, internal partners, and suppliers
  • Able to obtain and maintain a US DoW security clearance.
  • Must be a US citizen

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting Department of Defense and Federal programs, programs of record, capture pursuits, proposal development for large government acquisitions in the Defense/Aerospace industry.
  • Working knowledge of CPSR compliance, NIST SP 800-171, and cyber/supplier readiness requirements.
  • Knowledge of Lean, Six Sigma, or similar process improvement methodologies.
  • CPSM, CPC, CFCM, ISM, APICS, PMI PMP, or other relevant professional certification.
  • Experience working with RF, electronic warfare, missile, radar, SATCOM, aviation, space, manufacturing, or advanced defense technology supply chains.
  • Experience building strong supplier relationships that can be leveraged to assist in future issue resolution
  • Experience supervising or leading a team(s)
  • Working experience with ERP systems, ideally Deltek Costpoint and other procurement systems (ex. ivalua)

title: Staff Engineer - NVE PE
description:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all.

Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

As a Staff Engineer in the Non-Volatile Engineering (NVE) Product Engineering organization at Micron Technology, Inc., you will support NAND and NAND-based system product development to enable world-class end products. You will be responsible for enabling New Product Introduction with seamless and issue-free release to both internal and external non-volatile system customers. In this role, you will help establish the infrastructure, tools, and engineering practices needed to accelerate NAND development learning cycles and achieve best-in-class cycle time from first silicon to qualified system. This includes leveraging AI-enabled engineering workflows, advanced analytics, and automation solutions to improve development efficiency, accelerate debug and failure analysis, and drive data-driven decision making. Additionally, you will work closely with various Engineering and Development groups to prioritize work, apply innovative technologies including AI-assisted tools where appropriate, and ensure necessary actions are taken to meet specific product requirements. If you want a career that is meaningful, challenging, and offers the opportunity to work with a phenomenal team at the forefront of semiconductor innovation and AI-enabled engineering practices, STPG NAND Product Engineering may be a good fit for you.

Responsibilities include, but not limited to:

  • Partner with NAND Technology Development, NAND Design, NAND Product Development, and System Development teams to enable successful product development and qualification.
  • Set up infrastructure, automation frameworks, and AI-enabled workflows to support system-level evaluation of NAND during the NAND development phase.
  • Support controller-based NAND testing, validation, and failure analysis, leveraging advanced analytics and AI-assisted tools where applicable to accelerate root-cause detection and debug.
  • Responsible for Component NAND device qualification.
  • Drive failure analysis efforts from system level to NAND level and provide actionable, data-driven feedback to related teams.
  • Perform detailed electrical and physical failure analysis and work with cross-functional organizations to resolve SSD, Embedded NAND, and Component NAND related issues.
  • Troubleshoot customer-return failures and develop effective corrective actions and solutions.
  • Develop and implement automation, scripting, and AI-assisted engineering solutions to improve productivity, reduce development cycle time, and enhance product quality.
  • Leverage data analytics, machine learning, and AI-enabled methodologies to derive insights from validation, reliability, and manufacturing data and support informed engineering decisions.
  • Champion AI-enabled ways of working by identifying opportunities to apply automation, advanced analytics, and generative AI tools to accelerate product development, improve engineering effectiveness, and drive continuous improvement across the organization.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of related experience.
  • Effective communication skills in written and spoken English.
  • Understanding of all classes of NAND system products.
  • Experience with advanced NAND flash and non-volatile storage technologies.
  • Meaningful experience with computer hardware; knowledge of storage interfaces such as SATA and SAS is an advantage.
  • Proficiency in programming languages such as C, C++, Python, Perl, or equivalent.
  • Familiarity with AI-assisted development tools, automation frameworks, data analytics platforms, or other AI-enabled engineering solutions is highly desirable.

title: AVP Corporate Security & Safety
description:
You have a clear vision of where your career can go. And we have the leadership to help you get there. At CNA, we strive to create a culture in which people know they matter and are part of something important, ensuring the abilities of all employees are used to their fullest potential.

The Assistant Vice President, Corporate Security and Safety, leads an integrated, enterprise-wide program that protects the organization’s people, facilities, operations, executives, and reputation. This executive brings a proactive, intelligence-informed approach to physical security, personnel safety, workplace violence, travel, and crisis-related risks across corporate, field, and remote work environments.

Working closely with leaders in Human Resources, Employee Relations, Legal, Corporate Investigations, Risk Management, Facilities, Technology, and business operations, the AVP translates emerging threats and operational realities into practical strategies, clear policies, and effective response capabilities. The role serves as a trusted advisor to senior leadership, balancing strategic program leadership with visible, hands-on accountability for security and safety outcomes.

JOB DESCRIPTION:

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Security and Safety Leadership

  • Develop, implement, and continuously improve a risk-based corporate security and safety strategy aligned with the organization’s business objectives, culture, and risk tolerance.

  • Lead the assessment and mitigation of threats to employees, executives, visitors, facilities, operations, and brand reputation across domestic and international locations, as applicable.

  • Establish security and safety governance, policies, standards, performance measures, and reporting that provide senior leaders with meaningful visibility into risk, incidents, program maturity, and emerging issues.

  • Partner across the enterprise to ensure security and safety considerations are embedded in business planning, workplace design, operating decisions, and crisis preparedness.

Threat Management and Protective Services

  • Lead the organization’s workplace violence prevention and threat-management program in partnership with Employee Relations, Human Resources, Legal, Corporate Investigations, and other key stakeholders.

  • Direct the evaluation, escalation, and management of threats involving employees, facilities, executives, and company events, including remote and field-based work environments.

  • Assess executive-protection requirements and direct appropriate protective measures for senior leaders, including the CEO, based on risk, business need, and organizational protocol.

  • Oversee security support for business travel, corporate aviation, high-profile events, and other activities requiring enhanced protective planning.

  • Maintain productive external relationships with governmental agencies and relevant private-sector counterparts.

Operations, Technology, and Intelligence Analysis

  • Provide strategic and operational oversight of physical security systems and technologies, including access control, video surveillance, intrusion detection, visitor management, alarm monitoring, and related protective systems.

  • Direct security operations, incident response, investigations, vendor performance, and service-provider relationships to ensure consistent and effective protection across the organization.

  • Build and lead an intelligence-led, predictive approach to emerging workplace and enterprise risk, positioning the function at the forefront of evolving threats to employees, executives, facilities, travel, and business operations, and translating domestic and international intelligence into proactive prevention rather than reactive response.

  • Advance the effective use of technology, data, and analytics to strengthen situational awareness, incident management, investigations, and decision-making.

  • Partner with Technology and Information Security leaders on converged risks, including insider threat, information-related aspects of physical security incidents, and technology-enabled threats, while respecting clear ownership boundaries.

Safety, Emergency Preparedness, and Resilience

  • Lead the organization’s life-safety and emergency-management programs, and partner with enterprise crisis-management leadership to support crisis-preparedness efforts, ensuring that plans are current, scalable, tested, and aligned with operational needs.

  • Contribute security and safety expertise to the development, maintenance, and execution of the Crisis Management Plan, and serve as an active member of the Crisis Management Response Team in support of enterprise crisis-management leadership.

  • Direct emergency exercises, tabletop simulations, drills, training, and after-action reviews to strengthen organizational readiness and continuous improvement.

  • Partner with Facilities, Human Resources, Risk Management, and business leaders to identify and address workplace safety hazards, ergonomics concerns, regulatory requirements, and other employee-safety issues.

  • Support business continuity and resilience planning by ensuring security and safety risks are incorporated into response and recovery strategies.

Talent, Financial, and Stakeholder Leadership

  • Lead, develop, and retain a high-performing security and safety team; establish clear expectations, build bench strength, and promote succession planning for critical roles.

  • Create a culture of prevention, accountability, service, sound judgment, and continuous learning across the security and safety function.

  • Manage departmental budgets, external-provider expenditures, capital investments, and resource allocation to deliver measurable value and appropriate risk reduction.

  • Prepare and present concise, decision-oriented reports on security and safety metrics, incidents, trends, strategic initiatives, and resource needs to senior leadership.

  • Represent the organization with professionalism, discretion, integrity, and sound judgment during routine operations and high-consequence events.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in security management, criminal justice, risk management, business, safety, emergency management, or a related discipline; advanced degree preferred

  • A demonstrated commitment to continued professional education and development, staying current with the evolving security, technology, and regulatory landscape relevant to the organization’s industry and global footprint.

  • Ten or more years of progressively responsible corporate security, safety, law-enforcement, public-sector security, risk-management, or related experience, including significant leadership responsibility.

  • At least five years of experience leading security, safety, or protective-services teams, programs, budgets, and external vendors.

  • Demonstrated experience leading workplace violence prevention and threat-management efforts, physical-security operations, emergency preparedness, crisis response, and executive or travel security.

  • Experience operating in a complex, multi-site, matrixed organization; experience supporting a national or global enterprise is preferred.

  • Knowledge of relevant safety, life-safety, security, and emergency-management regulatory requirements and industry practices.

title: Senior Information System Security Officer(ISSO)
description:
Leidos has a new and exciting opportunity for a Senior Information System Security Officer in our National Security Sector's (NSS) Cyber & Analytics Business Area (CABA). Join us and make a difference in National Security!

Senior Information System Security Officer (ISSO)

Leidos currently has an opening for a Senior Information System Security Officer (ISSO) to work at our Annapolis Junction, MD location. The selected candidate will act as an ISSO for a large software development program which includes software maintenance and development, IT support (Network/Workstation/Server), systems integration and life cycle support, enterprise application development, network engineering, and information systems security (ISS). The candidate will work with other security professionals in developing and implementing strategies to detect and mitigate threats to information systems, protect critical data sets, and provide assessments of system and network vulnerabilities.


Primary Roles and Responsibilities

  • Provide support for implementing and enforcing information systems security policies, standards, and methodologies.

  • Assist in the evaluation of security solutions to ensure they meet security requirements for processing multiple types of information.

  • Assist with the Configuration Management for information system security software, hardware, and firmware.

  • Analyze threats and develop and implement best practice methodologies for incident detection, reporting, and vulnerability remediation.

  • Maintain records on workstations, servers, routers, firewalls, intelligent hubs, network switches, etc. to include system upgrades.

  • Evaluate security solutions to ensure they meet security requirements for processing information.

  • Maintain operational security posture for information systems.

  • Provide support to the Information System Security Manager (ISSM) for maintaining the appropriate operational IA posture for a system/program/enclave.

  • Develop and maintain documentation for Certification & Accreditation in accordance with specified policies.

  • Develop and update system security plans and other IA documentation.

  • Provide support for Information Assurance Vulnerability Alerts (IAVAs) management (initiating IAVA responses and system security scans, completing remediation, extending IAVA patches and security updates to designated sites, etc.).

  • Provide CM for security-relevant information system software, hardware, and firmware.

  • Develop system security policy and ensure compliance.

  • Administer the user identification and authentication mechanisms of the Information System.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in a related field and at least 12 years of relevant experience. Additional experience may be substituted for a degree.

  • TS/SCI with polygraph security clearance.

  • Must have at least 10 years of experience as ISSO working independently, and/or on teams maintaining secure information system operations in isolated, connected and standalone environments.

  • Must have at least 5 years of experience using tools to support IAVA management.

  • Must have at least 5 years of experience using tools to support the preparation, maintenance, and management of SSPs and other security related documentation.

  • Demonstrated knowledge of and experience with several of the following: current security tools; hardware/software security implementation; communication protocols; encryption techniques/tools.

  • In-depth experience completing security evaluations of software systems or architectures to ensure they meet security requirements.

  • In-depth experience proposing, coordinating, implementing, and enforcing information systems security policies, standards, and methodologies, preferably on a large software or IT program.

  • Demonstrated experience performing day-to-day security operations of large, complicated information and information processing systems.

  • Must be committed to developing and adhering to best practices.

  • Must possess a high level of self-initiative and must be a solutions-oriented team player.

  • Must have excellent interpersonal skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Extensive experience as an Information Systems Security Officer on large software development and integration programs.

  • DoD 8570 compliance with IAT Level II or higher.

  • DoD 8570 compliance with IAM Level II or higher.

title: Radar Optimization Engineer
description:
As one of Leidos’ oldest and largest programs supporting the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), the NAS Integration Support Contract (NISC) Program is seeking a qualified professional to support the FAA’s Brand-New Air Traffic Control System (BNATCS) initiative—specifically the Radar Surveillance Replacement (RSR) Program Office (AJM-41)—by serving as an RSR Radar Optimization Engineer. The selected candidate will support radar configuration, testing, calibration, troubleshooting, and optimization activities for the RSR PO at some of the nation’s busiest and most critical airports.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Represent the PO at RSR sites, executing to an aggressive multi-site schedule.
  • Serve as an RSR subject matter expert (SME) to the RSR program office’s project, optimization, and engineering leads.
  • Support the integration, configuration, testing, calibration, troubleshooting, and optimization of radar and associated electronic systems.
  • Configure radar tracking parameters, target-classification software, network interfaces, and integration middleware as required.
  • Perform advanced field troubleshooting and root-cause analysis to isolate signal interference, hardware faults, communications failures, and data-packet loss.
  • Support antenna alignment and mechanical tilt and azimuth verification, as well as the evaluation of equipment mounting, environmental enclosures, and thermal-management considerations affecting radar performance.
  • Use spectrum analyzers, oscilloscopes, power meters, and specialized radar diagnostic software to tune system gain, filter clutter, establish detection thresholds, and verify system performance.
  • Evaluate system interfaces, including Ethernet, serial, Controller Area Network (CAN), fiber-optic communications, power distribution, grounding, bonding, and surge-protection systems.
  • Analyze radar performance data and make necessary system adjustments to achieve required detection, tracking, accuracy, and reliability standards.
  • Document test results, system configurations, identified deficiencies, corrective actions, and final optimization settings.
  • Coordinate with FAA personnel, system engineers, vendors, and other technical stakeholders to resolve system-performance issues.
  • Ensure field activities comply with applicable FAA requirements, and site-specific safety procedures.

Travel Expectations

  • Travel is expected to be high—50% to 75% of the time.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree with 4–8 years of relevant experience, or additional years of relevant experience that may be considered or accepted in lieu of a degree.
  • A degree, formal certification, or equivalent technical training in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Technology, Military Radar Systems, or a closely related discipline.
  • Experience with research, design, development, integration, maintenance, testing, calibration, or optimization of electrical and electronic equipment and systems.
  • Completion of formal radar training at the FAA Academy, a military technical school, or another recognized radar training program.
  • Prior radar certification authority at one or more airports or operational radar facilities.
  • Several years of hands-on field experience with one or more radar systems in the active National Airspace System (NAS) or a comparable operational environment.
  • In-depth knowledge of radio-frequency (RF) propagation, microwave transceivers, signal processing, antenna alignment, and waveguide systems.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of system-integration interfaces, including Ethernet, serial, CAN, and fiber-optic communications; network protocols; power distribution; grounding and bonding; and surge protection.
  • Proficiency using spectrum analyzers, oscilloscopes, power meters, and specialized radar diagnostic software.
  • Ability to perform radar testing, calibration, and optimization activities, including adjusting gain, filtering clutter, establishing detection thresholds, and verifying system performance.
  • Understanding of mechanical tilt and azimuth alignment, environmental enclosures, equipment mounting, and thermal-management requirements as they relate to radar performance.
  • Ability to configure radar tracking parameters, target-classification software, network interfaces, and integration middleware.
  • Advanced troubleshooting and root-cause-analysis skills for isolating RF interference, hardware faults, communications failures, and data-packet loss.
  • Ability to analyze radar performance data, document test results, and recommend or perform corrective adjustments.
  • Comprehensive understanding of FAA operational risk-management practices.
  • Ability to perform at a high level independently and as part of a small team while meeting an aggressive radar optimization schedule.
  • Demonstrated commitment to high-quality radar maintenance, testing, calibration, and optimization practices.
  • Professionalism when representing Leidos to FAA customers, consistent with delivering “best of the best” support.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of applicable FAA technical, safety, and radar-system requirements.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain an FAA Public Trust clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

The ideal candidate is a former FAA radar specialist, engineer, or technician with multi-year responsibility for radar systems in the operational NAS.

  • Experience with FAA surveillance radar systems and associated communications.
  • Experience supporting radar modernization, integration, commissioning, operational testing, acceptance, calibration, troubleshooting, or optimization activities.
  • Experience analyzing radar plots, system-performance data, target reports, coverage, clutter, interference, and tracking anomalies.
  • Familiarity with FAA safety requirements, grounding and bonding requirements, radar-performance standards, and site-specific work procedures.
