title: Continuous Improvement Leader
description:
Job Description

We are looking for Continuous Improvement Lead to strengthen our Kraft Heinz family.

The Continuous Improvement Lead position is within our Production Department. This is a field-based position located in Susurluk, Balıkesir.

The CI Lead is responsible for identifying and eliminating losses and waste on the line or equipment within their area of responsibility. They actively engage in problem-solving activities, digitalization efforts, and continuous improvement projects.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in food engineering or a related engineering field

  • Preferably min intermediate level of English

  • Preferably experienced in a food manufacturing environment

  • Proficient in MS Office programs

  • Strong analytical skills, result-oriented, and a team player

  • Residing in or willing to relocate to Balıkesir Susurluk, Bursa (Karacabey-Mustafakemalpaşa), Manyas, or Bandırma areas

Job Description

  • Identifies and prioritizes loss elimination opportunities by analyzing daily and shift-based data

  • Ensures sustainability of CI tools used on the shop floor through regular monitoring

  • Works on the floor to collect data on losses and changes in the last 24 hours

  • Investigates root causes of major breakdowns and encourages countermeasure planning

  • Determines optimal settings on the lines and ensures their continuity, taking preventive actions as needed

  • Participates in daily management meetings, ensures performance and daily management boards are updated

  • Collaborates with Process Owners, Team Leaders, and Maintenance Leaders to address losses

  • Applies problem-solving techniques to eliminate chronic losses and supports related efforts

  • Carries out all other CI-related tasks assigned by management

  • Adheres to all GMP, hygiene, and cleaning standards, considering them in CI projects

  • Adjusts to various shift patterns when necessary to work with all shift employees

  • Uses MES (Manufacturing Execution Systems) and ensures data accuracy

About Us


The Kraft Heinz Company is one of the largest food and beverage companies in the world, with eight $1 billion+ brands and global sales of approximately $25 billion. We’re a globally trusted producer of high-quality, great-tasting, and nutritious foods for over 150 years. Our brands are truly global, with products produced and marketed in over 40 countries. These beloved products include condiments and sauces, cheese and dairy, meals, meats, refreshment beverages, coffee, infant and nutrition products, and numerous other grocery products in a portfolio of more than 200 legacy and emerging brands.

No matter the brand, we’re united under one vision To sustainably grow by delighting more consumers globally. Bringing this vision to life is our team of 39,000+ food lovers, creative thinkers, and high performers worldwide. Together, we help provide meals to those in need through our global partnership with Rise Against Hunger. We also stand committed to responsible, sustainable practices that extend to every facet of our business, our consumers, and our communities. Every day, we’re transforming the food industry with bold thinking and unprecedented results. If you share our passion – and are ready to create the future, build a legacy, and lead as a global citizen – there’s only one thing to do join our table and let’s make life delicious!

Our Culture of Ownership, Meritocracy & Collaboration

We're not afraid to think differently. Embrace new ideas. Dream big. We empower our people at every level – from entry-level intern to senior leader – to own their work. We share a responsibility to think like Owners – to be mindful of the collective and sustained success of Kraft Heinz – which we apply to every situation, every day. As part of Kraft Heinz, you're supported to grow and achieve. You’re expected to bring your authentic self to work every day, to lead with humility, and drive outstanding performance at every level – and you’ll be rewarded. You’re given opportunities to leave a mark and build a legacy. But you won’t do it alone. You’re supported by passionate teammates along the way, and our collective, collaborative spirit fuels our incredible progress.

title: Project Manager – Enterprise Endpoint & Network Migrations
description:
We are seeking a mid-level Project Manager to support the planning and execution of large-scale customer technology migrations, with a primary focus on network infrastructure and endpoint migrations. This role will coordinate cross-functional teams, customers, vendors, and technical stakeholders to ensure migrations are delivered safely, efficiently, and with minimal disruption to business operations. The ideal candidate is an organized, proactive project leader who can manage multiple concurrent migration workstreams, drive accountability across technical teams, communicate effectively with customers and executives, and identify and resolve risks before they impact delivery.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead end-to-end project planning and execution for large-scale customer network and endpoint migration initiatives.

  • Develop and maintain detailed project plans, schedules, milestones, dependencies, RAID logs, and cutover plans.

  • Coordinate migration activities across network engineering, endpoint engineering, security, infrastructure, service delivery, operations, vendors, and customer teams.

  • Manage multiple concurrent migration projects and prioritize activities based on customer impact, technical dependencies, and business timelines.

  • Facilitate project kickoffs, status meetings, technical working sessions, migration readiness reviews, and executive updates.

  • Establish clear ownership, deadlines, and escalation paths across internal and external stakeholders.

  • Track project scope, schedule, risks, issues, dependencies, and resource requirements through completion.

  • Coordinate migration waves, pilot deployments, production cutovers, validation activities, and post-migration stabilization.

  • Partner with technical teams to ensure migration prerequisites, testing, documentation, rollback plans, and operational readiness are completed before cutover.

  • Proactively identify project risks and develop mitigation and contingency plans.

  • Manage customer communications and provide clear, concise status reporting on progress, risks, decisions, and next steps.

  • Support change management and ensure project activities align with established change-control and operational processes.

  • Drive post-migration lessons learned and incorporate improvements into subsequent migration waves.

  • Maintain accurate project documentation and ensure appropriate handoffs to operational support teams.

Required Qualifications

  • Requires a BA degree and 8 – 12 years of prior relevant experience or Masters with 6 – 10 years of prior relevant experience.

  • Active DoD Secret clearance

  • 3–6 years of project or program management experience, preferably supporting technology infrastructure or IT transformation initiatives.

  • Experience managing large-scale infrastructure, network, endpoint, cloud, data center, or technology migration projects.

  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate complex projects involving multiple technical teams and stakeholders.

  • Strong understanding of project management fundamentals, including scope, schedule, dependencies, risk management, change control, and stakeholder management.

  • Experience working directly with customers or business stakeholders in a delivery environment.

  • Strong communication, organization, facilitation, and problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to manage competing priorities and multiple projects in a fast-paced environment.

  • Comfortable working with technical teams and translating technical project information into clear business-level communications.

  • Proficiency with project management and collaboration tools such as Jira, Smartsheet, Microsoft Project, Confluence, or similar platforms.

Preferred Qualifications

  • PMP, CAPM, or similar project management certification.

  • Experience with network migrations, LAN/WAN transformations, SD-WAN, network modernization, endpoint refreshes, device migrations, or enterprise infrastructure consolidation.

  • Experience managing large customer migration programs involving multiple sites, business units, or geographic regions.

  • Familiarity with ITIL, Agile, or hybrid project delivery methodologies.

  • Experience coordinating third-party vendors, managed service providers, or technology partners.

  • Experience with migration planning, cutover management, rollback planning, and hypercare/stabilization.

  • Technical background or sufficient technical fluency to effectively partner with network, endpoint, infrastructure, and security engineering teams.

title: Security Systems Technician
description:
Job Description

The Defense Solutions Group at Leidos currently has an opening for a Security Systems Technician to support the Automated Installation Entry (AIE) program at U.S. Army and Department of Defense installations across CONUS and OCONUS locations.

The AIE program provides cutting-edge biometric authentication, multi-database credentialing verification, and integrated access control capabilities to over 100 military installations, with rapid expansion planned across Army, Navy, and Joint Force locations. As a Security Systems Technician, you will be at the forefront of deploying and sustaining advanced physical security systems including facial recognition, biometric scanning, automated vehicle barriers, and networked access control infrastructure in dynamic operational environments.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Install and integrate AIE system components at military installation Access Control Points (ACPs), including facial recognition hardware, biometric scanners, IP cameras, handheld credential readers, gate automation systems, and turnstiles.

  • Configure and test access control workstations, guard booth equipment, visitor management kiosks, and cloud-connected security infrastructure to ensure seamless integration with Army credentialing databases (ie. DEERS, NLETS, ABIS).

  • Perform preventive maintenance and troubleshooting on fielded AIE systems, diagnosing and resolving hardware failures, network connectivity issues, software configuration problems, and environmental factors affecting system performance.

  • Assist Site Project Manager (SPM) to conduct site surveys and technical assessments to determine installation requirements, assess existing infrastructure compatibility, and provide recommendations for ACP modernization and expansion.

  • Execute rapid response field service to address system outages, equipment failures, and mission-critical issues affecting installation access control operations, minimizing downtime and ensuring force protection readiness.

  • Document system configurations, modifications, and maintenance activities in accordance with program Technical Data Package (TDP) requirements and Leidos quality standards.

  • Support new site activations and technology upgrades, including facial recognition lane installations, server hardware refresh, biometric integration, and cloud migration activities.

  • Provide technical support to Tier I Help Desk for escalated issues requiring hands-on intervention, hardware replacement, or on-site diagnostics.

  • Travel extensively (up to 75%) to military installations across CONUS and OCONUS (including PACOM region) to support surveys, installation, and maintenance activities.

Basic Qualifications

  • Education/Experience: High School Diploma or GED with 4+ years of hands-on experience supporting technical US defense programs OR Associate's Degree in Electronics, Information Technology, or related technical field with 2+ years relevant experience.

  • U.S. Citizenship: Required to obtain and maintain a Secret security clearance and access military installations

  • Physical Security Systems Experience: Demonstrated hands-on experience with Physical Access Control Systems (PACS) or enterprise access control platforms, IP-based camera systems or other video surveillance, biometric authentication or identity verification systems, or electronic security hardware

  • Network & IT Proficiency: Working knowledge of TCP/IP networking, Windows operating systems, client-server architectures, and ability to troubleshoot network connectivity issues affecting security hardware.

  • Technical Aptitude: Proficient use of hand/power tools, digital multimeters, cable testers, and diagnostic equipment for electronics troubleshooting and installation.

  • Physical Requirements: Ability to lift up to 50 lbs., work from ladders/lifts, perform overhead installations, and work outdoors in varied weather conditions.

  • Valid Driver's License: Clean driving record and ability to operate government/rental vehicles for site-to-site travel.

  • Availability: Willing and able to travel up to 75% (including occasional OCONUS deployments lasting 1-4 weeks) and respond to emergency service calls with short notice.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Active Secret security clearance.

  • AIE or DBIDS system experience: Direct familiarity with AIE, Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS), or similar DoD installation access control platforms.

  • Advanced certifications: CompTIA Security+, Network+, A+, or manufacturer-specific certifications (HID, NEC, Lenel, AMAG, etc.)

  • Biometric systems expertise: Experience with DoD Automated Biometric Information System (ABIS), facial recognition deployment, or multi-factor authentication systems.

  • Military or DoD installation experience: Prior service or contractor experience working on military bases with understanding of force protection protocols, AT/FP requirements, and installation security operations.

  • Database and vetting system knowledge: Familiarity with DEERS, NLETS, Real ID compliance, or credentialing/vetting workflows.

  • Cloud infrastructure experience: Exposure to cloud-based security systems, DISA environments, or enterprise-scale deployments.

  • Project management or lead technician experience: Ability to manage small installation teams, coordinate with government POCs, and execute site activations independently.

  • OSHA 10-Hour or 30-Hour certification.

  • Low voltage/electrical licensing (state-specific, if applicable).

  • Previous Leidos or AIE program experience: Understanding of Leidos processes, AIE architecture, and established customer relationships with PM FPS or Army Garrison security personnel

  • Technical communication skills: Ability to document work clearly, brief non-technical stakeholders, and provide operator-level training to military security forces.

We're looking for enthusiastic graduates with strong numerical, analytical and communication skills who are eager to learn and develop their careers. You will hold, or be on track to achieve, a degree in Quantity Surveying or a related construction, engineering or commercial discipline.

title: Chinese Triage Examiner
description:
The Intel Sector is currently looking experienced Chinese Triage Examiners in various languages to perform media exploitation (MEDEX) and triage in support a customer in the National Capital Region (NCR). Triage Examiners should be experienced in general linguist operations and Document and Media Exploitation (DOMEX) operations, and are expected to leverage language and analytical skills, as well as advanced computer systems aptitude in addressing triage examination projects. Triage Examiners will perform eDiscovery examinations of electronic media for content of interest using a suite of forensic examination tools and will identify and prioritize items of importance for further processing, in accordance with customer standard operating procedures. Examiners will also be expected to communicate effectively and provide ad-hoc notification to superiors on task progress and significant findings, and to produce a report of their findings for further dissemination to customer(s).

Required Language: Chinese

Locations: The NMEC-LEaRN program is located at the customer site in Bethesda, MD, and we also offer the option to work from different locations (JIRC sites).

The primary responsibilities of the Triage Examiners are:

  • Perform data discovery on large datasets of foreign language material and identify essential elements of information.

  • Convert, reformat, parse, and otherwise exploit media files using customer tools to ensure compatibility and readability for translation systems.

  • Prepare files and metadata for transfer to translation systems, including review of foreign-language data.

  • Produce report of findings and disseminate to customer, analysts, and liaison officers.

  • Prepare accurate written gists, translations, and/or transcriptions of general and technical material.

  • Candidate must have operational experience within the Chinese language.

​

​Basic Qualifications

  • Must have the sufficient language skills, analytic skills, and technical aptitude to gain proficiency with job-required tools and processes (On-the-job training may be provided as needed to address customer-specific needs, with ongoing evaluations throughout train-up period).

  • Native-level proficiency in English.

  • Two years of overall experience in Chinese linguist operations (i.e. translation, language analysis), and two years of experience performing media examination for Document and Media Exploitation projects.

  • Willingness to perform occasional shift work to meet mission demands.

  • Achieve a minimum score of a 3/3 in Reading and Listening in Chinese and 3+/3+ for Reading and Listening in English.

  • BA degree and/or 4 years prior relevant experience in lieu of degree, or Masters with 2 years of prior relevant experience.

  • Ability to compose summarizations of highly technical and complex subjects that are both succinct and accessible to a general reader.

  • Outcomes-based problem solving of ill-defined and abstract problems.

  • Ability to maintain project momentum while working independently with limited oversight over a long period of time.

  • Ability to quickly scan and process a large amount of material in a foreign language for essential elements of information.

  • Ability to comprehend customer prioritization requirements and apply them to files under review, as well as apply personal judgment when assessing the potential value of files and information.

  • Demonstrated history of working on screening or translation projects and in maintaining the integrity and meaning of the translated material.

  • Demonstrated ability to communicate in a professional manner (email, spoken, & reports).

  • Ability to make sound decisions and handle stress, while meeting deadlines and performing in a high-paced environment.

  • Familiarity with report writing styles for DOD and IC consumers.

  • Possess a working proficiency in standard computer systems and office programs, with additional experience in media examination tools.

  • Ability to use or train to proficiency on customer specific software programs and tools.

​

Clearance

  • Must currently possess at least an active TS/SCI with polygraph clearance.

  • Current or recent SCI-level access is a significant advantage and preferred.

​​

Preferred Qualifications

  • Native-level proficiency in foreign language

  • Graduate of the Defense Language Institute Chinese Course.

  • An advanced degree in one of the following fields: Engineering, Computer Science, Chemistry, Physics, Legal, Medical, Banking and Financing, Foreign Military, Forensics

  • Familiarity with Digital Forensics/eDiscovery/Document and Media Exploitation (DOMEX) processes and specialized tools (i.e. FTK, enCase, or similar).

  • Past performance as a media examiner in support of DOD or IC customers.

title: Technology Control Officer
description:
Job Title: Technology Control Officer

Job Profile: Cyber Threat Intelligence Expert (4084)
Location: Dallas, TX (Hybrid option available)

Employment Type: Full-Time
Reports To: Sr. FSO

US Citizen- Must have a security clearance

Scope

  • BYDS operates under a DCSA FOCI-mitigation agreement that requires one named authority who can attest to the TCP and answer directly to the Board's Government Security Committee (GSC). The TCP, the access decisions on ITAR-controlled data, and the annual program reports carry the TCO’s signature: this is not an advisory function, it is a position of record for the organization.
  • Key responsibilities include aligning security program goals with organizational objectives, assessing and mitigating risk, ensuring regulatory compliance, protecting personnel, information, facilities, and business operations.

What you’ll do

  • Own and execute the BYDS Technology Control Plan end-to-end: policy, oversight, assurance, Board reporting, and annual attestation to the GSC under DCSA FOCI guidance.
  • Carry the trade-compliance mandate under ITAR across BYDS operations; ensure compliance with BIS and DDTC regulations and guidance, including classifications, export authorizations, exemptions, and exceptions.
  • Define control requirements for product teams to implement and monitor; review technical specifications, audit logs, and assurance evidence; identify cybersecurity vulnerabilities and assist in implementing countermeasures.
  • Prepare reports on the status of security safeguards applied to computer systems.
  • Report to the BYDS GSC on all ITAR and EAR matters; execute projects under guidance of the GSC, BYDS Executive Leadership Team, and FSO; publish a Technology Control Plan, Electronic Communications Plan, and annual DCSA reports.
  • Investigate and document program and TCP violations, gather required information, and sign off on required compliance reports; revoke account access and licenses following required actions per applicable policies.
  • Lead cross-functional compliance coordination across client, project, and information-security teams; investigate and document reports of lost or stolen BYDS devices, documents, or data in collaboration with team members.
  • Conduct periodic reviews of information systems to verify compliance with security authorization packages.
  • Coordinate changes or modifications to hardware, software, or firmware of systems with team members prior to implementation.
  • Monitor system recovery processes to verify proper restoration of security features and procedures. Maintain current and accessible IS security-related documentation for authorized personnel. Collect, review, and document audit records, including any anomalies.
  • Attend technical and security training relevant to assigned duties (e.g., operating system, networking, security management).
  • Execute the cybersecurity portion of annual self-inspections, including providing security coordination and review of system assessment plans.

What we are looking for

  • Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, Information Security, or related field
  • Strong understanding of NISPOM, DAAPM, JSIG methodologies and techniques
  • Proven experience as an ISSO supporting DoD efforts
  • Knowledge of various FOCI Mitigations, DCSA Policies and Procedures
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Familiarity with security frameworks such as eMASS, NIST, and ISO 27001
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team

-------------------------------------------

title: Senior Engineer - Verification & Validation Delivery
description:
Role Title: Senior Engineer – Verification & Validation Delivery

We are Rolls-Royce SMR and we’re doing something that’s never been done before. We’re revolutionising an industry. That’s a once-in-a-career opportunity for those excited by such a challenge. This is more than just a job; this is a legacy.

The Development Engineering organisation is accountable for proving that the SMR power station design meets its objectives and requirements. It is also responsible for providing the data and evidence that underpin the design and delivery of the power station through verification, testing, demonstration and research programmes. This spans not only nuclear engineering but the wider engineering and operational disciplines required to deliver a major infrastructure project.

About the Role

Senior Verification and Validation (V&V) Engineers play a key role in Rolls-Royce SMR’s Systems Engineering approach by leading the process of verifying that the power station design meets its requirements. This forms a crucial part of our strategy to offer delivery certainty through the use of modern engineering tools and techniques — including analysis and rig testing — to substantiate the design before construction begins.

You will take ownership of complex, safety-critical or business-critical areas of the power station aligned to your expertise. Your initial responsibility will be to develop comprehensive verification strategies that define the activities and evidence required to demonstrate compliance. Throughout the verification lifecycle, you will work closely with design leads and technical specialists to execute these strategies and confirm compliance.

Alongside technical leadership, you will mentor other V&V Engineers, support capability development and complete rigorous technical reviews to ensure quality and consistency.

There are multiple roles to fill within the team & we are particularly interested in speaking with people from one or more the following backgrounds:

  • Equipment Qualification (EQ) on a previous nuclear project, or qualification of components in a safety critical environment

  • Reactor systems and/or components (e.g. reactor internals, integrated head package, control rod drive mechanisms, etc…)

  • Nuclear auxiliary systems or components (e.g. radioactive liquid/solid/gas processing and storage, Heating Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC), &/or nuclear sampling and handling)

We’ll Need You To:

  • Develop verification and validation strategies within your area of responsibility

  • Act as an intelligent customer in the V&V of the plant and across the RR SMR business

  • Support the verification and validation of the safety case

  • Produce reports for regulatory bodies and present/discuss findings with regulators

  • Define objectives and requirements for verification activities (e.g. rig tests, analyses) and agree these with delivery teams

  • Review and collect evidence of verification activities across internal teams and the supply chain

  • Collate evidence and use it to assess compliance against requirements

  • Manage technical interfaces across functions to ensure coherent and efficient technical solutions

  • Coach and review the work of others to elevate technical quality across the team

  • Perform detailed technical checks and provide constructive feedback to peers

Key Skills Required:

We know there’s no such thing as the ‘perfect’ candidate. If you meet around 75% of the criteria below, we’d love to hear from you:

  • Experience in verification and validation of new products, ideally in a safety-critical and highly regulated industry

  • Experience leading complex engineering projects; nuclear experience preferred but not essential

  • Strong project management capability including scope, schedule, resource and financial control

  • Experience identifying, managing and escalating technical and programme risks

  • Ability to resolve issues while ensuring quality and safety standards

  • Strong supplier and customer relationship management skills

  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills; able to unite multi-disciplinary teams

  • Strong analytical skills and a methodical approach

  • Systems-thinking mindset with experience collaborating across engineering disciplines

  • Degree in an engineering discipline and recognised by a professional body or working towards this

Location:

Hybrid working with one of the following locations as your primary site: Derby, Manchester or Warrington.

Salary and Package:

The salary band for this will be between £50,650 - £66,500 dependent on the skills, values, and knowledge you bring. There may be some flexibility with the starting salary in exceptional cases, and, in due course, there is the potential for you to develop the role further.

Benefits include:

  • Bonus - Performance-related target opportunity 12.5%

  • Benefits Allowance - £2,200 per annum for a bespoke package

  • Pension - 12% employer and 6% employee contributions

  • Holidays - 28 days (+ public holidays) with ability to buy or sell up to 4 days

  • Private Medical Insurance - BUPA single cover

  • Life Assurance - 6x pensionable pay

  • Home Office Support - £250 one-off payment for new starters

Job Description

Brookfield Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Fund

Brookfield Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Fund (“BAIIF” or “the Fund”) is Brookfield’s inaugural strategy dedicated to investing in the physical infrastructure underpinning artificial intelligence. The Fund targets opportunities across the full AI value chain—including digital hubs and AI factories, compute hardware, power transmission, and strategic adjacencies—positioning Brookfield to capitalize on the transformative growth of AI technologies.

The Fund builds on Brookfield’s leadership in infrastructure and deep operating capabilities to scale critical AI subsectors (data centers, power and wireless infrastructure) to capitalize on the over $7-trillion opportunity of investment in physical infrastructure required to support the $10-trillion potential productivity gain from AI adoption.

  • Focus on high-quality real assets or highly contracted businesses that underpin AI.

  • Conduct deep industry and market research to inform investment strategies and identify emerging trends in AI infrastructure.

Key Qualifications

Join us for the opportunity to grow and make a difference in ways that matter to you.

Role Summary

The Offer Management Director, Cash Management, serves as the business owner for the default cash position within the firm’s (direct-to-consumer) brokerage offering. The role is accountable for the full life cycle of the cash management offering—from initial design and launch through ongoing management, client retention & growth, and revenue optimization.

This individual owns the offer strategy, client value proposition, economics, and overall performance of the offering. The Director will manage the cash management P&L and pricing strategies, oversee key external partners, and define the supporting capabilities required to build a competitive and sustainable cash management offer.

This is a business ownership role. The Director will establish business requirements and priorities but will partner with digital product and technology leaders who own delivery teams and technical backlogs.

Responsibilities

Offer Strategy and Business Ownership:

  • Own the end-to-end strategy and business performance of the default cash position within direct-to-consumer brokerage accounts.
  • Develop the vision, client value proposition, road map, and phased launch plan for the cash management offering.
  • Establish how the offering will attract and retain client assets, generate sustainable revenue, and strengthen the broader brokerage relationship.
  • Maintain accountability for the offer after launch, including ongoing optimization, competitive positioning, and long-term growth.
  • Ensure the offering reflects the firm’s brand, fiduciary standards, client experience expectations, and long-term business strategy.

Financial Management and Pricing:

  • Own the P&L associated with brokerage cash balances and related cash management capabilities.
  • Develop business cases, financial forecasts, and profitability analyses for new features, pricing changes, and strategic investments.
  • Recommend pricing strategies based on market conditions, competitive positioning, client behavior, funding economics, and financial objectives.
  • Partner with finance, treasury, marketing, and business leadership to review and approve rate changes, promotional offers, and pricing decisions.
  • Monitor the relationship between client yield, spread revenue, balance retention, net flows, servicing costs, and overall profitability.
  • Establish processes for responding to changes in interest rates, competitor pricing, client behavior, and market conditions.

Offer Design and Supporting Capabilities:

  • Define the business requirements for a complete and competitive cash management experience.
  • Determine the features required to support a healthy cash business, including FDIC-insured sweep capabilities, partner-bank capacity, liquidity, money movement, debit functionality, direct deposit, and other relevant cash services.
  • Partner with digital product and technology teams to translate business strategy into client journeys, product requirements, and prioritized delivery plans.
  • Evaluate trade-offs among revenue, client yield, convenience, liquidity, operational complexity, and cost.
  • Ensure the default cash position is clearly integrated into the broader brokerage account experience.

Partner and Vendor Management:

  • Oversee the business relationship with clearing firms, sweep-program administrators, partner banks, and other external providers supporting the offering.
  • Maintain sufficient partner-bank capacity and diversification to support client balances, deposit insurance objectives, liquidity needs, and business growth.
  • Evaluate partner performance, economics, service levels, operational resilience, and strategic alignment.
  • Lead commercial discussions and support contract negotiations in partnership with sourcing, legal, finance, and business leadership.
  • Identify and manage concentration, capacity, operational, reputational, and third-party risks.

Client Experience, Marketing, and Brand:

  • Partner with marketing and digital teams to develop clear, accurate, and differentiated positioning for the offering.
  • Ensure client communications clearly explain yield, liquidity, deposit insurance, program structure, eligibility, and relevant risks.
  • Monitor client feedback, complaints, service interactions, and behavioral trends to identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Balance revenue objectives with client trust, competitive value, and the firm’s brand reputation.
  • Develop retention strategies for periods of changing interest rates, increased competitor activity, or elevated client cash movement.

Risk, Controls, and Regulatory Oversight:

  • Partner with legal, compliance, risk, and operations to ensure the offering meets applicable brokerage, banking, disclosure, and supervisory requirements.
  • Ensure appropriate controls exist for rate changes, bank allocation, client communications, liquidity, reconciliation, operational processing, and vendor oversight.
  • Participate in governance and approval processes for new features, material pricing changes, promotions, and external partnerships.
  • Proactively identify and address regulatory, conduct, operational, reputational, and financial risks.

Performance Management and Executive Reporting:

  • Define the key performance indicators used to evaluate the health and effectiveness of the offering.
  • Develop regular reporting for business and executive leadership on financial results, client outcomes, competitive positioning, operational performance, and emerging risks.
  • Use performance data and client insights to recommend investments, pricing changes, feature enhancements, and growth opportunities.
  • Maintain clear accountability for offer-level results and corrective actions when performance falls below expectations.

Qualifications
Required:

  • Bachelor's degree or the equivalent combination of education and relevant experience AND
  • 10+ years of total relevant work experience
  • Demonstrated experience owning the strategy and financial performance of a complex consumer financial product or offering.
  • Strong understanding of product economics, pricing, profitability, balance growth, retention, and client behavior.
  • Strong executive communication, stakeholder management, analytical, and decision-making capabilities.

Preferred:

  • Experience managing brokerage cash sweep, bank deposits, insured sweep programs, money market products, or other retail cash management solutions.
  • Experience at a digital-first retail bank, brokerage firm, financial technology company, or consumer financial services organization.
  • Knowledge of retail brokerage operations, clearing relationships, partner-bank programs, and third-party vendor management.
  • Familiarity with the legal, regulatory, compliance, operational, and disclosure considerations associated with brokerage cash offerings.
  • Experience launching and scaling a new financial product from design through implementation and ongoing operations.

This requisition is for future openings. Qualified applicants will be contacted and added to a pipeline for future vacancies.

As a BSR, you will provide key beneficiary education and enrollment services for the TRICARE Overseas Program (TOP) under the Defense Health Agency (DHA). Your work will help ensure that TRICARE-eligible beneficiaries receive the healthcare services and support they need.

What You’ll Do:

  • Verify Benefits & Enrollment: Process enrollments, disenrollments, portability transfers, and more via systems like Defense Online Enrollment System (DOES) and MHS Genesis.
  • Primary Care Manager (PCM) Changes: Follow Military Treatment Facility (MTF) guidelines to make individual and batch PCM updates.
  • Education & Customer Service: Offer guidance on TRICARE resources, benefits, enrollment, and claims, assisting beneficiaries both in person and over the phone.
  • Claims Assistance: Provide basic claims status updates and support.
  • Conduct Briefings: Lead informational sessions for various events such as in/out processing, maternity, and pre-separation/retirement.
  • Data Management: Collect and record daily activities and Other Health Insurance (OHI) info into applicable systems.
  • Assess & Escalate Issues: Evaluate the level of assistance needed and refer or escalate complex issues as needed for proper resolution.
  • Compliance & Confidentiality: Comply with all HIPAA regulations, maintain confidentiality and proper handling of Protected Health Information (PHI), and complete Leidos and other training courses on time.
  • Collaborate & Support: Assist with remote support, train new team members, and other duties as assigned.

Basic Qualifications:

  • High School diploma or GED, or equivalent years of experience
  • U.S. Citizenship
  • SOFA/Command-Sponsored status as a dependent of an Active-Duty Service Member, DoD employee, or U.S. Contractor supporting the DoD
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain ADP IT III clearance (Non-Sensitive Position, Tier 1)
  • 3+ years of customer service experience

Essential Skills:

  • Fluent in English with strong written and oral communication
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook)
  • Effective at delivering presentations
  • Ability to tactfully communicate with others, both in person and on the phone
  • Self-starter, able to work independently and with minimal supervision
  • Strong organizational, time management, and multitasking abilities
  • High attention to detail

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with TRICARE Overseas Program, Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System (DEERS), DOES, and MHS Genesis
  • Work background in the following areas:
    • U.S. military healthcare delivery system or civilian managed care
    • Medical or clinical environment
    • MHS Genesis or civilian healthcare systems, medical claims

SALARY: The annual salary for this specific position is $32,000 and the program is not able to negotiate that. * With a position in the UK, you are also eligible for an annual foreign service premium in the amount of $3,000.00.

If you're looking for comfort, keep scrolling. At Leidos, we outthink, outbuild, and outpace the status quo — because the mission demands it. We're not hiring followers. We're recruiting the ones who disrupt, provoke, and refuse to fail. Step 10 is ancient history. We're already at step 30 — and moving faster than anyone else dares.

title: Software Engineer 1 (DevOps) - Full-time, onsite
description:
Software Engineer 1 (DevOps) - Full-time, onsite

Engineering @ Grayhat

You'll work closely with software engineers, QA, product managers, and leadership to make sure our applications move from development to production smoothly - and stay there.

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys automation, solving infrastructure problems, improving reliability, and making engineering teams faster.

1. Infrastructure & Cloud

  • Manage and maintain cloud infrastructure and development environments.
  • Work with services such as AWS, Azure, or GCP.
  • Configure and maintain servers, networking, storage, databases, and related infrastructure.
  • Help design infrastructure that is reliable, scalable, and cost-effective.
  • Maintain development, staging, and production environments.

2. CI/CD & Deployment

  • Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines for web, mobile, backend, and other applications.
  • Automate build, testing, deployment, and release processes.
  • Improve deployment speed, reliability, and consistency.
  • Manage application releases and production deployments.
  • Reduce manual deployment and operational work through automation.

3. Docker & Containerization

  • Build and maintain Docker images and containerized applications.
  • Work with Docker Compose and/or Kubernetes where appropriate.
  • Improve container security, performance, and reliability.
  • Help engineering teams adopt consistent development and deployment environments.

4. Monitoring & Reliability

  • Set up and maintain application and infrastructure monitoring.
  • Monitor system health, performance, uptime, and resource usage.
  • Configure logging, alerts, dashboards, and incident monitoring.
  • Investigate production issues and help identify their root causes.
  • Continuously improve system reliability and availability.

5. Security & Access

  • Follow infrastructure and deployment security best practices.
  • Manage environment variables, secrets, credentials, and access controls securely.
  • Implement appropriate permissions and authentication mechanisms.
  • Help identify and address infrastructure security risks.
  • Work comfortably with Linux environments.
  • Manage processes, services, networking, permissions, storage, and system resources.
  • Troubleshoot server and application-level issues.
  • Use command-line tools effectively to diagnose problems.

7. Automation

  • Automate repetitive infrastructure and operational tasks.
  • Use scripting and infrastructure-as-code where appropriate.
  • Improve internal developer workflows and engineering tooling.
  • Look for ways to eliminate manual processes and reduce operational overhead.

8. Engineering Collaboration

  • Work closely with software engineers to understand application requirements.
  • Support developers in getting their applications running reliably in different environments.
  • Collaborate with QA on testing and release processes.
  • Help teams understand deployment, infrastructure, and production requirements.
  • Document important infrastructure and operational processes.
  • Use AI tools to accelerate troubleshooting, scripting, documentation, automation, and infrastructure work.
  • Explore practical ways AI can improve DevOps workflows.
  • No blind copy-paste engineering - you should understand what you deploy and why.

10. Ownership & Problem Solving

  • Take ownership of infrastructure and deployment tasks from start to finish.
  • Investigate problems instead of simply working around them.
  • Identify bottlenecks and proactively improve systems.
  • Stay calm and methodical when dealing with production issues.

What We’re Looking For

We're looking for someone who is:

  • Curious about how systems work under the hood.
  • Comfortable working across infrastructure, software, and cloud environments.
  • Strong at troubleshooting and logical problem-solving.
  • Detail-oriented when dealing with production systems.
  • Comfortable communicating with developers and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Able to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
  • Proactive rather than waiting for someone to tell you what needs fixing.
  • Comfortable taking ownership of systems and processes.
  • Interested in continuously improving how engineering teams build and ship products.

Must-Haves

  • 1-3+ years of professional experience in DevOps, Cloud Engineering, SRE, Infrastructure, System Administration, or a related field.
  • Strong understanding of Linux.
  • Practical experience with Git and Git workflows.
  • Experience building or maintaining CI/CD pipelines.
  • Experience with Docker and containerization.
  • Experience with at least one major cloud platform: AWS, Azure, or GCP.
  • Understanding of networking fundamentals: DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, TCP/IP, ports, firewalls, etc.
  • Experience with deployment and production environments.
  • Basic understanding of databases and application infrastructure.
  • Experience with monitoring, logging, and troubleshooting.
  • Scripting experience with Bash, Python, or similar.
  • Understanding of environment variables, secrets, permissions, and basic security practices.
  • Strong problem-solving and debugging skills.
  • Good communication and documentation skills.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating closely with engineering teams.
  • Comfortable using AI tools as part of modern engineering workflows.

Good to Have

  • Terraform or other Infrastructure as Code tools
  • AWS services such as EC2, ECS/EKS, RDS, S3, CloudWatch, IAM, VPC
  • Nginx or similar reverse proxies
  • Redis
  • GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or similar
  • Prometheus, Grafana, ELK/OpenSearch, Sentry, or similar
  • Infrastructure security and vulnerability management
  • Experience with microservices
  • Experience with mobile application deployment infrastructure
  • Experience supporting AI/ML workloads
  • Experience with SaaS, AI, fintech, gaming, or enterprise products
  • Experience working with international clients
  • Kubernetes orchestration and Helm
  • Strong understanding of cloud networking

What Success Looks Like

After joining Grayhat, success means:

  • Deployments become faster, safer, and more predictable.
  • CI/CD pipelines work reliably and require minimal manual intervention.
  • Infrastructure is properly documented and reproducible.
  • Production issues are detected quickly and resolved systematically.
  • Monitoring and alerting give the team meaningful visibility into system health.
  • Developers can focus on building products instead of fighting infrastructure.
  • Infrastructure becomes more secure, scalable, and cost-efficient.
  • You proactively identify problems before they become major incidents.
  • You gradually take ownership of increasingly complex infrastructure and DevOps responsibilities.

One Last Thing

We're not looking for someone who simply knows a list of DevOps tools.

We're looking for an engineer who understands why those tools exist, how systems fit together, and how to make engineering teams better through automation and reliability.

If you enjoy breaking down difficult infrastructure problems, automating repetitive work, and making systems that just work, you'll fit right in.

Build the infrastructure. Automate the boring. Keep everything running.

title: Campaign Director till internationell marknadsföringsbyrå
description:
Vill du ta ett helhetsansvar för kampanjer för några av marknadens mest spännande konsumentvarumärken och samtidigt arbeta i framkant av den snabbt växande creator marketing-branschen?

Vi söker nu en erfaren Campaign Director till en snabbväxande och internationell marknadsföringsbyrå i Stockholm. Här får du en central roll i att driva kundkampanjer från idé och uppstart till genomförande, analys och uppföljning - i en miljö där kreativitet, högt tempo och tydliga resultat går hand i hand.

OM FÖRETAGET

Vår kund är en etablerad och snabbväxande aktör inom creator marketing som hjälper välkända konsumentvarumärken att nå och engagera sina målgrupper genom kreatörer och sociala medier.

Bolaget grundades i Stockholm och har under de senaste åren vuxit från ett mindre team till närmare 100 medarbetare runt om i Europa. Verksamheten sträcker sig idag över fler än tio marknader och bolaget samarbetar med flera internationellt välkända B2C-varumärken. Företaget befinner sig i en expansiv fas och kulturen präglas av höga ambitioner, kreativitet, samarbete och ett tydligt fokus på resultat.

OM ROLLEN

Som Campaign Director får du ett övergripande projektledningsansvar för flera kundkampanjer och driver dem genom hela processen - från kickoff och planering till genomförande, analys och leverans.

Du blir en central kontaktpunkt för kunden och arbetar samtidigt nära interna specialistteam för att säkerställa att kampanjer håller rätt riktning, kvalitet och tempo samt levererar mot uppsatta KPI och förväntningar.

Rollen passar dig som trivs med att kombinera kundrelationer, projektledning och marknadsföring och som är trygg i att hålla ihop flera parallella kampanjer i en snabbrörlig miljö.

DINA HUVUDSAKLIGA ARBETSUPPGIFTER
  • Leda och projektleda kundkampanjer från start till leverans
  • Koordinera interna team och säkerställa att aktiviteter, deadlines och leveranser håller rätt riktning
  • Säkerställa att kampanjer levererar mot överenskomna KPI och kundförväntningar
  • Vara en nära och rådgivande kontakt för kunder genom hela samarbetet
  • Bygga och utveckla långsiktiga kundrelationer med fokus på hög kundnöjdhet och fortsatta samarbeten
  • Ta fram rapporter, analysera kampanjresultat och presentera datadrivna rekommendationer
  • Identifiera möjligheter att optimera genomförande och förbättra kampanjernas resultat
  • Hantera flera parallella kunder och kampanjer med bibehållen struktur och kvalitet
VI SÖKER DIG SOM
  • Har minst fyra års erfarenhet inom marknadsföring, projektledning eller närliggande område
  • Har tidigare erfarenhet från en kundnära roll och är trygg i att driva dialog med olika typer av stakeholders
  • Är en naturlig projektledare som är strukturerad, organiserad och van att hålla ihop flera parallella initiativ
  • Trivs i ett högt tempo och kan prioritera och fatta beslut även när förutsättningarna förändras
  • Har ett tydligt affärs- och resultatfokus och motiveras av att skapa värde för både kund och team
  • Är relationsskapande och har lätt för att bygga förtroende hos såväl kunder som kollegor.Har mycket god kommunikativ förmåga
  • Kommunicerar obehindrat på både svenska och engelska

Erfarenhet från creator marketing, influencer marketing, sociala medier eller närliggande områden är starkt meriterande.

OM TJÄNSTEN

Det här är en möjlighet att bli en del av en ambitiös och snabbväxande organisation som befinner sig mitt i utvecklingen av hur moderna varumärken arbetar med creator-led marketing.

Du får arbeta med spännande konsumentvarumärken i en internationell miljö tillsammans med kollegor som kombinerar kreativitet med ett starkt kommersiellt och datadrivet fokus.

Bolaget erbjuder bland annat:

  • Sex veckors semester
  • Generöst hälso- och friskvårdspaket
  • Försäkring och pension
  • Årliga konferensresor
  • En ambitiös och högpresterande miljö med stora möjligheter att utvecklas

Omfattning: HeltidStart: Så snart som möjligtPlats: Stockholm

REKRYTERINGSPROCESS & KONTAKT

Detta är en direktrekrytering, vilket innebär att kandidaten som får tjänsten blir anställd direkt hos vår kund. Rekryteringsprocessen hanteras av Nordicrule och vår kund önskar att alla frågor rörande tjänsten mejlas in till Nordicrule.

title: Junior Data Center Shift Engineer
description:
Amsterdam, Netherlands, Amsterdam, Noord-Holland, NL


Klik hieronder op \'Solliciteren\' om uw sollicitatie ter overweging in te dienen. Zorg ervoor dat uw cv up-to-date is en dat u eerst de functie-eisen heeft gelezen.

Salary Range: €43,000.00 To €48,000.00 Annually

Salute is a global leader in delivering Data Center services - firmly established in the US and with a rapidly growing client base across Europe and beyond.

This is an exciting time to join the team as we step up operations in new countries and commence work on new and challenging projects. As a result of this growth, we are looking to recruit and develop a Junior Data Centre Shift Engineer.

The Junior Data Center Shift Engineer (FE) is responsible for ensuring that all electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment within the data center is operating at peak efficiency. This involves both planned preventative maintenance of equipment, daily corrective work, and emergency response to emergent issues. The FE serves as a technical resource reporting to the Site Manager and interacting with onsite Engineering Operations Technicians (EOT) and any third-party vendors. They are expected to support all facility operations and equipment within a given data center. This equipment includes, but is not limited to, standby diesel generators, switchgear, UPSs, PDUs, AHUs, chillers, cooling towers, chemical treatment systems, pumps, motors, VFDs, and building automation systems.

**This position will be on a 3-shift pattern including night shifts.**

Responsibilities
  • Operate, monitor, maintain , and respond to abnormal conditions in facilities systems.
  • Complete planned and ad-hoc preventive maintenance work assignments requiring the skill and direction of several engineering, mechanical, and maintenance trades
  • Conduct periodic inspections of building systems, i.e., HVAC, electrical distribution, Maintain mechanical equipment rooms to ensure clean and safe conditions
  • Rapid response, investigation, and management of indoor emergency situations and air quality complaints
  • Have a complete working knowledge on creating, closing and tracking "work requests" (WR). Initiate or respond to work orders, follow-up and verify completion of work
  • Monitor performance/note deficiencies of service contractors and recommend changes as necessary
  • Performance other related duties and responsibilities as assigned by management
Qualifications
  • A minimum of 1 year of directly related experience in the operation, installation and maintenance of building systems with technical understanding and knowledge of HVAC, electrical, plumbing, fire/life safety, and control systems
  • High school diploma or College Degree
  • Good observation skills and problem-solving ability.

The role is a full-time position and your base salary will be commensurate with experience but is expected to be highly competitive.

What you'll get from us:

Here, at Salute, we value our people and take great pride providing not just a job but fantastic career opportunities. In addition to the opportunity to work in a great team and earn a competitive salary - you'll gain access to cutting edge industry training that aims to enhance your skills and propel your career forward. xgiwjmb Not only will you receive valuable development in your current role, but for those who are ambitious and motivated, the possibilities are endless.

Position Title:

Retirement Services Assistant (Operations & Policy Analyst 1)

Job Description:

Now Hiring! Retirement Services Assistant (Operations & Policy Analyst 1)

The Centralized PERS (CPERS) unit resides within the Office of State Controller. This unit is responsible for administering, reporting and ensuring that state agency employee PERS information is accurate and state employee retirement data is correctly posted to PERS member accounts. CPERS works to research, analyze, audit and correct complex state employee data which spans decades of information, crosses multiple operational systems, and includes application and interpretation of PERS specific legislation and policy parameters which differ from traditional state agency policies.

As the Retirement Services Assistant you will act as a liaison between state agencies, Public Employee Retirement System (PERS) staff and employees to resolve retirement account discrepancies and ensure consistent administration of retirement accounts for more than 55,000 current State of Oregon employees, terminated employees and retirees. You will research employee records and determine corrective actions necessary to allow suspended records to post and ensure employee retirement accounts are accurate and consistent across all state agencies. Additionally, you will provide guidance, administrative, analytical and technical advice and support in implementation and ongoing administration of the statewide PERS pension plan and other special project assignments.

Review the full position duties, details, and working conditions here.

This Is What You Need to Qualify

  • A Bachelor's Degree in Business or Public Administration, Behavioral or Social Sciences, Finance, Political Science or any degree demonstrating the capacity for the knowledge and skills; OR

  • Any combination of experience or education equivalent to three years technical-level experience that typically supports the knowledge and skill requirements listed for the classification.

Desired Attributes:

  • Intermediate knowledge and understanding of state human resources, payroll and/or PERS functions and information systems as they relate to processing of state employee personnel, payroll and retirement account transactions.

  • General knowledge of state laws, rules, and policies related to the state’s pension program and their impact on state government employees and PERS reporting.

  • Basic knowledge and understanding of information technology as it relates to processing of state employee personnel, payroll and retirement account transactions.

  • Ability to analyze data and problem solve.

  • Proactive, detail and solution oriented with the ability to organize and prioritize completing deadlines.

  • Demonstrated communication and team player skills.

Preference Statement:

Preference may be given to those candidates with prior experience working in payroll, human resource or retirement/pension services.

At DAS, we are committed to innovation, continuous improvement, outstanding service delivery, and support for each other as professionals and as people. We believe hiring highly skilled, diverse employees is key to cultivating positive results, well-informed outcomes, and value the unique skill set and perspective of all our team members.

Our amazing benefits include:

  • Comprehensive Health Coverage: Low-cost medical, vision, and dental plans for you and your family. Additional benefits include life insurance, short- and long-term disability, deferred compensation savings plans, and flexible spending accounts for health and childcare. Optional benefits including life insurance, disability, FSA, and more

  • Generous Paid Time Off: 11 holidays, 3 personal business days, monthly sick leave and vacation leave that increases with years of service.

  • Career Development: Opportunities for professional growth and advancement.

  • Get There - Oregon’s easy-to-use carpool matching tool and trip planner.

  • Public Service Loan Forgiveness: You may qualify for the PSLF program.

Applicants must be willing to relocate or live within commuting distance upon accepting an offer. Terms of hybrid work and the work schedule will be discussed and agreed upon with the successful candidate and hiring manager.

How to Apply

Please save a copy of this job announcement for reference, as it is not available for you to view after the announcement deadline.

title: Nutrition Trainer (Temporary)
description:
Job Description

UW Performance Nutrition has an outstanding opportunity for a Temporary Nutrition Trainer to join their team.

About this Opportunity

Reporting to the Director of Performance Nutrition, the Performance Dietitian is responsible for managing and delivering comprehensive nutritional services to approximately 650 student-athletes on 22 varsity athletic teams in collaboration with athletic trainers, team physicians, sports psychologists, and strength and conditioning coaches, and in support of coaches, athletics administrators and department personnel.

As a trusted partner within UW Athletics, the Performance Dietitian works closely with student-athletes, coaches, sports medicine providers, and performance staff to ensure nutrition is effectively integrated into training, competition, recovery, and long-term health goals. This position plays an essential role in fostering a culture of excellence, collaboration, and student-athlete-centered care across the Husky Athletics community. Learn more about UW Athletics:

Key Responsibilities

Provide nutrition services for assigned Olympic sport programs (60%):

  • Develop and implement team nutrition strategies while managing a substantial caseload of student-athletes requiring performance and medical nutrition support.
  • Conduct nutrition assessments and screenings, develop individualized nutrition care plans, and provide medical nutrition therapy for a broad range of conditions.
  • Review and provide guidance on dietary supplement use in accordance with NCAA, anti-doping, and University guidelines.

Provide nutrition education and outreach (5%):

  • Educate student-athletes, coaches, and support staff on evidence-based nutrition practices, including meal planning, grocery shopping, food storage, competition fueling, recovery nutrition, cooking skills, and other lifestyle nutrition topics that support health and athletic performance.

Conduct body composition assessment and education (5%):

  • Evaluate body composition and provide education to student-athletes and coaches regarding the relationship between body composition, health, and athletic performance throughout the training and competitive year.

Lead sport science and nutrition data initiatives (5%):

  • Coordinate hydration, sweat rate, body composition, and other nutrition-related performance assessments for assigned teams.
  • Utilize technology platforms and applications to support student-athlete education, monitor progress, and generate reports with data-informed recommendations for coaches and sport performance staff.

Collaborate as part of a multidisciplinary sports medicine team (5%):

  • Work closely with mental health providers, team physicians, athletic trainers, and other healthcare professionals to support student-athletes with eating disorders, disordered eating, body image concerns, and other nutrition-related medical conditions.

Provide dietary supplements, education and guidance (5%):

  • Educate student-athletes, coaches, and support staff on the safe and effective use of dietary supplements, including considerations related to efficacy, safety, drug-nutrient interactions, NCAA regulations, and anti-doping requirements.

Support medical nutrition supplementation recommendations (5%):

  • Collaborate with team physicians to evaluate and recommend vitamins, minerals, and dietary supplements for student-athletes with medically indicated needs.

Provide on-site nutrition coaching during training table meals (5%):

  • Attend team meals and training table services to offer individualized nutrition guidance and reinforce healthy fueling practices.

Serve as a nutrition resource for meal and menu planning (2.5%):

  • Advise athletic teams on year-round menu development, training table offerings, pre- and post-competition meals, and food service planning with hotels, caterers, and restaurants for home and away events.

Support staff development and training (2.5%):

  • Assist the Director of Performance Nutrition in mentoring and supervising performance nutrition fellows, dietetic interns, and student interns.

Required Qualifications

To be considered for this opportunity your application must demonstrate you meet both the minimum qualifications and additional qualifications listed below. Equivalent education and/or experience may substitute for minimum qualifications except when there are legal requirements, such as a license, certification, and/or registration.

Minimum Qualifications

Applicants who do not meet these qualifications WILL NOT be forwarded to the Hiring Manager.

  • Bachelor’s degree in food and nutrition sciences, Dietetics, or a related field with at least one year of experience providing nutrition counseling, with a focus on sports nutrition.
  • Must be registered with the Commission on Dietetic Registration (CDR).
  • Certification as a Dietitian by the Washington State Department of Health is required upon hire.

Additional Qualifications

  • Experience conducting body composition assessments (e.g., DXA and ISAK skinfold measurements), sweat testing, hydration assessment, and related performance nutrition evaluations are desired.
  • Have knowledge of complementary medicine, ergogenic aids, and nutritional supplements, including NCAA and WADA guidelines.
  • Skilled in nutrient analysis and meal planning, maintain a valid Washington State Food Worker Card, and demonstrate safe food handling and food service practices.
  • Ability to recognize signs and symptoms of eating disorders and disordered eating and collaborate with the medical team to support appropriate care for student-athletes.
  • A strong understanding of medical nutrition therapy and experience developing and implementing therapeutic nutrition plans.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience as a Sports Dietitian supporting NCAA Division I student-athletes.
  • Board Certified Specialist in Sports Dietetics (CSSD) credential, or willingness to obtain certification within one year of hire.
  • Master’s degree in food science, Nutrition, Exercise Physiology, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively as a member of a multidisciplinary team.
  • Ability to work independently while exercising sound judgment and initiative.
  • Strong time management, organizational, and record-keeping skills, with attention to detail.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Effective presentation, education, and nutrition counseling skills.
  • Proven ability to build and maintain positive working relationships with student-athletes, coaches, medical professionals, and other stakeholders.

Working Conditions

  • Maintain a regular work schedule with consistent weekly hours.
  • Occasional evening and weekend work, attendance at athletic events, and team travel may be required to support program needs.
  • Work is conducted in office, clinical, athletic, and food service environments.
  • Frequent interaction with student-athletes, coaches, and multidisciplinary healthcare professionals.
  • Regular use of computers and nutrition assessment equipment is expected.
  • Must be able to move throughout athletic facilities and occasionally lift to 25 pounds.
  • This position requires compliance with Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA), and knowledge of rules and regulations of athletic governing bodies: e.g., National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA), U.S. Anti-Doping Agency (USADA), World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA), regarding banned drugs and restricted substances.
  • Compliance with the rules and regulations of the University, the NCAA, the Conference, the State of Washington and any other governing body is of paramount importance to the University. The overall responsibility of this position is for the successful operation of the program in full compliance with all such rules and regulations. As a condition of employment, the Employee shall be required to participate in rules education programs offered by the Department of Intercollegiate Athletics.

About the Team

Washington Athletics aims to inspire champions in competition and in the classroom. We exist to enrich the lives of students to positively impact our community and world for generations to come. Operating with the four core values of growth mindset, committed service, humility and grit, the Huskies choose to lead by example. All Husky Athletics staff make an IMPACT by committing to creating a purpose driven culture that impacts students and our greater community. We engage in GROWTH through dynamic conversations, embracing creativity, and recognizing that every challenge represents an opportunity to learn. We are a COMMUNITY who strive to create experiences for our stakeholders every single day. At our core is the belief that INCLUSION means creating spaces and places that reflect equity, advocacy and belonging for all.

With over 650 student-athletes participating in UW's 22 sports programs, the department of Intercollegiate Athletics is committed to providing student-athletes with the ability to compete for national and conference championships while working toward a degree from one of the world's leading public research universities.

title: Legal Graduate
description:

Help shape the future of water, the environment and the communities we serve

With a current investment plan worth over £11 billion, we're building for better — for you, for the communities we serve, for our environment. As part of this we are looking for candidates to join Anglian Water's Graduate Programme and tackle some of the biggest environmental and infrastructure challenges facing the region. From climate resilience and major engineering projects to digital innovation and customer experience, you'll develop the skills, experience and support needed to become one of our future leaders or specialists.

Your career path

The water industry is changing rapidly, creating exciting opportunities for the next generation of talent. At Anglian Water, you'll work on real challenges that matter, developing expertise across your chosen profession while contributing to projects that support customers, communities and the environment.

You'll learn from experienced colleagues, take on meaningful responsibility and build the skills, knowledge and confidence to shape your future career, while helping us shape the future of water.

To find out more from our recent graduates please visit our Anglian Water careers page: Graduates - Anglian Water Careers

Professional Development & Memberships

We're committed to helping you build a career, not just gain a job. Through our two-year graduate programme, you'll experience different legal specialisms, work on real business challenges and learn from experienced colleagues across the organisation. You'll have access to a wide range of development opportunities, support towards professional qualifications , helping you grow your expertise and achieve professional accreditation where appropriate.

Your programme

As a Legal Graduate, you'll join our wider Anglian Water graduate cohort while completing a two-year training contract within our in-house Legal team. This is a unique opportunity to gain broad, hands-on experience across a range of legal specialisms while developing a deep understanding of the water industry and the role the legal team plays in supporting the Anglian Water business.

Throughout the programme, you'll work alongside experienced solicitors and legal professionals, building practical experience in areas such as property, commercial contracts, legal compliance, environmental and regulatory law and litigation. You'll contribute to real business projects, provide legal support to colleagues across the organisation, assist with drafting and reviewing legal documents and help manage a varied and interesting workload. Whether supporting major infrastructure projects, advising on commercial agreements, or helping the business navigate regulatory requirements, you'll gain exposure to work that makes a meaningful difference to our customers, communities and the environment.

Alongside your day-to-day work, you'll receive structured support and guidance from qualified solicitors as you work towards qualifying as a solicitor, developing the technical, commercial and professional skills needed for a successful legal career.

What we're looking for

We're looking for an ambitious and motivated individual who is passionate about pursuing a legal career in-house and is excited by the opportunity to work within a business that delivers essential services to millions of customers. You'll have a strong academic background and will either hold a qualifying law degree or have completed a law conversion course, together with the relevant professional qualifications required to begin a training contract/ qualifying work experience.

We're looking for candidates who are interested in developing expertise in commercial contracts, regulation and environmental law. You'll be a strong communicator with excellent attention to detail, able to build relationships with a range of stakeholders and thrive in a collaborative environment. We value individuals who are proactive, collaborative and eager to learn, with a genuine interest in the water sector, sustainability and the role legal teams play in shaping the future of our industry. An interest in how technology and digital tools can enhance the delivery of legal services would also be an advantage.

Benefits

Alongside a competitive salary, you'll receive a comprehensive health and wellbeing package, private healthcare, 26 days' annual leave plus bank holidays and a double-matched pension scheme with up to 21% total contribution. . We recognise some candidates may need to relocate for the opportunity. Where appropriate, Anglian Water may be able to offer support with relocation costs and provide additional financial assistance to successful candidates. Any support offered will be subject to eligibility criteria and business approval. We also offer an excellent family leave package, including enhanced maternity, paternity and shared parental leave, helping you balance your career with the moments that matter most

What we ask:

  • Consistently provide professional, attentive, and genuinely friendly service
